**Honour.** Heb. kabod, also meaning “glory,” and appropriately so rendered here (see Ps. 62:7; 72:19).
**Name.** See on Ps 5:11; 7:17.

3.zh:
當對神說：你的作為何等可畏！因你的大能，仇敵要投降你。

**可畏。**上帝拯救受迫害的人，使迫害者十分害怕（見詩65:5註釋；參啟15:3）。
**投降（kachash）。**“假裝順從”，“奉承”（見詩18:44）。這裡所提到的投降是虛假的，是因恐懼上帝權能的顯示所致。真正內心的降服，是因得到上帝的愛的啟示。
3.en:
**Terrible.** God’s deliverances of the persecuted are terrible to the persecutors (see on Ps. 65:5; cf. Rev. 15:3).
**Submit themselves.** Heb. kachash, “to feign obedience,” “to cringe” (see Ps. 18:44). The submission referred to here is hollow, insincere, feigned; induced only by the show of God’s power. True submission of heart is induced by the revelation of God’s love.

4.zh:
全地要敬拜你，歌頌你，要歌頌你的名。（細拉）

**全地。**見詩22:27註釋。
**名。**見詩5:11；7:17註釋。
**細拉。**見本冊註釋第629頁（《詩篇》序言）。
4.en:
**All the earth.** See on Ps. 22:27.
**Name.** See on Ps. 5:11; 7:17.
**Selah.** See on p. 629.

5.zh:
你們來看神所行的，他向世人所做之事是可畏的。

見詩46:8註釋。
5.en: **Come and see.** See on Ps. 46:8.

6.zh:
他將海變成乾地，眾民步行過河；我們在那裡因他歡喜。

**他將海變成。**指過紅海（見出14:21,22；出15:1-21）。
**步行過河。**指過約旦河（見書3:14-17）。詩人用詩歌的語言，把過約旦河與過紅海的史詩，融合成一幅上帝拯救以色列人的宏偉畫面。
**我們……歡喜。**希伯來人用歌聲表達他們的快樂（見出15:1-21）。
6.en:
**He turned the sea.** A reference to the crossing of the Red Sea (see Ex. 14:21, 22; Ex. 15:1–21).
**Through the flood.** A reference to the crossing of the Jordan (see Joshua 3:14–17). With poetic license the psalmist unites this epic episode with that of the Red Sea crossing in one grand picture of God’s interposition for Israel.
**Did we rejoice.** The joy of the Hebrews was expressed in song (see Ex. 15:1–21).

7.zh:
他用權能治理萬民，直到永遠。他的眼睛鑒察列邦；悖逆的人不可自高。（細拉）

**鑑察。**上帝不斷鑑察各國的行為（見詩11:4註釋；見《先知與君王》第535,536頁）。祂維護自己的子民，不讓他們被仇敵征服。
“上帝站在看不見的廕庇處，
從天上注視著自己的子民”（詹姆士·拉塞爾·洛厄爾《當代危機》）。
**悖逆的人。**指那些不願受上帝限制的人，或藐視上帝的人。這樣的人不可自高自大，因為他們最後得服從上帝的權能。
**細拉。**見本冊註釋第629頁（《詩篇》序言）。
7.en:
**Behold.** God is continually keeping watch to see how the nations behave (see on Ps. 11:4; see PK 535, 536). He is jealous for His people, and will not permit them to be crushed by the enemy. “… Behind the dim unknownStandeth God within the shadow,keeping watch above his own.” AMES USSELL OWELL,“The Present Crisis.”
**The rebellious.** Those who are impatient under God’s restraint, or who defy God. These should not be lifted up with pride, for they must eventually submit to God’s power.
**Selah.** See on p. 629.

8.zh:
萬民哪，你們當稱頌我們的神，使人得聽讚美他的聲音。

**萬民。**指各族人民；原文是複數。
8-12節是第三段歌詞，系本詩的核心，邀請眾人和詩人一起在獻祭時讚美上帝的拯救（13-15節）。
8.en:
**Ye people.** Or, “O ye peoples”; the Hebrew is plural, evidently referring to the nations.
Verses 8–12 constitute the third stanza, the heart of the psalm, in which the people are invited to praise God for deliverance before uniting with the psalmist in the act of sacrifice (vs. 13–15).

9.zh:
他使我們的性命存活，也不叫我們的腳搖動。

**我們的性命。**這裡是習慣性用法，指示“我”（見詩16:10註釋）。上帝的子民雖然遭遇危險，仍會受到保護而存活（見詩3:2；7:2）。
**搖動。**見詩121:3；箴3:23,26。
9.en:
**Our soul.** Here used idiomatically for “us” (see on Ps. 16:10). God’s people had been preserved alive despite the danger suffered (see Ps. 3:2; 7:2).
**To be moved.** See Ps. 121:3; Prov. 3:23, 26.

10.zh:
神啊，你曾試驗我們，熬煉我們，如熬煉銀子一樣。

**曾試驗。**上帝允許苦難臨以色列人，考驗他們對祂的忠誠。
**如熬煉銀子一樣。**亞13:9；彼前1:6,7；參詩12:6。古時煉銀子是一個緩慢的過程。以色列長期遭受苦難。
10.en:
**Hast proved.** God had allowed calamity to come upon Israel as a test of her loyalty to Him.
**As silver is tried.** See Zech. 13:9; 1 Peter 1:6, 7; cf. Ps. 12:6. Anciently the refining of silver was a slow process. Israel had suffered long.

11.zh:
你使我們進入網羅，把重擔放在我們的身上。

**進入網羅。**如同野獸掉到陷阱裡（見何7:12）。
**重擔。**上帝決不允許祂的子民受試煉過於所能承擔的（見林前10:13）。本節可能指在埃及受奴役。
11.en:
**Into the net.** As wild animals are trapped in a snare (see Hosea 7:12).
**Affliction.** God never allows His people to be tried beyond their strength (see 1 Cor. 10:13). This verse may allude to the affliction of bondage in Egypt.

12.zh:
你使人坐車軋我們的頭；我們經過水火，你卻使我們到豐富之地。

**人（'enosh）。**“軟弱的人”（見詩8:4；9:19註釋）。
**坐車軋我們的頭。**一個比喻。可能源於古代東方征服者踐踏被征服者身體的做法。
**經過水火。**指經受許多的危險。
**豐富之地（rewayah）。**“充盈”。其他地方只出現在詩23:5，譯為“滿溢”。指“豐富”，詩人說上帝把以色列人帶到富裕的地方。七十士譯本為anapsuche，可能源於希伯來語rewachah，意思是“安舒”，“緩解”。若是這樣，rewachah就是指以色列人到達應許之地時所得到的安舒。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《服務真詮》第486頁。
12.en:
**Men.** Heb. ’enosh, “man in his frailty” (see on Ps. 8:4; 9:19).
**Ride over our heads.** A figure, perhaps derived from the ancient custom of Oriental conquerors victoriously riding over the bodies of the conquered.
**Through fire and through water.** This phrase, now part and parcel of the English language, is a graphic representation of the many dangers to which men are exposed.
**Wealthy place.** Heb. rewayah, “abundance [of drink].” Rewayah occurs elsewhere only in Ps. 23:5, where it is translated “runneth over” (literally, “an overflowing”). Perhaps the idea of “abundance” is intended, and the psalmist is asserting that God has brought the Israelites into a state of abundance. The LXX has anapsuche, as if from the Heb. rewachah, meaning “relief,” “respite.” If rewachah is the correct reading, then there is perhaps an allusion to the relief experienced when the children of Israel reached the Promised Land.

13.zh:
我要用燔祭進你的殿，向你還我的願，

**燔祭。**見本註釋卷一698-700頁；參賽1:11。
13-15節是本詩第四段。這裡人稱代詞的轉換，在希伯來文學中是常見的。
**願。**指大衛所許的願（見詩22:25註釋；詩50:14）。摩西的律法對不同的願均有規定（見利27:1-8；見利27:9-30；民6:2-21註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋（13–14節）**。《證言》卷四第471頁。
13.en:
**Burnt offerings.** See Vol. I, pp. 698–700; cf. Isa. 1:11.
Verses 13–15 form the fourth stanza. The change of pronouns here illustrated is common in Hebrew literature.
**Vows.** The promises that David had made (see on Ps. 22:25; Ps. 50:14). The Mosaic law had regulations concerning various kinds of vows (see Lev. 27:1–8; see on Lev. 27:9–30; Num. 6:2–21).

14.zh:
就是在急難時我嘴唇所發的、口中所許的。

**嘴唇所發的。**就是在情急之中開口。
**在急難時。**人在患難中特別容易向上帝許願（見士11:30,31；撒上1:11）。他們真應該記住要還所許的願！到了健康和順利的時候，他們經常把這些願忘記。
14.en:
**Have uttered.** The lips opened under the influence of deep emotion.
**In trouble.** Especially in times of trouble men are prone to make promise to God (see Judges 11:30, 31; 1 Sam. 1:11). How careful they should be to keep these promises! How often they forget them, when health and prosperity return.

15.zh:
我要把肥牛作燔祭，將公羊的香祭獻給你，又把公牛和山羊獻上。（細拉）

**把肥牛作燔祭。**即肥畜適合於作祭物。
**公牛和山羊。**二者均可用於摩西所規定的敬拜（關於這些動物如何用作祭物，見本註釋卷一698-703頁）。
**細拉。**見本冊註釋629頁（《詩篇》序言）。
15.en:
**Burnt sacrifices of fatlings.** That is, of fatted animals suitable for sacrifice.
**Bullocks with goats.** Both were required in the worship prescribed by Moses (on the use of these animals in sacrifices, see Vol. I, pp. 698–703).
**Selah.** See on p. 629.

16.zh:
凡敬畏神的人，你們都來聽！我要述說他為我所行的事。

**凡敬畏上帝的人。**大衛願意在眾人面前見證上帝的慈愛，不論他們是不是他的同胞（見撒下15:18註釋）。
16-19節是第五段。大衛呼籲一切忠心敬拜上帝的人，與他一同認識上帝必應允真誠之人的祈禱。
**我要述說。**大衛為自己說話，也可能為百姓說話，因為他是他們的國王和領袖。
**我。**見詩16:10註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷六第227頁；《證言》卷八第182頁。
16.en:
**All ye that fear God.** David was willing to bear witness to God’s goodness before all, whether they were his countrymen or not (see on 2 Sam. 15:18).
Verses 16–19 are the fifth stanza. David calls on all faithful worshipers of God to recognize with him that God answers the prayers of those who are sincere and honest.
**I will declare.** David speaks for himself, and may well have spoken for the people whose king and leader he was.
**My soul.** Used idiomatically for “me” (see on Ps. 16:10).

17.zh:
我曾用口求告他；我的舌頭也稱他為高。

**懷愛倫註釋（17–18節）**。《證言》卷四第533頁。

19.zh:
但神實在聽見了；他側耳聽了我禱告的聲音。

大衛不懷疑自己祈禱的應允；他表達了自己對上帝悅納的信心（見詩116:1,2）。
19.en: **God hath heard.** David did not doubt the answer to his prayer; he expressed his assurance of God’s approval (see Ps. 116:1, 2).

20.zh:
神是應當稱頌的！他並沒有推卻我的禱告，也沒有叫他的慈愛離開我。

我們的上帝是傾聽和回答祈禱的神（見詩65:2；《證言》卷一120,121頁）。
20.en: **Hath not turned away.** Our God is a prayer-hearing and a prayer-answering God (see Ps. 65:2; 1T 120, 121).

7.en: **He that worketh deceit.** Compare Rev. 14:1, 5; see on Prov. 12:17; 20:17.
7.zh:
行詭詐的，必不得住在我家裡；說謊話的，必不得立在我眼前。

參啟14:1,5；見箴12:17；20:17註釋。

0.zh:
序言——本詩歸納了指導領導者進行管理的原則。對於“保護家庭影響”的父母有著特殊的價值（《基督教育之研究》第119頁）。第1-4節涉及領導者的私人生活；第5-8節是他的社會活動。
本詩的作者是大衛（《基督教育之研究》第119頁），可能寫於他執政的初期。這首詩用優美的詞句描寫了大衛王高尚的情操。
關於本詩的題記，見本冊註釋第616,627頁（《詩篇》序言）。
大衛的詩。
0.en:
INTRODUCTION.—Ps. 101 presents a condensed tabulation of the principles that should guide a ruler in his state. It is of special value to parents in “guarding the influences of the home” (CT 119). Verses 1–4 concern the ruler’s private life; vs. 5–8, his public activities.
The psalm was composed by David (CT 119), possibly during the early part of his reign. It is a beautiful expression of the nobility of soul of King David.
On the superscription see pp. 616, 627.

1.zh:
（大衛的詩）我要歌唱慈愛和公平；耶和華啊，我要向你歌頌！

**慈愛（chesed）。**見詩36篇補充註釋）。
1.en: **Mercy.** Heb. chesed (see Additional Note on Ps. 36).

2.zh:
我要用智慧行完全的道。你幾時到我這裡來呢？我要存完全的心行在我家中。

**我要用智慧行。**這是國王的決心，符合國王的心態。
幾時？這是虔誠的人突然發出的問題，希望實現自己的決心。只有上帝完全進入他的生活，這才有可能。大衛強烈希望與上帝交往。
**在我家中。**敬虔是從家裡開始的。
2.en:
**Behave myself wisely.** A kingly resolution, worthy of a kingly soul.
**When?** The question is the sudden outburst of the devout soul, longing for the fulfillment of his resolution, which is possible only when God comes fully into his life. David had a strong desire for fellowship with God.
**Within my house.** Godliness begins at home.

3.zh:
邪僻的事，我都不擺在我眼前；悖逆人所做的事，我甚恨惡，不容沾在我身上。

**邪僻的事。**直譯是“匪類的事”（見申13:13註釋）。
**在我眼前。**大衛決心不看罪惡（見約壹2:16；參林後3:18），以致他的生活不會效法他所眼見的。我們在很大的程度上受喜歡看的東西所影響。“不聽罪惡，不看罪惡，不說罪惡”。關於約伯對個人純潔的重視，見伯31:1,7。
**不容沾。**雖然我可能與罪惡接觸，但馬上就和它分開。“我們無法禁止鳥兒從頭上飛過，但可以不讓它們在我們的頭髮上築巢”。
3.en:
**Wicked thing.** Literally, “thing of Belial” (see on Deut. 13:13).
**Before mine eyes.** David resolves not to look upon evil (see 1 John 2:16; cf. 2 Cor. 3:18), that his life may not imitate what he would see. To a great extent we are what we habitually behold. “Hear no evil; see no evil; speak no evil.” Concerning Job’s high estimate of personal purity see Job 31:1, 7.
**Not cleave.** Though I come into contact with evil, I shall immediately separate myself from it. “We cannot keep the birds from flying over our heads, but we can keep them from building nests in our hair.”

4.zh:
彎曲的心思，我必遠離；一切的惡人（或譯：惡事），我不認識。

**彎曲的（`iqqesh）。**見箴11:20。詩人在這裡從個人的決心，轉到在社會活動中作為領導人的決心。
4.en: **Froward.** Heb. ‘iqqesh, “crooked,” “perverted” (see Prov. 11:20). At this point the psalmist turns from resolutions of a private nature to resolutions that concern his public life as ruler.

5.zh:
在暗中讒謗他鄰居的，我必將他滅絕；眼目高傲、心裡驕縱的，我必不容他。

**在暗中。**私下秘密地。
**我必不容他。**作為國王，大衛決心在他的宮廷中不容忍那些自以為了不起的人。
5.en:
**Privily.** Privately, secretly.
**Not I suffer.** As king, David resolves not to tolerate in his official household those who are characterized as above.

6.zh:
我眼要看國中的誠實人，叫他們與我同住；行為完全的，他要伺候我。

**我眼。**大衛決心注意讓忠實的人成為他宮廷的重要成員。
**行為完全的。**見第2節。大衛希望自己的官員像他一樣。選擇的標準是內在的價值，而不是高貴的出身或天賦。大衛怎樣要求自己，也照樣要求別人。
6.en:
**Mine eyes.** David resolves to keep on the watch for faithful men who will make worthy members of his court.
**In a perfect way.** See v. 2. David desires his official associates to be like him. They will be chosen for inherent worth, not for high birth or talent. What David requires in himself, he requires in others.

8.zh:
我每日早晨要滅絕國中所有的惡人，好把一切作孽的從耶和華的城裡剪除。

**我每日早晨要滅絕。**罪惡不允許延續。只要一出現，就要消滅。
**耶和華的城。**就是大衛的首都耶路撒冷。如果一個國家的首都在道德清潔了，全國就會效法她的榜樣。
如果真的實行了本詩的決心，就會使國王得到大衛在撒下23:3,4所表達的讚美。
8.en:
**Early destroy.** No evil will be allowed to persist. At its first appearance, it will be destroyed.
**City of the Lord.** Jerusalem, David’s capital. If a nation’s capital is morally clean, the example thus set will probably be followed in the nation.
Surely the high resolutions of this psalm, if kept, would make a king worthy of David’s praise as expressed in 2 Sam. 23:3, 4.

3.en:
**In the morning.** The psalmist lifts his voice in prayer regularly, morning by morning, but especially at this time, when he is beset by his enemies (see Ps. 55:17; 59:16; 88:13). There is no better habit than the habit of morning prayer, when alone with God the soul prepares to discharge the duties and meet the problems of the unknown day. “A moment in the morning—a moment, if no more— Is better than an hour when the trying day is o’er.”
It is well to cultivate the habit of offering the first fruits of our consciousness as a morning offering to God.
**Direct.** Heb. ‘arak, literally, “set in order.” The word is used for the arranging of the wood upon the altar in Gen. 22:9 and of the arranging of the shewbread on the table (Ex. 40:23). The psalmist’s prayer is a sort of well-arranged morning sacrifice; it is not performed thoughtlessly.
**Look up.** The psalmist looks upward for a token of God’s favor, for the answer to his prayer. Compare the Saviour’s injunction to “watch and pray” (Matt. 26:41).
3.zh:
耶和華啊，早晨你必聽我的聲音；早晨我必向你陳明我的心意，並要警醒！

**早晨。**詩人每日清晨均高聲祈禱，特別是在這被仇敵圍困的時候（見詩55:17；59:16；88:13）。沒有什麼習慣比清晨的祈禱更好。一個人單獨與上帝相處，就能準備好卸下心靈的擔子，迎接新的一天未知的挑戰。
“清晨的一刻，勝過艱難的一天過去後的一個小時。
最好養成習慣，把我們思維的第一批果實作為晨祭獻給上帝。
**陳明（`arak）。**直譯是“整理”，在創22:9中指整理祭壇上的木材，在出40:23中指整理桌子上的陳設餅。詩人的祈禱是思路清晰的晨祭，不是隨口而說的。
儆醒。詩人警醒仰望上帝悅納的標誌，作為對他祈禱的回答。請對照救主的勸勉：“總要儆醒禱告”（太26:41）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《今日的生活》第15頁；《證言》卷一第397頁。

0.zh:
序言——《詩篇》第五篇是一首晨禱，和第四篇體現同樣的精神。兩首詩的寫作背景可能也是一樣的。經過一夜的安睡，詩人在進入上帝的居所以前，發出了這篇禱詞（第7節）。他相信上帝不會讓惡人得勢。祂一定會讓信靠祂的人得到滿足的喜樂。詩歌一開始就祈禱上帝，然後表達對上帝堅定不移的信心，求上帝在人生的困惑中引導，最後勸大家都信靠上帝。
關於題記，見本書第616,627,629頁。
大衛的詩，交與伶長。用吹的樂器 。
0.en:
INTRODUCTION.—Ps. 5 is a morning prayer, written in the same spirit as Ps. 4, an evening prayer. The circumstances under which the two psalms were written were probably similar. After a night of calm sleep the psalmist utters this prayer before entering God’s house (v. 7). He is confident that God, who will not allow wicked men to prevail, will surely cause those who trust in Him to have fullness of joy. The psalm begins with prayer to God, then expresses unwavering confidence in God, pleads for God’s guidance in life’s perplexities, and finally, exhorts all to put their trust in God.
On the superscription see pp. 616, 627, 629.

1.zh:
（大衛的詩，交與伶長。用吹的樂器。）耶和華啊，求你留心聽我的言語，顧念我的心思！

詩人求上帝不僅傾聽自己的祈禱，而且關注祈禱的內涵和心中尚未表達出來的願望。“心思”（hagig）一詞只出現在這裡和詩39:3，譯為“默想”。似乎指“呻吟”或“嘆息”。詩人所說的hagig可能相當於保羅的stenagmoi（“嘆息”，羅8:26）。“禱告是心靈表達或未表達出來的真誠願望”。
1.en: **Meditation.** The psalmist prays that God may regard not only his words but their intent, the secret and unexpressed desires of his heart. The word for “meditation,” hagig, is found only here and in Ps. 39:3, where it is translated “musing.” It seems to indicate “groaning,” or “a sigh.” By hagig the psalmist may have referred to what Paul called stenagmoi, “groanings” (Rom. 8:26). “Prayer is the soul’s sincere desire, unuttered or expressed.”

2.zh:
我的王我的神啊，求你垂聽我呼求的聲音！因為我向你祈禱。

值得注意的是，國王大衛在這裡承認自己從屬於他的上帝萬王之王。“上帝”的原文是'Elohim（見本註釋卷一170,171頁）。詩人承認上帝的全知全能。烏加列文獻有許多稱國王為'el的例子。
2.en: **My King, and my God.** It is noteworthy that David, a king, should acknowledge his subjection to the King of kings, his God. “God” is here a translation of ’Elohim (see Vol. 1, pp. 170, 171). The psalmist recognizes the omnipotence of God. Ugaritic literature shows many examples of the designation “king” for ’el.

4.zh:
因為你不是喜悅惡事的神，惡人不能與你同居。

**喜悅惡事。**上帝非常聖潔，根本不會參與惡人的計謀。如果祂悅納他們，就等於讓他們來到祂的住所。
**居（gur）。**“惡人”在KJV版裡為“惡”，把它擬人化，似乎能住在一個地方。詩15章描寫了與上帝同居的人。
**懷愛倫註釋（4–5節）**。《證言》卷二第351頁。
4.en:
**Pleasure in wickedness.** God is too holy and pure to have any part in furthering the designs of wicked men. If He showed favor to them, it would be like His admitting them to His dwelling.
**Dwell.** Heb. gur, literally, “sojourn.” Evil is personified as if capable of dwelling in a habitation. Those who may dwell with God are described in Ps. 15.

5.zh:
狂傲人不能站在你眼前；凡作孽的，都是你所恨惡的。

**狂傲人（holelim）。**指自吹自擂，傲慢無禮的罪人。
**不能站。**上帝不贊成狂傲人的理由（見詩5:5）。祂憎恨一切形式的罪孽。在《詩篇》裡，“作孽的”一直用來指罪惡原則的具體表現。
5.en:
**The foolish.** Heb. holelim, “boasters,” the proud, the insolent, sinners.
**Shall not stand.** God will not approve of the cause of the boasters (see Ps. 1:5). He hates all forms of iniquity; in the psalms, “workers of iniquity” are continually referred to as the concrete embodiment of the principle of evil.

6.zh:
說謊言的，你必滅絕；好流人血弄詭詐的，都為耶和華所憎惡。

**謊言。**見詩4:2註釋。在英文KJV版裡，該詞只用在這兩節經文裡。
**憎惡。**上帝憎恨罪惡，不會放任罪人心中的罪孽。上帝憎恨的人是“流人血弄詭詐的”。這裡用“血”的複數形式表示謀殺（見創4:10）。大衛的仇敵以欺詐和謀殺而聞名。
6.en:
**Leasing.** See on Ps. 4:2. This Old English word for “lie” is found only in these two verses in the KJV.
**Abhor.** God holds sin in such abomination that He cannot overlook its presence in the sinner. Those whom God abhors are literally “men of bloods and deceit.” The plural form “bloods” refers to bloodguiltiness or murder (see Gen. 4:10). David’s enemies are distinguished for fraud and murder.

7.zh:
至於我，我必憑你豐盛的慈愛進入你的居所；我必存敬畏你的心向你的聖殿下拜。

**至於我。**這是強烈的對比。詩人與惡人不同。他確信自己能進入上帝的居所。這是他的權利。
**你豐盛的慈愛。**上帝的兒女在上帝的居所受到歡迎。惡人在那裡則不受歡迎。他確信上帝會接待，就像一個孩子相信天上的父那樣。
**敬畏。**暗示敬拜時極其敬重。
**下拜。**敬拜者還不能進入聖所。他們在近處或遠處朝聖所跪拜，視聖所為上帝的居所。
**聖殿（hekal）。**在賽39:7；但1:4為王宮；或指上帝的殿。Hekal曾用來表上帝的殿（撒上1:9；3:3；撒下22:7）和所羅門的殿（王下18:16；23:4等）建造以前的會幕。所以hekal出現在本節，並不像一些學者所主張的，證明本詩創作於大衛以後。注意在第27篇裡聖所分別用“殿”（hekal，詩27:4）和“帳幕”（'ohel，詩27:6）來表示。
更值得注意的是，本節兩個並行的詞“居所”（bayith）和“聖殿”（hekal）經常出現在烏加列文獻裡（見第618頁），作為神居所的同義詞。下面是一個典型的例子：“然後亞納進入她的居所（bt），女神進入她的殿（hkl）”。
在現代猶太教的儀式裡，詩5:7被選為敬拜者進入會堂時的頌詞。
7.en:
**But as for me.** A strong contrast. Unlike the wicked, the psalmist feels calm assurance upon entering God’s house. It is his right.
**Multitude of thy mercy.** The child of God is as welcome in God’s house as the wicked man’s presence would be unwelcome there. He is sure of God’s hospitality. This is truly a childlike trust in a heavenly Parent.
**Fear.** This expression implies profound reverence in worship.
**Worship.** Literally, “prostrate myself.” The worshipers were not permitted to enter the sanctuary, but, near or far, prostrated themselves toward it as the dwelling place of God.
**Temple.** Heb. hekal, a palace as in Isa. 39:7; Dan. 1:4; or a temple where God may dwell. Hekal is used to designate the tabernacle that preceded the building of the Temple (1 Sam. 1:9; 3:3; 2 Sam. 22:7), as well as the Solomonic Temple (2 Kings 18:16; 23:4; etc.). The use of the word hekal in this verse, therefore, is no argument, as certain critics maintain, that the psalm is of post-Davidic origin. Note also that in 27 the sanctuary is designated as both “temple” (hekal) (v. 4) and “tabernacle” (’ohel) (v. 6).
It is further noteworthy that the parallel expressions “house” (bayith) and temple (hekal) appearing in this verse, occur frequently in Ugaritic literature (see p. 618) as synonyms for the dwelling place of a deity. The following is a typical example: “Then went Anath to her house (bt), the goddess proceeded to her temple (hkl).
In the modern Jewish ritual, Ps. 5:7 has been selected for recital as the worshiper enters the synagogue.

9.zh:
因為，他們的口中沒有誠實；他們的心裡滿有邪惡；他們的喉嚨是敞開的墳墓；他們用舌頭諂媚人。

**誠實（nekonah）。**源於kun，意為“確立”，“可靠”。仇敵完全是靠不住的。他們虛偽又陰險。押沙龍就是憑藉謊言前往希伯倫的（見撒下15:7-10）。
**邪惡。**直譯為“毀滅”。他們的喉嚨象張開的墳墓，隨時準備吞沒他人的幸福。保羅引用本節刻畫了人類普遍的罪惡（羅3:13）。詩人還提到人的另一個器官——舌頭，說它一樣的可惡（見雅3:5-9）。這正是押沙龍和他的叛逆同謀的寫照（見撒下15:1-6）。
9.en:
**Faithfulness.** Heb. nekonah, from kun, meaning “to be firmly established,” “to be trustworthy.” The enemies are wholly undependable; they are utterly false and treacherous. Absalom had gone to Hebron on a false pretense (see 2 Sam. 15:7–10).
**Wickedness.** Literally, “destruction.” Moreover, their throats, like open graves, are ready to devour the happiness of others. Paul employs this passage to characterize man’s universal depravity (Rom. 3:13). Further, the psalmist refers to another member of the body, the tongue, as being equally depraved (see James 3:5–9). This description appears pertinent to the treachery of Absalom and his fellow rebels (see 2 Sam. 15:1–6).

10.zh:
神啊，求你定他們的罪！願他們因自己的計謀跌倒；願你在他們許多的過犯中把他們逐出，因為他們背叛了你。

定……罪（'asham）。詩人希望上帝定他仇敵的罪。他們確實是罪人。他祈求讓他們“因自己的計謀而跌倒”，也就是讓他們搬起石頭砸自己的腳（見詩7:15,16；箴26:27；箴28:10）。《舊約》經常出現這樣的觀念。罪惡最終會自取滅亡。
10.en: **Destroy.** Heb. ’asham, “to be guilty.” In the form employed here, the word ’asham means “to hold guilty.” The psalmist desires that God would treat his enemies as guilty, which they undoubtedly are. He asks that they may “fall by their own counsels,” that is, that their own plans may be the means of their destruction (see Ps. 7:15, 16; Prov. 26:27; Prov. 28:10). This idea is frequent in the OT. Sin eventually consumes itself.

11.zh:
凡投靠你的，願他們喜樂，時常歡呼，因為你護庇他們；又願那愛你名的人都靠你歡欣。

**喜樂。**見詩2:12註釋。相信上帝的人始終有喜樂的理由。他們用歡呼表達自己的快樂。他們喜樂是因為上帝保護他們。詩人把自己的喜樂，擴大到所有相信上帝的人。
**名。**常常是“人”的同義詞。
**靠你歡欣。**虔誠的基督徒將因上帝把祂自己顯現出來而歡欣。他在上帝裡面，通過默想上帝的品性和祂慈愛的證據，通過與祂交往，憑著愛心為祂服務而得到自己的喜樂。
11.en:
**Rejoice.** See on Ps. 2:12. Those that trust in God ever have an occasion for joy. Their joy finds expression in shouting. They rejoice because God defends them. The psalmist extends his own joy to include all who trust in God.
**Name.** Often synonymous with “person.”
**Be joyful in thee.** The devout Christian will rejoice in all that God has revealed of Himself. He finds his joy in God, in contemplating His attributes and the evidences of His love, in communion with Him, and in loving service for Him.

12.zh:
因為你必賜福與義人；耶和華啊，你必用恩惠如同盾牌四面護衛他。

**四面護衛他。**或“給他加冕”。
**盾牌（sinnah）。**是護衛全身的大盾牌，不是詩3:3的magen（小盾牌）。正如在戰鬥時盾牌保護著戰士，上帝也給義人提供充分的保護。在詩歌的結束，詩人宣稱自己完全信靠上帝的保護。有人把“恩惠”解釋為“悅納”。
詩人用這樣的晨禱，來迎接白天仇敵的進攻。司布真說得好：“讓我們把每天的清晨和生命中的清晨獻給上帝。禱告是白天的鑰匙和夜間的鎖。是晨星，也是昏星（注：傍晚出現的）。如果我們有良好的開端，就能在一天中更加體驗上帝的同在，晚上睡覺時也更加自信和安寧。
12.en:
**Compass him.** Or, “crown him.”
**Shield.** Heb. sinnah, a large shield that is said to have covered the whole body (not the magen of Ps. 3:3). As the shield is thrown around the soldier in the day of battle, so God gives complete protection to the righteous. The psalm closes with the psalmist’s avowal of perfect trust in God’s complete protection. The Bay Psalm Book paraphrases the verse: “And wilt him crowne as with a shield, with gracious acceptation.”
With a morning prayer such as this, the psalmist is ready to meet the onslaughts of the day’s foes. Spurgeon has appropriately remarked, “Let us give to God the mornings of our days and the mornings of our lives. Prayer should be the key of the day and the lock of the night. Devotion should be both the morning star and the evening star. If we start the day right, we shall be more aware of God’s presence through its hours, and surer of coming to our beds at night with quietness and confidence in our hearts.”

15.en:
**Their request.** See Num. 11:31.
**Leanness.** Heb. razon, “emaciation” (see Num. 11:33, 34).
15.zh:
他將他們所求的賜給他們，卻使他們的心靈軟弱。

**他們所求的。**見民11:31。
**軟弱（razon）。**見民11:33,34。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《服務真詮》第312頁；《證言》卷三第171頁。

14.en:
**Lusted exceedingly.** See Num 11:4–6.
**Tempted.** Heb. nasah, “tested,” “tried.”
14.zh:
反倒在曠野大起慾心，在荒地試探神。

**大起欲心。**見民11:4-6。
**試探（nasah）。**“考驗”，“試煉”。

0.zh: 序言——本詩一般被認為是詩105篇的續篇。它們都是以色列民族的讚歌，回顧以色列早期的歷史，顯示上帝的守約。但本詩的顯著特點是展示以色列如何慣於悖逆，自食其犯罪的可怕後果。本詩縱覽以色列從埃及到曠野流浪，以及在迦南士師時期的歷史。本詩以長段不一的段落交替描寫了以色列的軟弱愚昧和上帝通過拯救和懲罰所顯示的大能。這首詩開頭和結尾都是讚美和祈禱，被稱為第一首哈利路亞詩歌（另見詩111-113；117；135；146-150篇）。本詩和詩105篇一樣，應當根據《證言》卷八107-116頁，《給傳道人的證言》98頁和《懷氏傳略》第196頁的亮光進行研究。
0.en: INTRODUCTION.—Ps. 106 is generally considered a sequel to Ps. 105. It is a national hymn of Israel, and like Ps. 105 reviews Israel’s early history to show God’s faithfulness to the covenant. However, it has this striking difference: the psalmist shows how chronic was Israel’s disloyalty and what awful consequences she suffered as a result of her sins. The psalm covers the history of Israel from Egypt through the wilderness wandering, and her history in the Holy Land through the period of the judges. This hymn exhibits a swing of thought between the weakness and folly of Israel and the strength of God as shown both in deliverance and in punishment, in alternating unequal stanzas. It begins and closes with praise and prayer. The psalm is the first of the so-called hallelujah psalms (see also Ps. 111–113; 117; 135; 146–150). Like Ps. 105, Ps. 106 should be studied in the light of 8T 107–116; TM 98; and LS 196.

1.zh:
你們要讚美耶和華！要稱謝耶和華，因他本為善；他的慈愛永遠長存！

**慈愛（chesed）。**“上帝的愛”（見詩36篇補充註釋）。上帝不變的愛使以色列沒有被完全拋棄。“他的慈愛永遠長存”是詩136篇一再重複的副歌。本節出現在大衛為慶祝約櫃在耶路撒冷安家而寫的詩中（見代上16:34）。在基督的時代，本節是住棚節聖殿慶典詩歌的一部分（見《歷代願望》第448頁）。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–48節）**。《證言》卷八第109-112頁；《給傳道人的證言》第98頁。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第448頁。
1.en: **Mercy.** Heb. chesed, “divine love” (see Additional Note on Ps. 36). God’s steadfast love had prevented Israel from being utterly rejected. The complete clause “his mercy endureth for ever” is the recurrent refrain of Ps. 136. The words of Ps. 106:1 appear in David’s psalm for the ceremony of enshrining the ark in Jerusalem (1 Chron. 16:34). In the time of Christ this verse was sung as a part of the Temple festivities at the Feast of Tabernacles (see DA 448).

2.zh:
誰能傳說耶和華的大能？誰能表明他一切的美德？

**美德（tehillah）。**tehillim是希伯來語對《詩篇》的稱呼（見本冊註釋第615頁）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《服務真詮》第101頁。
2.en: **Praise.** Heb. tehillah. Tehillim is the Hebrew title of the Psalter (see p. 615).

3.zh:
凡遵守公平；常行公義的，這人便為有福！

見詩1:1註釋。
3.en: **Blessed.** See on Ps. 1:1.

4.zh:
耶和華啊，你用恩惠待你的百姓；求你也用這恩惠記念我，開你的救恩眷顧我，

從1-3節全體的祈禱轉向到個人的祈求。
4.en: **Remember me.** The general prayer of vs. 1–3 now turns to personal petition.

5.zh:
使我見你選民的福，樂你國民的樂，與你的產業一同誇耀。

**國民。**同義詞有“蒙揀選的”，“民族”和“後裔”。
5.en: **Nation.** The words “chosen,” “nation,” and “inheritance” are synonymous.

6.zh:
我們與我們的祖宗一同犯罪；我們作了孽，行了惡。

6-39節回顧了以色列從埃及到迦南歷史中的悖逆，例舉了這個民族所承認的八條罪狀。
6.en: **We have sinned.** Verses 6–39 review Israel’s disloyalties from Egypt to Canaan, citing eight transgressions for which the nation makes confession.

7.zh:
我們的祖宗在埃及不明白你的奇事，不記念你豐盛的慈愛，反倒在紅海行了悖逆。

**不明白。**先輩們沒有認真思考上帝對埃及的懲罰，以致忘記了上帝的慈愛（見申32:28,29）。和以色列人一樣，我們都容易心安理得地接受上帝的福氣，卻沒有讓這些慈愛的證據長期留在我們心中。
**行了悖逆。**八條罪狀中的第一條（見第6節註釋；見出14:11,12）。
7.en:
**Understood not.** Their lack of careful consideration of God’s judgments upon Egypt caused the fathers to forget His mercies (see Deut. 32:28, 29). Like the Israelites, we are prone to accept God’s blessings as mere matter of fact, not allowing these tokens of beneficence to make any lasting impression on us.
**Provoked him.** The first of the eight acts of transgression (see on v. 6; see Ex. 14:11, 12).

8.zh:
然而，他因自己的名拯救他們，為要彰顯他的大能，

見詩31:3註釋。
8.en: **For his name’s sake.** See on Ps. 31:3.

9.zh:
並且斥責紅海，海便乾了；他帶領他們經過深處，如同經過曠野。

見出14:21,22；參詩104:7。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先知與君王》第16頁。
9.en: **Rebuked.** See Ex. 14:21, 22; cf. Ps. 104:7.

11.zh:
水淹沒他們的敵人，沒有一個存留。

見出14:27-30；15:5。
11.en: **Covered their enemies.** See Ex. 14:27–30; 15:5.

12.zh:
那時，他們才信了他的話，歌唱讚美他。

見出14:31。摩西的歌出色地描寫了紅海的拯救（出15:1-21）。但以色列人很快就忘記了上帝的慈愛。
12.en: **Believed they.** See Ex. 14:31. The song of Moses (Ex. 15:1–21) is a magnificent poetic expansion of the deliverance at the Red Sea. But the Israelites soon forgot God’s goodness.

13.zh:
等不多時，他們就忘了他的作為，不仰望他的指教，

**等不多時，他們就忘了。**13-33節承認了以色列在曠野的罪：對肉食的貪慾，對摩西和亞倫的背叛，造金牛犢，探子的事件，在巴力毗珥的罪，以及在米利巴發怨言。
本詩所回顧一系列的罪行之間並沒有採用明顯的過渡手段。這種情節的連續描寫在修辭上屬於連接詞省略。這是本詩的特徵（見第6,7,13,24等）。其效果是不停頓地回顧以色列民族在歷史上的錯誤，似乎百姓急於要作充分的認罪。
**不仰望。**他們跑到上帝計劃的前面。每當我們不等待上帝顯示祂對我們的計劃時，我們就會陷入麻煩。
13.en:
**Soon forgat.** Verses 13–33 are the confession of Israel’s sins in the wilderness: their lust for flesh, their revolt against Moses and Aaron, the sin of the golden calf, the incident of the spies, the sin at Baal-peor, and the murmuring at Meribah.
The successive sins recalled in the psalm follow without formal transition. This tendency to pass immediately from episode to episode without expressed connection is an example of the rhetorical figure called asyndeton. It is a characteristic of Ps. 106 (see vs. 6, 7, 13, 24, etc.). The effect of the asyndeton is to leave the impression of an almost breathless recollection upon recollection of the historic mistakes of the nation of Israel, as if the people were hastening to make a full confession.
**Waited not.** They ran ahead of God’s plan for them. Whenever we fail to wait for God to reveal His plan for us, we fall into trouble.

16.zh:
他們又在營中嫉妒摩西和耶和華的聖者亞倫。

**嫉妒摩西。**在曠野的第二條罪：背叛摩西和亞倫（見民16；17章）。
**聖者。**直譯是，“聖潔者”。悖逆的人說全會眾個個都是聖潔的（見民16:3）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》第320頁。
16.en:
**Envied Moses.** The second sin in the wilderness: the revolt against Moses and Aaron (see Num. 16; 17).
**Saint.** Literally, “the holy one.” The disaffected party protested that all the congregation were holy (see Num. 16:3).

17.zh:
地裂開，吞下大坍，掩蓋亞比蘭一黨的人。

見申11:6。聖經說“可拉的眾子沒有死亡”（見民26:11）。
17.en: **Dathan.** See Deut. 11:6. It is recorded that “the children of Korah died not” (see Num. 26:11).

18.zh:
有火在他們的黨中發起；有火焰燒毀了惡人。

見民16:2,26,35。
18.en: **The wicked.** See Num. 16:2, 26, 35.

19.zh:
他們在何烈山造了牛犢，叩拜鑄成的像。

19-23節描寫在曠野的第三條罪：拜金牛犢（見出32；參申9:8-12）。
**懷愛倫註釋（19–20節）**。《先祖與先知》第317頁。
19.en: **Horeb.** Verses 19–23 describe the third sin in the wilderness: the sin of the golden calf (see Ex. 32; cf. Deut. 9:8–12).

20.zh:
如此將他們榮耀的主換為吃草之牛的像，

即上帝的榮耀（耶2:11；羅1:23）。上帝的榮耀與吃草的牲口之間形成鮮明的對照。人類墮落到何等的深淵！
20.en: **Their glory.** That is, the glory of God (Jer. 2:11; Rom. 1:23). The contrast between God’s glory and a brute eating grass is a startling one. To what depths does carnal man descend!

21.zh:
忘了神─他們的救主；他曾在埃及行大事，

**忘了。**見13節註釋；見申6:12。第21,22節概括了出埃及期間在埃及發生的事。
**救主。**見賽43:3。
21.en:
**They forgat.** See on v. 13; see Deut. 6:12. Verses 21, 22 summarize the events in Egypt at the time of the Exodus.
**Saviour.** See Isa. 43:3.

22.zh:
在含地行奇事，在紅海行可畏的事。

見詩105:23註釋。
22.en: **Ham.** See on Ps. 105:23.

23.zh:
所以，他說要滅絕他們；若非有他所揀選的摩西站在當中（原文是破口），使他的忿怒轉消，恐怕他就滅絕他們。

見出32:10-14,32-34；參結22:30。
23.en: **In the breach.** See Ex. 32:10–14, 32–34, cf. Eze. 22:30.

24.zh:
他們又藐視那美地，不信他的話，

**那美地。**見申8:7；耶3:19；結20:6。24-27節描寫在曠野的第四條罪：探子回來以後發生的叛逆（見民13；14）。
**不信。**見申1:22；參來3:18。
24.en:
**The pleasant land.** See Deut. 8:7; Jer. 3:19; Eze. 20:6. Ps. 106:24–27 describes the fourth sin in the wilderness: the rebellion that occurred upon the return of the spies (see Num. 13; 14).
**Believed not.** See Deut. 1:22; cf. Heb. 3:18.

26.zh:
所以，他對他們起誓：必叫他們倒在曠野，

這是用人的語言辭描寫上帝，說祂舉手發誓（見出6:8，“起誓”直譯為“舉起我的手”）。
26.en: **Lifted up his hand.** God is pictured, in the language of men, as a man lifting his hand in taking an oath (see Ex. 6:8, where “did swear” is literally “lifted up my hand”).

27.zh:
叫他們的後裔倒在列國之中，分散在各地。

參結20:23。

28.zh:
他們又與巴力‧毘珥連合，且吃了祭死神（或譯：人）的物。

**他們又與……連合。**28-31節描寫在曠野的第五條罪：在縱慾的狂宴中參與巴力毗珥崇拜（見民25章）。
**巴力毗珥。**見民23:28；25:18；民31:16；書22:17。關於巴力崇拜，見士2:11註釋，另見本註釋卷二第40頁。
**祭死神（或作人）的物。**見本冊註釋第684頁；林前10:20；參林前8:4-6。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《善惡之爭》第556頁；《先祖與先知》第684頁。
28.en:
**Joined themselves.** Verses 28–31 describe the fifth sin in the wilderness: the licentious carousing in connection with the worship of Baal-peor (see Num. 25).
**Baal-peor.** See Num. 23:28; 25:18; Num 31:16; Joshua 22:17. On Baal worship see on Judges 2:11; see also Vol. II, p. 40.
**Sacrifices of the dead.** See PP 684; 1 Cor. 10:20; cf. 1 Cor. 8:4–6.

29.zh:
他們這樣行，惹耶和華發怒，便有瘟疫流行在他們中間。

見民25:8,9,18；《先祖與先知》第455頁。

30.zh:
那時，非尼哈站起，刑罰惡人，瘟疫這才止息。

見民25:7,8。

31.zh:
那就算為他的義，世世代代，直到永遠。

參創15:6。因為這個信心的舉動，上帝應許讓他的家族永遠擔任祭司（見民25:10-13）。
31.en: **For righteousness.** Compare Gen. 15:6. As a result of this act of faith, the Lord promised the continuance of the priesthood (see Num. 25:10–13).

32.zh:
他們在米利巴水又叫耶和華發怒，甚至摩西也受了虧損，

**米利巴水。**曠野中的第六條罪：在米利巴水處悖逆摩西和亞倫（見民20:2-13）。
**摩西也受了虧損。**見民20:10-12；參申1:37；3:26。
32.en:
**Waters of strife.** The sixth sin in the wilderness: the rebellion against Moses and Aaron at the waters of Meribah (see Num. 20:2–13).
**Ill with Moses.** See Num. 20:10–12; cf. Deut. 1:37; 3:26.

33.zh:
是因他們惹動他的靈，摩西（原文是他）用嘴說了急躁的話。

**說了急躁的話（bata'）。**“說話輕率”，“說話不假思索”（見本註釋卷一953,954頁）。所承認在曠野的六條罪到此結束。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》第420頁；《救贖的故事》第165頁。
33.en: **Spake unadvisedly.** Heb. bata’, “to speak rashly,” “to speak thoughtlessly” (see Vol. I, pp. 953, 954). The confession of the six sins in the wilderness is completed.

34.zh:
他們不照耶和華所吩咐的滅絕外邦人，

以色列人沒有遵照上帝的命令，消滅拜偶像的民族（見出23:32,33；申7:2；書23:12,13；士1:21,27等）。順從這條命令是很重要的，因為導致以色列毀滅的就是和外邦人同流合汙。
第34-39節討論進入迦南以後繼續犯罪。
**懷愛倫註釋（34–36節）**。《教育論》第45頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（34–38節）**。《先祖與先知》第544頁。
34.en:
**Did not destroy.** The Israelites did not destroy the idolatrous nations, as God had commanded (see Ex. 23:32, 33; Deut. 7:2; Joshua 23:12, 13; Judges 1:21, 27; etc.). Obedience to this command was of the utmost importance, for it was contact with the heathen that dragged Israel to her ruin.
Verses 34–39 discuss the continued sinning after entering Canaan.

35.zh:
反與他們混雜相合，學習他們的行為，

36-39節提供了細節。以色列人的悖逆到了何等深的地步！這對於屬靈的以色列人是一個教訓。
35.en: **Learned their works.** The details are given in vs. 36–39. To what levels did disobedience lower the Israelites! Here is a lesson for spiritual Israel.

36.zh:
事奉他們的偶像，這就成了自己的網羅，

見出23:33；34:12；申7:16。

37.zh:
把自己的兒女祭祀鬼魔，

**祭祀。**摩洛的崇拜涉及獻人祭（見利18:21註釋；見王上11:7）。這是最可憎的異教儀式之一。
**鬼魔。**見林前10:20；《先祖與先知》第685,686頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（37–38節）**。《先祖與先知》第686頁。
37.en:
**Sacrificed.** The worship of Molech involved human sacrifice (see on Lev. 18:21; 1 Kings 11:7). This was one of the most abominable of the rites of the heathen.
**Devils.** See 1 Cor. 10:20; PP 685, 686.

39.zh:
這樣，他們被自己所做的汙穢了，在行為上犯了邪淫。

他們犯了屬靈的姦淫，違背了與上帝所立的約。以色列與上帝的關係是用婚姻來比喻的（見耶3:14；結16）。
39.en: **Went a whoring.** They committed spiritual adultery, breaking their covenant relationship with God. The relation between Israel and God is represented by the figure of marriage (see Jer. 3:14; Eze. 16).

40.zh:
所以，耶和華的怒氣向他的百姓發作，憎惡他的產業，

**怒氣。**見詩78:59。這個觀念就像一條黑線，貫穿在整個士師時期。
第40-43描寫懲罰為悖逆的結果。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》第544頁。
40.en:
**Wrath.** See Ps. 78:59. The idea runs like a dark thread throughout the story of the judges.
Verses 40–43 describe the punishment as a result of disobedience.

43.zh:
他屢次搭救他們，他們卻設謀背逆，因自己的罪孽降為卑下。

見士2:16。

45.zh:
為他們記念他的約，照他豐盛的慈愛後悔。

**記念。**並不是說上帝忘記了祂的約。希伯來語的“記念”不但指記住某事或想起忘記的事，而往往是指因想起某事而採取的行動。上帝現在要實行聖約的條款。
**慈愛（chasadim）。**見詩36篇補充註釋。
45.en:
**Remembered.** This does not imply that God had forgotten His covenant. The Hebrew word for “remember” frequently signifies more than a retention in the conscious memory, or the sudden recalling of a fact that may have slipped from the mind. The word often denotes the action that results because a circumstance is “remembered.” God will now act with reference to the covenant stipulations.
**Mercies.** Heb. chasadim (see Additional Note on Ps. 36).

46.zh:
他也使他們在凡擄掠他們的人面前蒙憐恤。

見王上8:50（參尼1:11；但1:9）。
46.en: **To be pitied.** See 1 Kings 8:50 (cf. Neh. 1:11; Dan. 1:9).

48.zh:
耶和華─以色列的神是應當稱頌的，從亙古直到永遠。願眾民都說：阿們！你們要讚美耶和華！

**阿們。**《詩篇》第四部分以感恩頌結束（見詩41:13；72:18,19；89:52；另見本冊註釋第626頁和詩105篇序言）。
**你們要讚美耶和華。**見詩104:35註釋。儘管詩人長篇敘述了以色列人的頑梗，悖逆和犯罪，在結束時仍高聲感謝上帝的慈愛。
48.en:
**Amen.** The doxology marks the close of Book Four (see Ps. 41:13; 72:18, 19; 89:52; see also p. 626 and Introduction to Ps. 105).
**Praise ye the Lord.** See on Ps. 104:35. Despite the long recital of Israel’s stubbornness, rebellion, and sin, the psalmist closes on a high note of thanksgiving for God’s mercy.

8.en:
**Tellest.** Dost number, recount, or keep count of (see on Ps. 48:12). David turns abruptly from imprecation to tender petition for himself.
**My wanderings.** See 1 Sam. 21:10.
**Put thou my tears.** As though God took note of his tears, drop by drop. The illustration is a recognition of God’s tender solicitude for His child.
**Bottle.** Heb. no’d, the skin bottle that was used by the Easterners as a container for water, milk, wine, etc. The psalmist prays that his tears may be placed in a skin bottle, that they may be remembered before God.
**Book.** Compare Ps. 69:28; 139:16;; Mal. 3:16. “In the book of God’s remembrance … every act of sacrifice, every suffering and sorrow endured for Christ’s sake, is recorded” (GC 481).
8.zh:
我幾次流離，你都記數；求你把我眼淚裝在你的皮袋裡。這不都記在你冊子上嗎？

**記數。**統計（見詩48:12註釋）。大衛突然從咒詛轉到為自己懇求。
**我幾次流離。**見撒上21:10。
**求你把我眼淚裝。**似乎上帝注意到他的每一滴眼淚。這句話說明上帝關愛著祂的兒女。
**皮袋（no'd）。**東方人用來裝水，奶和果酒等。詩人祈求把他的眼淚裝在皮袋裡，在上帝面前蒙紀念。
**冊子。**參詩69:28；139:16;；瑪3:16。“在上帝的紀念冊裡，……每一個犧牲的舉動，每一次因基督的緣故所受的痛苦和悲傷，都有記錄（《善惡之爭》第481頁）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《善惡之爭》第481頁。

0.zh:
序言——《詩篇》56和57篇稱為“姊妹篇”，因為她們在內容和主題的展開上很相似；有著相同的開頭；由兩個相似的部分構成，內容是祈求得救，和讚美得救；在每一段的結尾用了副歌。這兩首詩都是在極其困難的環境下寫的，表達了完全信賴上帝，從而戰勝一切的懼怕。本詩增加了兩節感恩的話。根據題記，本詩是大衛所作（和詩57篇一樣，見該詩序言），起因是他在迦特與非利士人的遭遇（見撒上21:13註釋）。
關於本詩的題記，見本冊註釋第616,628頁（《詩篇》序言）。“鴿”的希伯來語是yonah。調名可能與大衛的情感有關：他被迫離家，遠走他鄉避難，就像鴿子被趕出鳥巢。題記含有哀婉，柔弱的色彩。
非利士人在迦特拿住大衛，那時，他作這金詩，交與伶長。調用遠方無聲鴿。
0.en:
INTRODUCTION.—Ps. 56, 57 have been called “twin psalms,” because of similarities in content and in development of theme. They begin with the same words, consist of two similar parts embodying prayer for deliverance desired, and praise for deliverance gained; and employ a refrain at the close of each section. Written under circumstances of grievous trouble, they both express the complete confidence in God that overcomes all fear. The two parts of Ps. 56 (vs. 1–4, 5–11) are similar in thought, the second more emphatic than the first. Each closes with a refrain, augmented on its second occurrence. Two verses of gratitude are added to the poem. According to the superscription Ps. 56 was the work of David (as Ps. 57 is known to be; see Introduction to Ps. 57), composed as a result of his experience with the Philistines at Gath (see on 1 Sam. 21:13).
On the superscription see pp. 616, 628. “Jonath” is from the Heb. yonah, meaning “dove.” It may be that the title of the melody to which this psalm was sung was suggested by the feelings of David, driven from home, seeking safety in a remote region, like a dove driven from its nesting place. There is something plaintive and tender implicit in this supposition.

1.zh:
（非利士人在迦特拿住大衛。那時，他作這金詩，交與伶長。調用遠方無聲鴿。）神啊，求你憐憫我，因為人要把我吞了，終日攻擊欺壓我。

**求你憐憫我。**見詩51:1；57:1。
**人（'enosh）。**“軟弱的人”（見詩8:4註釋）。與“大能者”上帝”形成強烈的對比。
**把我吞了。**七十士譯本為“踐踏我”。參第2節。
**終日。**參第2,5節。
1.en:
**Be merciful.** See Ps. 51:1; 57:1.
**Man.** Heb. ’enosh, “man in his frailty” (see on Ps. 8:4). The contrast between “God,” the Powerful One, and ’enosh is strong.
**Swallow me up.** The LXX reads “trample me down.” Compare v. 2.
**Daily.** Compare vs. 2, 5.

2.zh:
我的仇敵終日要把我吞了，因逞驕傲攻擊我的人甚多。

**逞驕傲。**希伯來語是marom（“從高處”）。英文KJV版為“至高者啊！”
2.en: **O thou most High.** Heb. marom, not used elsewhere as a title of the Deity, and it is doubtful whether it is so intended here. A slight change in vowel pointing yields the reading “from a height,” which may be interpreted as meaning “haughtily.”

3.zh:
我懼怕的時候要倚靠你。

**要倚靠你。**這是本詩的基調。在懼怕的時候，我們可以有意識地信賴上帝。這樣的決心，是基督徒經驗的可靠基礎。我們需要維護我們的信心。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第467頁；《福山寶訓》第156頁；《先祖與先知》第692頁。
3.en: **I will trust.** The keynote of the psalm. When fear oppresses, by an act of will we may put our trust in God. There is in such a resolution a sound basis for Christian experience. We need to assert our trust.

4.zh:
我倚靠神，我要讚美他的話；我倚靠神，必不懼怕。血氣之輩能把我怎麼樣呢？

見太10:28。第4節是本詩的副歌，經過擴大在第10和第11節中重複。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《今日的生活》第297頁。
4.en: **What flesh can do.** See Matt. 10:28. Verse 4 is the refrain of the psalm, and is repeated in augmented form in vs. 10 and 11.

6.zh:
他們聚集，埋伏窺探我的腳蹤，等候要害我的命。

**他們聚集。**本節用一連串簡練的短句說明敵人設計陷害詩人。
**命。**見詩16:10註釋。
6.en:
**They gather.** The devious methods employed to pursue the psalmist are represented by the rapid succession of clauses without expressed grammatical connection.
**Soul.** See on Ps. 16:10.

7.zh:
他們豈能因罪孽逃脫嗎？神啊，求你在怒中使眾民墮落！

他們豈能因罪孽逃脫麼？原文含義不明。詩人實際上是問：在罪惡中有安全嗎？仇敵能把他們表面上的平安，歸功於他們的罪惡嗎？
**眾民。**直譯是“各國人民”。詩人在這裡可能擴大了“仇敵”的範圍，把所有的惡人和罪惡都包括在他的詛咒之中（見第624）。
7.en:
**Shall they escape by iniquity?** The Hebrew of the clause thus translated is obscure. If the KJV rendering is correct the psalmist is inquiring in effect, Can they find safety in wickedness? Can it be possible that the enemies owe their apparent safety to their great wickedness?
**The people.** Literally, “the peoples.” The psalmist may here be extending the range of the word “enemies” to include all wicked people, all wickedness, in his imprecation (see p. 624).

9.zh:
我呼求的日子，我的仇敵都要轉身退後。神幫助我，這是我所知道的。

詩人確信上帝站在他一邊。這樣的信心是不會失敗的。我們要好好數算基督徒經驗中“我所知道的”（見伯19:25；詩20:6；135:5；140:12；提後1:12）。
9.en: **This I know.** The psalmist is sure that God is on his side. Such certainty brooks no defeat. We do well to count the “I know’s” of Christian experience (see Job 19:25; Ps. 20:6; 135:5; 140:12; 2 Tim. 1:12).

10.zh:
我倚靠神，我要讚美他的話；我倚靠耶和華，我要讚美他的話。

這是第4節副歌的擴大（第4節）。
10.en: **Will I praise.** This entire clause is a forceful addition to the earlier refrain (v. 4).

11.zh:
我倚靠神，必不懼怕。人能把我怎麼樣呢？

**人（'adam）。**見詩8:4註釋。在第4節裡為“血氣之輩”。
**懷愛倫註釋（11–13節）**。《服務真詮》第101頁。
11.en: **Man.** Heb. ’adam (see on Ps. 8:4); the clause that stands parallel in v. 4 reads “flesh.”

12.zh:
神啊，我向你所許的願在我身上；我要將感謝祭獻給你。

**我向你所許的願。**詩歌的最後是兩節感恩的話（其姊妹篇57篇只有11節，以副歌結束，沒有這樣的感恩句）。詩人曾許願要表示感謝上帝應允他的祈禱。現在他要履行自己的諾言。
**感謝祭（todoth）。**見耶17:26；33:11。
12.en:
**Thy vows.** Two verses of thanksgiving conclude the poem (the “twin psalm,” Ps. 57, closes with a refrain, without verses of this type, having only 11 verses in all). The psalmist has vowed to express his gratitude to God for answering his prayer. He now proceeds to fulfill his obligation.
**Praises.** Heb. todoth, also representing “thank offerings” (see Jer. 17:26; 33:11).

13.zh:
因為你救我的命脫離死亡。你豈不是救護我的腳不跌倒、使我在生命光中行在神面前嗎？

**上帝面前。**意思是符合上帝的旨意。上帝對亞伯拉罕說：“你當在我面前作完全人”（創17:1）。
**生命光。**參伯33:30。
13.en:
**Before God.** The phrase suggests agreement with the will of God. God said to Abraham: “Walk before me, and be thou perfect” (Gen. 17:1).
**Light of the living.** Compare Job 33:30.

30.en: **Praise him.** We should praise the Lord publicly. He is ever at our side to help us and to save us from those enemies who are seeking to destroy us.
30.zh:
我要用口極力稱謝耶和華；我要在眾人中間讚美他；

我們應該在大庭廣眾中讚美上帝。祂一直在我們的身旁幫助我們，救我們脫離想要害我們的仇敵。

0.zh:
序言——這首詩是寫給伶長的，可能用於會幕和聖殿侍奉時的吟唱。本詩警告那些以怨報愛，忘恩負義的人。《新約》引用本詩的段落指猶大的下場（見徒1:16-20）。本詩分為三段：第一段是詩人祈求幫助來對付仇敵（第1-5節）；第二段懇求讓這夥罪魁禍首得到報應（第6-20節）；第三段在求救的呼籲之後，迸發出感謝耶和華的歌聲（第21-31節）。
關於本詩的題記，見本冊註釋第616,627頁（《詩篇》序言）。
大衛的詩，交與伶長。
0.en:
INTRODUCTION.—Ps. 109 is dedicated to the chief musician. Probably it was intended to be sung for the tabernacle and Temple services. It is a warning against those who return hatred for love and ingratitude for kindness. The NT makes reference to a portion of this psalm as applying to the experience of Judas (see Acts 1:16–20). The psalm falls into three divisions: the psalmist appeals for help against his enemies (vs. 1–5); he invokes retribution against the leader of this treacherous group (vs. 6–20); he breaks forth into a song of thanksgiving to Jehovah after a plea for deliverance (vs. 21–31).
On the superscription see pp. 616, 627.

1.zh:
（大衛的詩，交與伶長。）我所讚美的神啊，求你不要閉口不言。

敵人在誹謗詩人，嘲笑他的上帝。大衛與他的主十分熟悉，並深深地信靠祂，所以他敢求這位“朋友”打破沉默。
1.en: **Hold not thy peace.** The enemies were slandering the psalmist and mocking his God. David knew his Lord so intimately and his confidence was so deep that he boldly asked his Friend to break the silence and to speak.

2.zh:
因為惡人的嘴和詭詐人的口已經張開攻擊我；他們用撒謊的舌頭對我說話。

偽證人對詩人提出毫無根據的指控。謠言是很難忍受的。但主教導我們，當人因基督的緣故捏造各樣壞話毀謗我們的時候，我們要歡喜快樂（太5:11）。
2.en: **Lying tongue.** False witnesses support the unfounded accusations against the psalmist. It is hard to endure lying reports, but we are admonished to rejoice when all manner of evil is spoken of us falsely for Christ’s sake (Matt. 5:11).

3.zh:
他們圍繞我，說怨恨的話，又無故地攻打我。

參耶18:18。
3.en: **Words of hatred.** Compare Jer. 18:18.

4.zh:
他們與我為敵以報我愛，但我專心祈禱。

詩人不想報復，卻專心祈禱懇求。那些在與上帝交通的隱秘處躲避一切試探和毀謗的人是有福的。
4.en: **Unto prayer.** Rather than retaliate, the psalmist gave himself to prayer and intercession. Happy is the man who can find refuge from every trial and false accusation in the secret place of communion with God.

5.zh:
他們向我以惡報善，以恨報愛。

詩人愛仇敵，卻受到了他們更深敵意的回報。上帝的兒子基督，表現出對仇敵最大的愛心（見羅5:7-10）。從來沒有人表達出像祂那樣的愛。儘管祂表現出這樣的愛，仍然被出賣和釘在十字架上。祂在臨死的極大痛苦中，絲毫沒有減少對仇敵的愛。祂祈禱說：“父阿，赦免他們。因為他們所作的，他們不曉得”（路23:34）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第265頁；《善惡之爭》第20頁。
5.en: **For my love.** The kindness of the psalmist to his enemies was required by more severe hatred on their part. The greatest demonstration of love toward enemies was seen in Christ, the Son of God (see Rom. 5:7–10). There never was love manifested like His. Despite the manifestation of this love He was betrayed and crucified. Yet in His dying agony His love for His enemies lost none of its ardor as He prayed, “Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do” (Luke 23:34).

6.zh:
願你派一個惡人轄制他，派一個對頭站在他右邊！

上帝常常允許一個罪惡的暴君統治犯罪的百姓。
6.en: **Wicked man over him.** God often permits a wicked tyrant to control a sinful people.

7.zh:
他受審判的時候，願他出來擔當罪名！願他的祈禱反成為罪！

這裡的動詞是一般將來時，表示一種希望。惡人的祈禱並不是出於真心的懺悔，而是為犯罪的後果悲哀。這樣的祈禱上帝是不接受的（見箴28:9；賽1:15）。
7.en: **Let his prayer become sin.** Literally, “his prayer shall become sin.” The verb here used is a simple future, as distinguished from the form specifying a wish. The prayer of the wicked does not proceed from true penitence, but from sorrow for the results of the sin. Such prayers God cannot accept (see Prov. 28:9; Isa. 1:15).

8.zh:
願他的年日短少！願別人得他的職分！

**願他的年日短少。**或“他的年日將短少”（見第7節註釋）。
**職分（pequddah）。**指監督的職分。彼得以本節為依據，提出另選一位使徒代替猶大（見徒1:20）。
8.en:
**Let his days be few.** The Hebrew allows the alternate translation, “his days will be few” (see on v. 7).
**Office.** Heb. pequddah, signifying the office of the overseer. This verse was cited by Peter as a sanction for filling the place of Judas by the election of another apostle (see Acts 1:20).

9.zh:
願他的兒女為孤兒，他的妻子為寡婦！

在這個犯罪的世界中，“兒女不可避免地要受到父母犯罪的影響”（《先祖與先知》第306頁；見書7:15註釋）。但上帝恩待義人的後代，一代接著一代向他們發慈愛（出20:6）。
9.en: **Fatherless.** In this world of sin “it is inevitable that children should suffer from the consequences of parental wrongdoing” (PP 306; see on Joshua 7:15). Conversely, the Lord is gracious to the offspring of the righteous and extends mercy to their succeeding generations (Ex. 20:6).

11.zh:
願強暴的債主牢籠他一切所有的！願外人搶他勞碌得來的！

指放高利貸的人。這裡說他奪取債務人的一切財產。
11.en: **Extortioner.** One who puts out his money to usury. He is here represented as demanding everything that his debtor possesses.

12.zh:
願無人向他延綿施恩！願無人可憐他的孤兒！

雖然上帝的愛是永恆的（見耶31:3），但聖靈的懇勸和對忘恩負義之罪人的施恩會有結束的時候（見創6:3）。
12.en: **To extend mercy.** That is, to make mercy continue or last. While it is true that the Lord’s love is everlasting (see Jer. 31:3), there comes an end to the pleadings of the Holy Spirit and to the extending of mercy to ungrateful sinners (see Gen. 6:3).

13.zh:
願他的後人斷絕，名字被塗抹，不傳於下代！

以色列人有強烈的自家認同感，希望自己的名號在子孫身上延續。他們把名號的斷絕視為巨大的災難（見創38:8註釋）。
13.en: **Generation following.** The Israelite, with his strong sense of family solidarity, looked forward to his name living on in his descendants. The extinction of the family name was considered a terrible calamity (see on Gen. 38:8).

17.zh:
他愛咒罵，咒罵就臨到他；他不喜愛福樂，福樂就與他遠離！

這裡表達惡人的命運和第7節一樣，不是作為一種希望，而是惡人的行為給自己所帶來的不可避免的結局。
17.en: **Let it come.** Here, as in v. 7, the fate of the wicked is expressed, not so much in the form of a wish, but in the simple historical form, as the inevitable result of the decision that the wicked have pronounced upon themselves by their conduct.

20.zh:
這就是我對頭和用惡言議論我的人從耶和華那裡所受的報應。

蔑視上帝慈愛和恩典的人給自己帶來咒詛。他們的懲罰是罪有應得的，是他們自己選擇的必然結果。
20.en: **Reward.** Those who despite God’s love and His grace bring a curse upon themselves. Their punishment is a reward for their actions, the inevitable result of their own choice.

23.zh:
我如日影漸漸偏斜而去；我如蝗蟲被抖出來。

**日影。**太陽下山時，影子就會延長，直到完全消逝在所降臨的暮色之中。
**被抖出來。**詩人覺得自己無依無靠，就像可憐的蝗蟲。
23.en:
**Shadow.** When the day declines, the shadow lengthens till it vanishes in the descending darkness.
**Tossed up and down.** Better, “shaken off.” The psalmist feels as helpless as the poor locust.

26.zh:
耶和華─我的神啊，求你幫助我，照你的慈愛拯救我，

在詩歌的結尾又一次提出懇求。詩人完全依靠上帝的慈愛。本詩的最後希望苦難之後是榮耀，十架之後是冠冕。
26.en: **Help me.** In the concluding section of the psalm, the cry for help is renewed, and the psalmist casts himself wholly upon the mercy of God. The psalm closes with the joyous prospect that after the suffering will come the glory, after the cross, the crown.

28.zh:
任憑他們咒罵，惟願你賜福；他們幾時起來就必蒙羞，你的僕人卻要歡喜。

只要我們知道天國的福氣正降臨我們身上，受惡人的咒罵又有何妨？
28.en: **Bless thou.** What matters whether we are cursed by wicked men as long as we know that the blessing of Heaven is resting upon us?

29.zh:
願我的對頭披戴羞辱！願他們以自己的羞愧為外袍遮身！

犯罪總會帶來羞辱（見創3:7-11）。
29.en: **Clothed with shame.** Sin always brings shame and disgrace (see Gen. 3:7–11).

31.zh:
因為他必站在窮乏人的右邊，要救他脫離審判他靈魂的人。

第 一百一十首 篇
序言——本詩為大衛所作（見太22:41-45；可12:35-37；路20:41-43），在希伯來文學中屬最莊嚴的詩歌。本詩被稱為“彌賽亞詩歌的珍珠”，不僅描寫基督為世界的君王和統治者，而且憑著上帝莊嚴的誓言，擔任永遠的祭司。參亞6:13，稱彌賽亞被為祭司和君王。
本詩大量出現烏加列語詞語（見本冊第618頁）。在整部《詩篇》中約有46%的詞彙在烏加列語出現。但在本詩中烏加列語詞語的比例高達71%，和詩29篇和93篇一樣。
關於本詩的題記，見本冊註釋第616,627頁（《詩篇》序言）。
大衛的詩。

1.en: **I was glad.** The psalmist rejoiced at the opportunity of joining others for the journey to worship at Jerusalem. There is joy in worshiping in the society of kindred spirits.
1.zh:
（大衛上行之詩。）人對我說：我們往耶和華的殿去，我就歡喜。

詩人感到高興是因為有機會和別人一同前往耶路撒冷敬拜。志同道合的人一起敬拜是很高興的事。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–6節）**。《先祖與先知》第538頁。

0.zh:
序言——這又是一首朝聖的詩歌（見《詩篇》120篇序言）。本詩表達了有權前往耶路撒冷敬拜的喜樂。
大衛上行之詩。
0.en: INTRODUCTION.—Ps. 122 is another of the pilgrim psalms (see Introduction to Ps. 120). It is an expression of joy for the privilege of going up to Jerusalem to worship.

2.zh:
耶路撒冷啊，我們的腳站在你的門內。

似乎是在回顧。詩人過去一定到過聖城，所以他懷著聖潔的喜樂，盼望再次有機會到那裡敬拜。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第76,448頁；《先祖與先知》第412頁。
2.en: **Our feet shall stand.** Or, “our feet were standing,” as if stated in retrospect. The psalmist had undoubtedly been blessed by his past visits to the Holy City, and in the light of these he anticipated with holy joy another opportunity to worship there.

3.zh:
耶路撒冷被建造，如同連絡整齊的一座城。

**連絡（chabar）。**相關的希伯來名詞chaber指“同伴”。故有人認為這是指上帝的子民在屬靈上的結合。七十士譯本更加明確了團契的概念，可譯為“耶路撒冷造成了一座城。大家（metoche）同心合意”。
3.en: **Compact.** Heb. chabar, “to be united,” “to be joined with”; the corresponding Hebrew noun, chaber, means “companion” or “fellow.” Some see in this an allusion to the gathering of God’s people for spiritual fellowship. The idea of fellowship is more definitely expressed in the LXX, which here may be translated, “Jerusalem is built as a city, whose fellowship [Gk. metoche] is together.”

4.zh:
眾支派，就是耶和華的支派，上那裡去，按以色列的常例（或譯：作以色列的證據）稱讚耶和華的名。

**常例。**指上帝所規定的制度（見申16:16；參詩81:3-5；見詩19:7註釋）。直譯是“以色列的證據，稱讚耶和華的名”。“按”是外加的。
4.en: **Testimony.** In the sense of an institution ordained by God (see Deut. 16:16; cf. Ps. 81:3–5; see on Ps. 19:7). The clause reads literally, “a testimony for Israel, to give thanks to the name of Yahweh.” The words “unto the” before “testimony” have been supplied.

5.zh:
因為在那裡設立審判的寶座，就是大衛家的寶座。

政權的所在地耶路撒冷是全國司法的中心。如果以色列的國王能按上帝的旨意執政，他們的政權就會保持和促進憐憫，公義，平安，喜樂和仁愛。這些都是來自上帝寶座的品格。
5.en: **Thrones of judgment.** Jerusalem, as the seat of government, was the center of justice for the entire nation. Had Israel’s kings ruled as God designed, their governments would have promoted and conserved mercy, righteousness, peace, joy, love. These are the qualities that come from the divine throne.

6.zh:
你們要為耶路撒冷求平安！耶路撒冷啊，愛你的人必然興旺！

這個名稱暗示耶路撒冷應是一個平安的地方。
6.en: **Jerusalem.** The very name implied that the city should be a place of peace.

7.zh:
願你城中平安！願你宮內興旺！

參撒上25:6；路10:5；約20:19。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第76頁；《先祖與先知》第539頁。
7.en: **Peace.** Compare 1 Sam. 25:6; Luke 10:5; John 20:19.

8.zh:
因我弟兄和同伴的緣故，我要說：願平安在你中間！

耶路撒冷有平安對於所有的以色列人都是有好處的。第8,9節闡明瞭每一個基督徒必須遵循的兩條大原則：一，愛兄弟；二，愛教會。愛上帝的人必然會愛組成上帝教會的兄弟。
8.en: **For my brethren.** It was to the obvious advantage of all Israel that there should be peace in Jerusalem. Verses 8, 9 lay down two great principles that should actuate every Christian: (1) love for the brethren, (2) love for the church. Those who love God will love the brethren of whom God’s church is composed.

2.en: **The beauty of holiness.** Literally, “in holy adornment.” This phrase appears again in Ps. 96:9. Beyond the attiring of the body is the adorning of the soul. No external comeliness can compare with the beauty of holy character (see 1 Peter 3:3, 4). In this prelude, if angels are intended by the phrase “mighty” (see on Ps. 29:1), the psalmist lifts us from the earth to heaven by calling on the angels to praise Him whose power is manifested in the thunderstorm about to be described.
2.zh:
要將耶和華的名所當得的榮耀歸給他，以聖潔的（的：或譯為）妝飾敬拜耶和華。

**聖潔的妝飾。**這個短語還出現在詩96:9中。心靈的裝飾勝過身體的打扮。外表的美麗是無法與聖潔的品格媲美的（見彼前3:3,4）。如果把詩歌開頭的“眾子”理解為天使（見第1節註釋），詩人是通過呼籲天使讚美上帝，把我們的思想從地上提高到天上。上帝的大能表顯在下面所描寫的雷暴雨中。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督教育之研究》第245頁；《證言》卷四第555頁；《證言》卷六第363頁。

0.zh:
序言——本詩被稱為“雷暴雨之歌”和“七雷之歌”，是一首典型的希伯來描述自然的詩歌。希伯來詩人從來不滿足於用語言來描繪自然景象。他總是從大自然中看到創造主的能力和榮耀。上帝的名“耶和華”在本詩共出現了18次。本詩繪聲繪色地描寫了一場暴風雨，從一開始到高潮，到最後消失。本詩的結構呈現精巧的對稱，無論是在開頭（第1,2節），還是用七次“耶和華的聲音”（第3-9節）描寫打雷，還是在結尾（第10,11節）。本詩猶如一塊文字的浮雕寶石。
本詩描寫了一場源于海洋的大風暴，伴隨著陣陣狂風和雷聲，以及耀眼的閃電，從地中海開始，掃過黎巴嫩和前黎巴嫩的山脈，最後消失在東方沙漠。本詩在烏加列語（見本書第618,619頁）中有許多細微的對稱。值得一提的是三重複現象，如第1,2節的“歸給”，第4,5節的“聲音”和第6節的“黎巴嫩” 和“西連”（見申3:9註釋）。烏加列語文獻版還澄清了幾個含糊的地方（見第6,8節註釋）。
根據遺統，在第二聖殿時期，住棚節的最後一天要唱這首詩。本詩已成了五旬節第一天猶太會堂禮儀的一部分，也包括在安息日的禮拜中。
關於題記，見本書第616,627頁（《詩篇》序言）。
大衛的詩。
0.en:
INTRODUCTION.—Ps. 29 has been entitled The Song of the Thunderstorm, The Song of the Seven Thunders. It is typical of all the Hebrew nature psalms. The Hebrew poet is never satisfied merely to paint word pictures of nature. He always sees in nature the power and glory of her Creator (God’s name [Yahweh] appears 18 times in the psalm). In this psalm a storm is thrillingly described from its beginning, through the height of its intensity, until it dies away. The structure of the poem exhibits elaborate symmetry, which appears in the prelude (vs. 1, 2), in the description of the storm with its sevenfold repetition of the phrase “the voice of the Lord” (vs. 3–9), and in the conclusion (vs. 10, 11). It is a verbal cameo.
The psalm describes the fury of a great storm originating over the sea, accompanied by gale winds, by peals of thunder, and by fiery flashes of lightning, coming in from the Mediterranean and sweeping over the Lebanon and Anti-Lebanon mountains before it loses its force in the eastern desert. The poem finds numerous detailed parallels in Ugaritic (see pp. 618, 619). Of these may be mentioned the tricolons of vs. 1 and 2 (give) and of vs. 4 and 5 (voice), and the names “Lebanon” and “Sirion” (see on Deut. 3:9) of v. 6. The Ugaritic has also cleared up several obscurities (see on vs. 6, 8).
Tradition says that in the Second Temple this psalm was sung on the last day of the Feast of Tabernacles. The psalm now forms a part of the synagogue service on the first day of Pentecost and is included in the Sabbath liturgy.
On the superscription see pp. 616, 627.

1.zh:
（大衛的詩。）神的眾子啊，你們要將榮耀、能力歸給耶和華，歸給耶和華！

**眾子（bene 'elim）。**含義不明。KJV版為“有能力的”。七十士譯本為“上帝的眾子”，可能指天使（見伯1:6註釋）。該詞在《詩篇》其他地方中出現一次，就是詩89:6。那裡的對稱句似乎傾向於這種解釋。
**榮耀。**詩人承認上帝為有榮耀和能力的神。“榮耀”一詞成了第9節的高潮（見詩68:34）。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–2節）**。《證言》卷六第366頁。
1.en:
**Mighty.** Heb. bene ’elim, the translation of which is uncertain. The LXX reads, “sons of God,” by which possibly the angels are meant (see on Job 1:6). The parallelism of Ps. 89:6 (the only other occurrence of the phrase in the psalms) seems to lend support to this idea.
**Glory.** The psalmist acknowledges God as the God of glory and might. The word “glory” is used as a climax in v. 9 (see Ps. 68:34).

3.zh:
耶和華的聲音發在水上；榮耀的神打雷，耶和華打雷在大水之上。

**耶和華的聲音。**詩人在3-9節的交響曲中描寫了一場他所回憶的雷暴雨。這場雷暴雨源於地中海，橫掃黎巴嫩，最後消失在東方，給沙漠留下寧靜和溫暖。對於他來說，雷聲就是“耶和華的聲音”（見詩18:13）。這個短語在第3-9節用了七次。
**榮耀的上帝。**參“榮耀的王”（詩24:7-10）。“榮耀”在詩29:1-3中重複了三次。
**大水。**或“眾水”。
3.en:
**The voice of the Lord.** In the verbal symphony of vs. 3–9 the psalmist describes what is obviously his own recollection of a thunderstorm sweeping in from the Mediterranean Sea, breaking in fury on Lebanon, and then dying away in the east, leaving the desert warm and peaceful. To him, thunder is “the voice of the Lord” (see Ps. 18:13). The phrase is used seven times in vs. 3–9.
**God of glory.** Compare the expression “King of glory” (Ps. 24:7–10). The word “glory” is repeated three times in Ps. 29:1–3.
**Many waters.** Or, “great waters.”

4.zh:
耶和華的聲音大有能力；耶和華的聲音滿有威嚴。

**大有能力。**詩人從風暴中看到上帝的一些特性。
**滿有威嚴。**風雷開始滾過大地。
4.en:
**Powerful.** Literally, “with power.” The psalmist sees certain of God’s attributes displayed in the storm.
**Full of majesty.** Literally, “in majesty.” The thunder is beginning to roll over the land.

5.zh:
耶和華的聲音震破香柏樹；耶和華震碎利巴嫩的香柏樹。

風暴襲擊了黎巴嫩山脈，大風颳斷了山上有名的香柏樹。雷電也摧毀了許多大樹。
5.en: **Breaketh the cedars.** The storm swoops down upon the Lebanon Mountains, famous for their cedars, and the heavy wind breaks the mighty trees. The lightning, too, may have added to the destruction by shattering many a stately cedar.

6.zh:
他也使之跳躍如牛犢，使利巴嫩和西連跳躍如野牛犢。

**之。**指黎巴嫩山和西連山在風暴的衝擊下震撼晃盪。
**跳躍如牛犢。**參詩68:16；114:4。
**西連。**西頓人對黑門山的稱呼。它是前黎巴嫩最高的山，海拔9,232英尺（見申3:9註釋）。
**牛犢。**或“野牛”（見詩22:21註釋）。
6.en:
**Them.** In the Hebrew this pronoun appears as a suffix to the verb in the form –em. The form is actually an archaic grammatical (enclitic) form not understood by the Jewish scholars who added the pronunciation to the vowelless text from the 7th century .. and on. Ugaritic (see p. 618) has shown that the ending –em should remain untranslated, so that the passage should be rendered: “He makes Lebanon to skip like a calf, and Sirion like a young wild ox” (RSV). The mountains of Lebanon and Sirion themselves are meant, which appear to skip under the impact of the storm.
**Skip like a calf.** See Ps. 68:16; 114:4.
**Sirion.** The Sidonian name for Mt. Hermon, the highest mountain in the Anti-Lebanon range, towering 9,232 feet above sea level (see on Deut. 3:9).
**Unicorn.** Rather, “wild ox” (see on Ps. 22:21).

7.zh:
耶和華的聲音使火焰分岔。

**分岔。**直譯是“割掉”，“砍掉”。描寫閃電帶著鮮明而顯耀的曲折線條、如同蛇的形狀。
7.en: **Divideth.** Literally, “cut,” “hew out.” The verse describes the vivid, zigzag, serpentlike flashes of the lightning.

8.zh:
耶和華的聲音震動曠野；耶和華震動加低斯的曠野。

在烏加列文獻發現以前，人們認為風暴是掃過整個巴勒斯坦的，從北部的黎巴嫩到南部邊境的加低斯。加低斯在別是巴西南（見民20:16）約70.4公里，就是加低斯巴尼亞。以色列人曾在這裡派遣探子到迦南地（民13:17-20），後來因發怨言而被迫撤到曠野去（民14章）。但經過對烏加列文獻的考證（見本書第618頁），認定“加低斯的曠野”是指敘利亞沙漠（見第3節註釋）。
8.en: **Wilderness of Kadesh.** Before the discovery of the Ugaritic texts it was thought that the storm was pictured as passing over all Palestine, from Lebanon in the north to Kadesh on the southern border, about 45 mi. (70.4 km.) southwest of Beersheba (see Num. 20:16). Kadesh was identified with Kadesh-barnea, the place from which the Hebrews sent the spies into Canaan (Num. 13:17–20) and from which the people were made to retreat into the wilderness because of their murmuring (Num. 14). However, a study of the Ugaritic texts (see p. 618) has shown that the term “wilderness of Kadesh” was a name for the Syrian Desert (see on v. 3).

9.zh:
耶和華的聲音驚動母鹿落胎，樹木也脫落淨光。凡在他殿中的，都稱說他的榮耀。

**母鹿落胎。**明顯是由於雷暴雨所造成的恐懼。有些阿拉伯詩人，以及普盧塔克（古希臘作家，約公元46-120）和普林尼（羅馬作家，約公元61-112）曾記錄了這種現象。
在英文RSV版把“母鹿”譯為“橡樹” ，使平行更加明顯一些。但不知希伯來語的'ayyaloth能否視為'ayil（橡樹）的複數。'ayil的複數通常是'elim（見賽1:29）。
**脫落淨光（chasaph）。**“剝去”，“赤身”。
**他殿中。**可能不是指帳篷，而是指大自然。
**都。**雷鳴，閃電，劈開的大樹，震動的曠野，樹上掃落的葉子，都宣告上帝的大能和榮耀。柯爾律治（英國詩人，1772-1834）說：“地球以其千萬聲音讚美上帝”（柯爾律治）。參詩19:2。我們最好以敬畏之心面對大自然驚人的現象，然後用心來讚美威嚴大能的上帝。宇宙的合唱使我們想起以賽亞異像中撒拉弗的不住頌讚（見賽6:2,3）。隨著本節的高潮，風暴消退了，詩人轉向平靜的思考，並宣佈上帝的主權和祂所賜的奇妙平安。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《教育論》第308頁；《福山寶訓》第70頁；《證言》卷九第30頁。
9.en:
**Hinds to calve.** Obviously because of fear induced by the thunderstorm. Certain Arabian poets, also Plutarch and Pliny, have recorded this phenomenon.
The RSV translation “oaks” instead of “hinds” supplies a better parallelism. But it is questionable whether the Heb. ’ayyaloth (“hinds” KJV) can properly be considered the plural of ’ayil, “oak.” The normal plural of ’ayil is ’elim (see Isa. 1:29).
**Discovereth.** Heb. chaśaph, “to strip,” “to lay bare.”
**His temple.** Probably here not the tabernacle, but the world of nature.
**Every one.** Or, “everything.” All things—the thunder, the lightning, the crashing of the trees, the shaking of the wilderness, the leaves being stripped from the trees—declare the power and glory of God. “Earth, with her thousand voices, praises God” (Coleridge). Compare Ps. 19:2. It is a good thing for us to stand in awe in the presence of the violent phenomena of nature, and then to lift our hearts in praise to the God of majesty and power. The universal chorus of praise reminds us of the continuous adoration of the seraphim in Isaiah’s vision (see Isa. 6:2, 3). With the climactic description of this verse, the storm subsides, and the psalmist turns to quiet meditation and to a declaration of God’s sovereignty and His wonderful gift of peace.

10.zh:
洪水泛濫之時，耶和華坐著為王；耶和華坐著為王，直到永遠。

**洪水。**有人認為是指挪亞洪水。其實把它說成雷暴雨描述的繼續更自然一些。洪水是伴隨著風暴的大雨所造成的。
**坐著為王，直到永遠。**正如上帝出現在過去的風暴中，祂將永遠執掌絕對的王權。本詩的最後宣佈了在風暴的混亂和恐怖以後給心靈所帶來平安和信心。
10.en:
**Flood.** Some see a reference here to the Noachian Deluge, but it seems more natural to continue the description of the thunderstorm and see in the flood a picture of the heavy rain accompanying the storm, and its results.
**King for ever.** As God was in the storm now passed, so He will preside as absolute sovereign forever. There is a finality to the declaration that brings calm and confidence to the soul after the commotion and consternation of the storm.

11.zh:
耶和華必賜力量給他的百姓；耶和華必賜平安的福給他的百姓。

**力量。**上帝在風暴中顯示了驚人的大能。祂足以高舉祂的子民（見賽40:29-31）。
**平安。**這是上天賜給人類最寶貴的禮物（見詩85:8,10；約14:27；腓4:7；帖前5:23）。在任何一種語言中，沒有什麼比平安更美好的詞語了。邱吉爾說過：“外面雖然是戰爭的風暴，大地被狂風所掃蕩，但我們的內心有平安”。這部詩篇的交響曲在震耳欲聾的漸強音以後，就這樣以最極輕柔的聲音結束了（松西諾《詩篇》註釋）。和平之君說：“願你們平安”（約20:21,26）。
11.en:
**Strength.** The God whose power is seen so strikingly in the storm is abundantly able to uphold His people (see Isa. 40:29–31).
**Peace.** The most gracious gift that Heaven can bestow upon mortals (see Ps. 85:8, 10; John 14:27; Phil. 4:7; 1 Thess. 5:23). There is no sweeter word in any language. Churchill said, “Outside, the storms of war may blow and the lands may be lashed with the fury of its gales, but in our own hearts … there is peace.” Thus the symphony of Ps. 29, which has swelled to an ear-shattering crescendo, ends in the softest pianissimo (Soncino, on the Psalms). “Peace be unto you” (John 20:21, 26), says the Prince of Peace.
**Their inward thought.** The rich seem to forget that, sooner or later, men forget the name of the man who once owned their estates, and his memory passes into oblivion.
11.zh:
他們心裡思想：他們的家室必永存，住宅必留到萬代；他們以自己的名稱自己的地。

富人似乎忘記了，遲早人們會遺忘財產原來主人的名字，不再去紀念。

0.zh:
序言——本詩回答了以下的問題：“為什麼富人似乎擁有人生的好處？”本詩說明財富不能推遲死亡；，富人在死時降到與窮人一樣的地步。在四節前言以後，這首訓誨詩講述了人生的短暫，特別是擁有屬世財富的人（第5-13節）；然後描寫義人最後得到的安慰，就是永生，與惡人的命運形成對照（第14-20節）。在現代正統的猶太人家庭裡，家人去世後傷心的一週裡，要背誦《詩篇》49篇。
關於本詩的題記，見本書617,627頁（《詩篇》序言）。
可拉後裔的詩，交與伶長。
0.en:
INTRODUCTION.—Ps. 49 contains an answer to the question, “Why do the rich appear to have the advantage in life?” The psalm teaches that wealth cannot postpone death, and that at death the rich are reduced to the same level as the poor. After an introduction of four verses, this didactic poem treats the transitoriness of man, with particular attention to the worldly rich (vs. 5–13); and then the consolation to be gained from the ultimate end of the righteous, which is eternal life, as contrasted with that of the wicked (vs. 14–20). Ps. 49 is recited in the modern orthodox Jewish home during the week of mourning following a death in the family.
On the superscription see pp. 617, 627.

1.zh:
（可拉後裔的詩，交與伶長。）萬民哪，你們都當聽這話！世上一切的居民，

**萬民啊。**本詩所要討論的問題值得全人類關注。
1-4節是嚴肅而正式的訓誨性前言（見申32:1；詩50:1；賽1:2；彌1:2）。
**世上（cheled）。**“壽命”。或各世代的世人（見詩17:14）。
1.en:
**All ye people.** The problem to be discussed merits the attention of all mankind.
Verses 1–4 constitute an introductory exhortation, solemn and formal (see Deut. 32:1; Ps. 50:1; Isa. 1:2; Micah 1:2).
**World.** Heb. cheled, “duration of life.” Cheled is also used to designate “the world” as composed of the passing generations of men (see Ps. 17:14).

2.zh:
無論上流下流，富足貧窮，都當留心聽！

**無論上流下流。**直譯是“普通人（'adam）的後代和偉人（'ish）的後代”（見詩4:2；8:4註釋）。本詩教訓卑微人不要嫉妒或者懼怕有錢人，還教訓富人不要依靠自己的財富，濫用財富，欺壓窮人。這樣，富人得到了警告，窮人得到了安慰。
2.en: **Low and high.** Literally, “sons of ordinary men [Heb. ’adam] and sons of great men [Heb. ’ish]” (see on Ps. 4:2; Ps. 8:4). The psalm teaches the humble not to envy or to fear the rich, and the rich not to trust in their riches or to use them unjustly to lord it over the poor. Thus the rich are warned and the poor consoled.

3.zh:
我口要說智慧的言語；我心要想通達的道理。

原文的“智慧”和“通達”都是複數的，表達了這些品質的不同側面。關於“智慧”和“明白”的定義，見箴1:2註釋。
3.en: **Wisdom.** In the Hebrew the words for both “wisdom” and “understanding” are in the plural, calling attention to the varied aspects of these qualifications. See on Prov. 1:2 for definitions of “wisdom” and “understanding.”

4.zh:
我要側耳聽比喻，用琴解謎語。

**比喻（mashal）。**還有“格言”，“詩歌”之意（見本書945頁）。
**琴。**即“里拉琴”（見第34頁）。思想感情往往通過音樂存在人的腦海裡。“沒有什麼方法能比唱詩更有效地把上帝的話留在記憶之中”（《教育論》第167頁）。
4.en:
**Parable.** Heb. mashal, “similitude,” “proverb,” “song,” or “poem” (see p. 945).
**Dark saying.** Or, “riddle,” a point so obscure as to need untangling.
**Harp.** Better, “a lyre” (see p. 34). Sentiments worthy of retention are often best stored in the mind when set to music. “There are few means more effective for fixing His [God’s] words in the memory than repeating them in song” (Ed 167).

5.zh:
在患難的日子，奸惡隨我腳跟，四面環繞我，我何必懼怕？

詩人在開始討論以前，先講述自己因默想而得到的安慰。他下結論說，沒有懼怕的理由。
5.en: **Wherefore?** The psalmist puts the consoling results of his meditation first, before he proceeds with the discussion. He has concluded that he has no reason to fear.

6.zh:
那些倚仗財貨自誇錢財多的人，

**懷愛倫註釋（6–8節）**。《證言》卷二第198頁。

7.zh:
一個也無法贖自己的弟兄，也不能替他將贖價給神，

這個否定詞在希伯來語中是強調的。人無法靠自己的財產救別人脫離死亡，即使是自己的親兄弟。沒有人可以推脫自己的責任，或承擔別人的責任。
**懷愛倫註釋（7–8節）**。《服務真詮》第210頁。
7.en: **Can by any means redeem.** A denial emphatically expressed in the Hebrew. No man by his wealth can rescue another from death, not even his own brother. No man can shift his responsibility or accept another’s.

8.zh:
叫他長遠活著，不見朽壞；因為贖他生命的價值極貴，只可永遠罷休。併於上節。

**朽壞。**見詩16:10註釋。
**贖。**第8節是插入語。詩人討論的主題是個人得贖脫離死亡。
**他生命。**就是“他們自己”（見詩16:10註釋）。
**價值極貴。**財富無法救人脫離死亡。
**只可永遠罷休。**無論化多少時間，財富也不足以救人脫離墳墓。
8.en:
**Redemption.** Verse 8 is parenthetical.
**Their soul.** “They themselves” (see on Ps. 16:10). Ransom of an individual from death is the theme of the psalmist’s discussion.
**Precious.** Or, “costly.” It is beyond the power of wealth to save a man from death.
**Ceaseth for ever.** Wealth is insufficient, no matter how long it may be employed, to save one human being from the grave.

10.zh:
他必見智慧人死，又見愚頑人和畜類人一同滅亡，將他們的財貨留給別人。

**他。**有錢人（第6節）。第10節闡述了一條無據自明的自然法則。即使是智慧，也不能使人免去死亡。
**畜類人。**或“愚蠢人”。
10.en:
**He.** The wealthy man (v. 6). Verse 10 states a self-evident natural law. Not even wisdom keeps its possessor from dying.
**Brutish.** Or, “stupid.”

12.zh:
但人居尊貴中不能長久，如同死亡的畜類一樣。

**尊貴中。**或“在輝煌中”。
**不能長久。**12節是本詩的副歌。它再次出現在第20節，稍有變動。
**居（lin）。**“過夜”，不是常住。他甚至不會度過人生之“夜”，而是很快離去。
**死亡。**直譯是“安息”，或“沉默”。
12.en:
**In honour.** Or, “in splendor.”
**Abideth not.** Verse 12 is the refrain of the psalm. It appears again with variation as v. 20.
**Abideth.** Heb. lin, “to spend the night,” not remaining permanently. He will not even spend the “night” of life, but will soon pass away.
**Perish.** Literally, “are reduced to silence,” or “are brought to rest.”

13.zh:
他們行的這道本為自己的愚昧；但他們以後的人還佩服他們的話語。（細拉）

**他們以後的人。**他們的後代與父輩一樣愚蠢。
**佩服他們的話語。**直譯是“嘴上高興”。那些愚蠢的後代與他們富有的祖先一樣，說愚蠢的話。罪惡延續了下來。
**細拉。**見本書第629頁（《詩篇》序言）。
13.en:
**Their posterity.** Those who follow them are as foolish as their fathers.
**Approve their sayings.** Literally, “delight in their mouth.” These foolish descendants also take pleasure in uttering the same foolish sentiments as their wealthy ancestors. The evil is perpetuated.
**Selah.** See p. 629.

14.zh:
他們如同羊群派定下陰間；死亡必作他們的牧者。到了早晨，正直人必管轄他們；他們的美容必被陰間所滅，以致無處可存。

**陰間（she'ol）。**見箴15:11註釋。
**必作……牧者（ra`ah）。**或“餵養羊群”，“履行牧人的職責”。不是說死亡吃了他們，乃是說死亡將成為他們的牧人。
**美容。**肉體化為塵灰。
14.en:
**Grave.** Heb. she’ol (see on Prov. 15:11).
**Shall feed on.** Heb. ra‘ah, “to feed a flock,” “to perform the function of a shepherd.” The idea is not that death shall eat them, but that death shall be their shepherd.
**Beauty.** The body crumbles to dust.

15.zh:
只是神必救贖我的靈魂脫離陰間的權柄，因他必收納我。（細拉）

**我的靈魂。**就是“我”（見詩16:10註釋）。
**陰間的權柄。**直譯是“從陰間（she'ol）的手裡”（見箴15:11註釋）。這是生動的擬人手法。
**他必收納我。**或“祂將因自己的緣故收納我”。這句話簡短而有力，因為它提示了來生和復活的道理（見《先知與君王》第264頁）。在創5:24裡，該動詞的另一種形態，描述了以諾的昇天（見創5:24；王下2:10）。
**細拉。**見本書第629頁（《詩篇》序言）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先知與君王》第264頁。
15.en:
**My soul.** “Me” (see on Ps. 16:10).
**From the power of the grave.** Literally, “from the hand of she’ol” (see on Prov. 15:11), a vivid personification.
**He shall receive me.** Better, “He shall receive me for Himself.” In this short clause, all the more powerful because of its brevity, is a suggestion of the doctrine of a future life and the resurrection from the dead (see PK 264). In Gen. 5:24 another form of the same verb describes the translation of Enoch (see 2 Kings 2:10).
**Selah.** See p. 629.

16.zh:
見人發財、家室增榮的時候，你不要懼怕；

**不要懼怕。**詩人從鼓勵自己，轉到鼓勵他人。
**增榮。**指財富所帶來的奢侈。
16.en:
**Be not thou afraid.** The psalmist turns from encouraging himself to encouraging others.
**Glory.** This may be thought of as the sumptuousness that wealth provides.

17.zh:
因為，他死的時候什麼也不能帶去；他的榮耀不能隨他下去。

**什麼也不能帶去。**見伯1:21；傳5:15；路12:20；提前6:7。
**榮耀。**見第16節註釋。富人的財產不能帶到墳墓裡去。雖然許多民族有用財產殉葬的習慣，但是肉體還是要回歸塵土。
17.en:
**Carry nothing away.** See Job 1:21; Eccl. 5:15; Luke 12:20; 1 Tim. 6:7.
**Glory.** See on v. 16. The rich man’s wealth cannot go down to the grave with him. Despite the custom of many peoples of burying wealth with the deceased, the body returns to the dust.

18.zh:
他活著的時候，雖然自誇為有福（你若利己，人必誇獎你）；

**自誇為有福。**指富人誇耀自己積蓄財富的聰明（見申29:19；路12:19）。
**人必誇獎你。**許多人喜歡稱讚別人積蓄財富。積蓄是人類普遍的慾望。這種稱讚並不是最後成功的證據。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督比喻實訓》第258頁。
18.en:
**Blessed his soul.** The picture is that of a rich man complimenting himself on his sagacity in amassing his fortune (see Deut. 29:19; Luke 12:19).
**Men will praise thee.** Many are ready to praise a man for accumulating that which is the universal desire among men. This general acclaim is no proof of ultimate success.

19.zh:
他仍必歸到他歷代的祖宗那裡，永不見光。

**他仍必歸。**指惡人。他們是本詩的主要對象。
**永不見光。**富裕的罪人和他們的先輩決不會再去光顧他們驕傲和自滿的源泉（見伯33:30）。
19.en:
**He shall go.** That is, the unrighteous man, who is the subject of the psalm.
**Shall never see light.** The rich sinner and his progenitors will never again look upon the things that were to them the source of their pride and self-congratulation (see Job 33:30).

20.zh:
人在尊貴中而不醒悟，就如死亡的畜類一樣。

本節重複了12節的副歌，稍有變動。12節是“不能長久”，而本節則是“不醒悟”。在七十士譯本里，這兩節都用“醒悟”。在原文中，這兩處只有一個字母之別。根據第12節，一般的人就像死亡的畜類一樣；根據本節的含義，如果沒有真智慧，人死亡就像畜類一樣。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督比喻實訓》第258頁；《傳道良助》第18頁；《證言》卷四第526頁。
20.en: **Like the beasts.** The refrain of v. 12 is repeated, with slight alterations. Instead of “abideth not,” this verse has “understandeth not,” although a number of Hebrew manuscripts read “abideth not” here also. The LXX has “understands not” in both instances. In Hebrew there is a difference of only one letter between the two readings. According to v. 12, men in general are like beasts that perish; according to this verse, men perish like brutes only if they do not have the true wisdom.

7.en: **Harp.** Heb. kinnor, lyre (see p. 34).
7.zh:
你們要以感謝向耶和華歌唱，用琴向我們的神歌頌。

**琴（kinnor）。**里拉。見本冊註釋第34頁。

8.en: **Who prepareth rain.** All growing things are dependent upon God for rain, sunshine, and life itself (see Ed 104).
8.zh:
他用雲遮天，為地降雨，使草生長在山上。

一切生物的成長都有賴於上帝所賜的雨露，陽光和生命本身（見《教育論》第104頁）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督教育之研究》第185頁；《醫療佈道論》第7頁；《先祖與先知》第115頁。

0.zh: 序言——這是第二首哈利路亞詩歌。詩人為上帝對待選民的恩慈，和祂賜給地球的福氣而讚美祂。本詩分成三段，每段均以呼籲新的讚美開始。由於上帝是整個大自然的醫治者，供應者和管理者，詩人呼籲全宇宙讚美耶和華。關於本詩的作者，見《基督教育原理》第371頁。
0.en: INTRODUCTION.—Ps. 147 is the second of the Hallelujah psalms. The psalmist ascribes praise to God for His goodness to His chosen people and for His blessings to the earth. The psalm consists of three divisions, each beginning with a call to renewed praise. Since God is healer, restorer, provider, and controller of all nature, the psalmist calls for universal praise. On the authorship of this psalm see FE 371.

1.zh:
你們要讚美耶和華！因歌頌我們的神為善為美；讚美的話是合宜的。

見詩33:1註釋。上帝如此恩待人類，人類理應感謝讚美上帝。然而在自稱為基督徒的人中，只有極少數人表現出真誠的感謝。
1.en: **Praise is comely.** See on Ps. 33:1. Nothing is more appropriate than for man, who owes so much to God, to show gratitude to the Lord. And yet how few, even among the professed followers of Jesus, show true gratitude.

3.zh:
他醫好傷心的人，裹好他們的傷處。

上帝是心靈的大醫師。祂知道人心中的每一點痛苦。“凡是有關我們平安的事，祂絕不會認為太小而不與關注”（《喜樂的泉源》第77頁）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第329頁；《先知與君王》第668頁；《拾級就主》第105頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（3–4節）**。《服務真詮》第71頁；《今日的生活》第297頁；《論節制》第120頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（3–7節）**。《基督教育之研究》第371頁。
3.en: **Healeth.** God is the Great Physician of the soul and is touched by every pang that rends the heart. “Nothing that in any way concerns our peace is too small for Him to notice” (SC 105).

4.zh:
他數點星宿的數目，一一稱他的名。

**數點。**指統計天體。現代天文學的巨大進展使人認識到，即使宇宙存在界限，人類也無法測透。更新更大倍數的望遠鏡雖然能夠觀察到更加遙遠的太空，所發現的只能是更多的星星和星系。
**數目。**見第5註釋。上帝管理無數的星星，引導並保持它們在各自的位置上，這需要多大的智慧和能力啊！
**名。**見賽40:26。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第329頁。
4.en:
**Telleth.** Rather, “counts,” or, “enumerates,” the heavenly bodies. The great advances of modern astronomy reveal the futility of man’s ever being able to penetrate to the limits of the universe, if, indeed, such there be. New and larger telescopes capable of reaching farther into space reveal only more stars and systems.
**The number.** See on v. 5. What wisdom and power are displayed in marshaling the countless hosts of stars and in guiding and keeping them in their particular spheres.
**Names.** See Isa. 40:26.

5.zh:
我們的主為大，最有能力；他的智慧無法測度。

**無法測度（'en mispar）。**Mispar 在第4節譯為“數目”。有關上帝的知識是深不可測的。人的認識是有限的，無法測透上帝的智慧。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《服務真詮》第433頁；《證言》卷八第282頁                         【 SDA3.1155】。
5.en: **Infinite.** Heb. ’en mispar, “without number.” Mispar is translated “number” in v. 4. It is impossible to calculate the unfathomable depth of God’s knowledge. There is a limit to human knowledge, but there is no searching out of God’s understanding.

6.zh:
耶和華扶持謙卑人，將惡人傾覆於地。

控制著強大的恆星在各自軌道上運行的上帝，竟願扶持謙卑的人。這是多大的屈尊啊！
6.en: **Lifteth up the meek.** He who controls the mighty suns in their orbits stoops to sustain those who are of a humble spirit. What condescension!

9.zh:
他賜食給走獸和啼叫的小烏鴉。

參太6:26；路12:6,7。
9.en: **Young ravens.** Compare Matt. 6:26; Luke 12:6, 7.

10.zh:
他不喜悅馬的力大，不喜愛人的腿快。

與周圍的外邦國家不同，以色列人在戰爭中不依靠兵馬和戰車（見申17:16註釋）。上帝有無數方法可以實施祂的計劃，不需要依靠受造者的幫助。
10.en: **Strength of the horse.** In contrast with the heathen nations around, Israel was not to depend on horses or chariots in warfare (see on Deut. 17:16). The Lord has a thousand ways of accomplishing His plans and does not need to depend on any of His creatures to assist Him.

11.zh:
耶和華喜愛敬畏他和盼望他慈愛的人。

見詩19:9；箴1:7註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋（11–12節）**。《基督教育之研究》第371頁。
11.en: **Fear him.** See on Ps. 19:9; Prov. 1:7.

13.zh:
因為他堅固了你的門閂，賜福給你中間的兒女。

上帝的保護是最好的國防。否則其他的防護都是徒然的（見詩127:1）。
13.en: **He hath strengthened.** God’s protection is the best defense of any country. Without it other defenses are vain (see Ps. 127:1).

14.zh:
他使你境內平安，用上好的麥子使你滿足。

**你境內。**從軍事角度來看，前沿城鎮是最容易受到攻擊的。如果邊界平安，全國就平安。
**上好的麥子。**即“飽滿的麥子”。上帝願意賜給祂的子民最好的屬靈福分和物質福分。
14.en:
**In thy borders.** From a military standpoint the frontier towns lie most exposed. If there is peace on the perimeter of a territory, there is usually peace throughout the land.
**The finest of the wheat.** Literally, “the fat of the wheat,” meaning “choice wheat.” God desires to give His people the choice material blessings as well as spiritual.

15.zh:
他發命在地；他的話頒行最快。

地和住在地上的，都要服從上帝的命令。
15.en: **His commandment.** The earth, as well as those who dwell therein, is subject to the commands of God.

16.zh:
他降雪如羊毛，撒霜如爐灰。

**懷愛倫註釋**。《服務真詮》第416頁；《先祖與先知》第115頁；《證言》卷八第270頁。

17.zh:
他擲下冰雹如碎渣；他發出寒冷，誰能當得起呢？

**碎渣（pittim）。**比喻冰雹。
17.en: **Morsels.** Heb. pittim, here used metaphorically of hail.

19.zh:
他將他的道指示雅各，將他的律例典章指示以色列。

**指示（nagad）。**即“把一件事情明顯地擺在一個人的面前”。
19.en: **Sheweth.** Heb. nagad. The form used here means “to place a matter conspicuously before a person.”

20.zh:
別國他都沒有這樣待過；至於他的典章，他們向來沒有知道。你們要讚美耶和華！

**沒有這樣待過。**參羅9:4,5。
**你們要讚美耶和華。**“哈利路亞”（見詩146:1註釋）。
20.en:
**Not dealt so.** Compare Rom. 9:4, 5.
**Praise ye the Lord.** The psalm concludes with a “hallelujah” (see on Ps. 146:1).

5.en:
**Than the angels.** Heb. me’elohim, literally, “than God.” The Targums, the LXX, the Syriac, and the quotation of this verse in Heb. 2:7 read “angels” instead of “God.” However, the Greek versions of Aquila, Symmachus, and Theodotion, as well as the Vulgate, retain the translation “God.” It has been supposed that ’Elohim may be applied to men or angels (see Ex. 21:6; Ps. 82:1; Vol. I, p. 171). Gesenius renders the text: “Thou hast caused him to want but little of God,” that is, “thou hast made him but little lower than God” (see Gen. 1:26). Whether we read “than the angels” (see GC 511) or “than God,” man is shown to be on a much higher level than the animal kingdom, because of his kinship with God. Nevertheless, at his best, finite man is far inferior to the infinite God. See further on Heb. 2:7.
**Glory and honour.** As king and ruler of the earth, man partakes of the attributes of God (see Ps. 29:1; 104:1; 145:5), who is king of the universe.
5.zh:
你叫他比天使（或譯：神）微小一點，並賜他榮耀尊貴為冠冕。

**比天使（me'elohim）。**直譯是“比上帝”。塔古姆譯本，七十士譯本，敘利亞譯本，以及來2:7的引言都是“天使”，而不是“上帝”。但亞居拉譯本，辛馬庫譯本和狄奧多田譯本等希臘譯本，以及武加大譯本都譯為“上帝”。據說'Elohim既能指人也能指天使（見出21:6；詩82:1；本註釋卷一171頁）。格塞紐把這句譯為“你叫他比上帝缺一點”，即“低一點”（見創1:26）。不論是“比天使”（見《善惡之爭》第511頁），還是“比上帝”，人比動物都要高貴得多，因為他是上帝的兒女。然而有限的人類比無限的上帝還是要低得多。詳見來2:7註釋。
**榮耀尊貴。**身為地球的君王和統治者，人類與宇宙大君上帝的性情有份（見詩29:1；104:1；145:5）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《善惡之爭》第511頁；《證言》卷三第50,568頁；《證言》卷四第416頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（5–6節）**。《先祖與先知》第50頁。

4.en:
**What is man?** “Man” is from the Heb. ’enosh, which designates man in his frailty and weakness. When one stands in the presence of the vastness, the mystery, the glory of the heavens as seen at night, and begins to reflect upon the infinity of space and the countlessness of the heavenly bodies, he must feel that man is an insignificantly small dot in the universe. If this is the reaction of ordinary unschooled mortals, how much truer must it be of the one who looks upon the heavens with the aid of the modern telescope, in the light of the steadily unfolding knowledge of modern astronomy.
**Son of man.** Heb. ben–’adam, probably emphasizing man’s earthly nature as formed from the ground (see on Gen. 1:26; 2:7).
**Visitest.** Heb. paqad, a word describing not only the act of visiting but also what the visitor accomplishes by his visit. Hence here the word indicates God’s care of the human being, His favor and attention shown toward man (see Gen. 21:1). Why should the infinite God, who has a universe of worlds to claim His attention, be “mindful” of finite man? Why should He honor man by making him viceroy of the earth? Only in the realization of the worth of a human soul created in God’s likeness can one answer these questions. This realization comes only in appreciation of the Saviour’s death on the cross. “The worth of man is known only by going to Calvary. In the mystery of the cross of Christ we can place an estimate upon man” (2T 634, 635).
Important as the revelation of God in external nature may be, the revelation of God in human life is more important. Size and extent are no criteria of value. It has been said that the eye and brain that see the physical heavens are more wonderful than the heavens that are seen through the most powerful telescope.
4.zh:
便說：人算什麼，你竟顧念他？世人算什麼，你竟眷顧他？

人算什麼？“人”，源於希伯來詞'enosh，意為“脆弱”。當人在夜間觀察宇宙的廣袤，威嚴和榮耀，思考無垠的太空和無數的天體時，他會感到人類只是滄海一粟。人憑肉眼觀察就有這樣的反應，更何況藉助現代望遠鏡觀察天空，並擁有越來越多的現代天文學知識。
**世人（ben-'adam）。**可能強調人是用泥土所造的（見創1:26；2:7註釋）。
**眷顧（paqad）。**其內涵包括具體的內容。所以這裡是指上帝對人類的眷顧和關愛（見創21:1）。無窮的上帝需要看顧如此龐大的宇宙，為什麼還要“眷顧”人類？為什麼還要使人類管理地球？只有理解按上帝的形象所創造的人類生命的價值，才能回答這些問題。而要有這樣的理解，就必須先理解救主在十字架上的受死。“人類的價值只有來到髑髏地才能明白。只有在基督十字架的奧秘中，我們才能對人作出評價”（《證言》卷二634,635頁）。
上帝在大自然的啟示固然重要，但祂對人生的啟示更加重要。規模和大小不是價值的標準。據說人的肉眼和思維所觀察的天空，要比最大功率的望遠鏡所觀察到的更加奇妙。

0.zh:
序言——這是第一篇有關大自然的詩歌（見《詩篇》19,29,104篇等），啟示上帝在大自然和人類生活中的威嚴。這首詩被稱為星空之歌是很恰當的。它證明希伯來語詩人所關注的不但是大自然本身，而是透過大自然看到大自然的上帝。這首詩又稱為“人類尊嚴的讚歌”。在詩歌裡，詩人站在廣闊無邊，朗月照耀，星光點綴的穹蒼之下，注視上帝在大自然中的手跡，深感驚愕。在無垠的宇宙之中，他突然意識到人類的渺小。人一旦有了這種感覺，就真正體驗到做人的尊嚴，因為作為上帝在地上的代表，他在自然界的地位只是略低於上帝；萬物都臣服在他的腳下。怪不得詩人如此感嘆人類在宇宙中的尊貴地位，崇揚他創造主的偉大。本詩展現了“信封結構”這種修辭方式的魅力。其首句和末句是一樣的（第1,9節；參詩103，104篇），中間部分需按這種“信封結構”的理念來解釋。
儘管我們不知道本詩的創作背景，但不難想象大衛是在牧羊生活初期的某一個夜裡寫下這一首優美的抒情詩。那時他與羊群單獨相處，抬頭仰望星空，深感自己作為創造主兒女的尊貴；也可能是他到了晚年，回顧早年生活的歡樂而寫下了這首詩。
關於題記，見本書616,629頁（《詩篇》序言）。
大衛的詩，交與伶長。用迦特樂器。
0.en:
INTRODUCTION.—This psalm is the first of the nature psalms (see Ps. 19, 29, 104, etc.), and is a revelation of God’s majesty in nature and in human life. This Song of the Starry Night, as the poem has appropriately been termed, is witness to the fact that the Hebrew poet did not see nature as an end in itself, but always looked beyond nature to nature’s God. The psalm has also been called A Psalm in Praise of the Dignity of Man. In it the poet stands under the open canopy of the moonlit and star-studded sky, awe-struck by his contemplation of God’s handiwork in nature. In the presence of all this vastness, there comes upon him a sudden realization of the insignificance of puny man.
