**Was still.** The earth appeared to be silent, reverently listening to the voice of God pronouncing judgment (see Ps. 114:3–7).

10.zh:
人的忿怒要成全你的榮美；人的餘怒，你要禁止。

**成全你的榮美。**人的罪惡使上帝有機會表現祂的大作為。人類對上帝的敵意，給上帝提供機會顯示祂的大能，使祂得到讚美（見出9:16；18:11）。
**禁止。**直譯是“你要穿戴”。本節平行的兩句說明，上帝利用軟弱之人孤注一擲的失敗，來增進自己的榮耀。但以理的經歷就是這條原則運用的範例（見《先知與君王》第543,544頁）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先知與君王》第543頁；《證言》卷五第453頁。
10.en:
**Shall praise thee.** The wickedness of man gives occasion for great deeds on God’s part. Man’s hostility to God gives opportunity for the display of God’s power that brings praise to Him (see Ex. 9:16; 18:11).
**Restrain.** Literally, “thou wilt gird.” The parallelism of the two clauses in the verse indicates that God puts on, as an ornament, the last powerless efforts of feeble man to assert his own strength, clothing Himself thus to His own glory. The experience of Daniel is a notable example of the operation of this principle (see PK 543, 544).

11.zh:
你們許願，當向耶和華─你們的神還願；在他四面的人都當拿貢物獻給那可畏的主。

**許願。**詩人對上帝的子民說話（見詩22:25）。
**拿貢物。**我們的禮物有時表達我們的感恩程度。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷四第471頁                                         【 SDA3.1149】。
11.en:
**Vow.** The poet addresses God’s people (see Ps. 22:25).
**Bring presents.** Our measure of gratitude is sometimes shown in our gifts.

12.zh:
他要挫折王子的驕氣；他向地上的君王顯威可畏。

**他要挫折。**上帝要挫掉他們的傲氣，就是本詩所慶祝的上帝的作為。“挫折”指葡萄工的工作：修剪枝子，割下葡萄串（見賽18:5）。
**驕氣（ruach）。**直譯是“風”（見傳12:7註釋）。
**君王。**上帝要按照自己的美意，挫敗君王和王子們的計劃。參啟6:15-17；19:17-21。
12.en:
**He shall cut off.** God will cut down their pride, referring to what He had done as celebrated in this psalm. “Cut off” suggests the work of a vinedresser, pruning the vines or cutting off the clusters of grapes (see Isa. 18:5).
**Spirit.** Heb. ruach, literally, “wind” (see on Eccl. 12:7).
**Kings.** God defeats the plans of kings as well as of princes when His good pleasure dictates. The psalm closes with an expression of the finality of God’s dealing with evil men. Compare Rev. 6:15–17; 19:17–21.

76.9:
**When God arose.** See Ps. 3:7; 7:6; 44:26; 68:1.
**Selah.** See p. 629.

0.zh:
序言——這是一首悲歌，悲嘆耶路撒冷被巴比倫人征服時期的荒涼（見詩74篇）。本詩一開始描寫耶路撒冷成為廢墟，居民死於刀下，然後祈求拯救和懲罰侵略者，最後是讚美和永遠感恩的承諾。本詩的詩節並不規則，但語言流暢，特別受法國胡格諾派和英國清教徒所喜愛。
關於本詩的題記，見詩74篇序言；又見本冊註釋第617,627頁（《詩篇》序言）。
亞薩的詩。
0.en:
INTRODUCTION.—Ps. 79 is an elegy on the desolation of Jerusalem at the time of the Babylonian captivity (see Ps. 74). It begins with a graphic description of Jerusalem in ruins and her inhabitants put to the sword, proceeds with prayer for deliverance and the meting out of justice upon the invaders, and closes with a song of praise and promise of eternal gratitude. The psalm, while irregular in stanzaic form, flows smoothly throughout in thought. It was a favorite of the French Huguenots and of the English Puritans.
On the superscription see Introduction to Ps. 74; also pp. 617, 627.

1.zh:
（亞薩的詩。）神啊，外邦人進入你的產業，汙穢你的聖殿，使耶路撒冷變成荒堆，

**外邦人。**或“各國”（見詩2:1註釋）。第1-4節形象地悲嘆臨到以色列的可怕災害。
**產業。**見詩28:9；74:2；78:62。
**汙穢。**巴比倫人闖到裡面，盜竊聖物，毀壞設施，放火焚燒：玷汙了聖殿（見代下36:17,18；耶52:17-23；比較詩74:4-7）。
**變成荒堆。**見代下36:19；耶9:11；26:18；彌3:12。
1.en:
**Heathen.** Or, “nations” (see on Ps. 2:1). Verses 1–4 graphically lament the terrible calamities that have come upon Israel.
**Inheritance.** See Ps. 28:9; 74:2; 78:62.
**Have they defiled.** By breaking into it, stealing the sacred furniture, demolishing its appointments, setting fire to it, the Babylonians had polluted the Temple (see 2 Chron. 36:17, 18; Jer. 52:17–23; cf. Ps. 74:4–7).
**On heaps.** See 2 Chron. 36:19; Jer. 9:11; 26:18; Micah 3:12.

2.zh:
把你僕人的屍首交與天空的飛鳥為食，把你聖民的肉交與地上的野獸，

本節描寫迦勒底人攻佔耶路撒冷時的可怕屠殺。橫屍遍野，無法埋葬，成為野獸和禿鷲的食物（見代下36:17；參申28:26；耶7:33；8:2；9:22等）。
2.en: **Dead bodies.** This verse describes the horrible slaughter when Jerusalem was taken by the Chaldeans. The dead were left unburied, food for wild animals and vultures (see 2 Chron. 36:17; cf. Deut. 28:26; Jer. 7:33; 8:2; 9:22; etc.).

3.zh:
在耶路撒冷周圍流他們的血如水，無人葬埋。

見耶14:16。古人視沒有受到體面的埋葬為巨恥大辱。即使是判處死刑的罪犯，也要得到適當的掩埋（見申21:23）。
3.en: **None to bury.** See Jer. 14:16. To the ancients, not to be accorded honorable burial was considered a great ignominy. Even executed criminals were required to be buried decently (see Deut. 21:23).

4.zh:
我們成為鄰國的羞辱，成為我們四圍人的嗤笑譏刺。

**鄰國。**見第12節註釋。
4.en: **Neighbours.** See on v. 12.

5.zh:
耶和華啊，這到幾時呢？你要動怒到永遠嗎？你的憤恨要如火焚燒嗎？

到幾時呢？參詩74:1,10；77:7-9；89:46。
憤怒。見詩78:58註釋。
5.en:
**How long?** Compare Ps. 74:1, 10; 77:7–9; 89:46.
**Jealousy.** See on Ps. 78:58.

6.zh:
願你將你的忿怒倒在那不認識你的外邦和那不求告你名的國度。

**倒。**把6,7節與耶10:25進行比較，二者非常相似。
**不認識。**或“不承認”。上帝對所有的國家都給予一定的啟示（見羅1:18-25；2:14-16）。
6.en:
**Pour out.** With vs. 6, 7 compare Jer. 10:25, which is strikingly similar.
**Have not known.** Perhaps better, “did not acknowledge.” All nations have been given a degree of divine revelation (see Rom. 1:18–25; 2:14–16).

8.zh:
求你不要記念我們先祖的罪孽，向我們追討；願你的慈悲快迎著我們，因為我們落到極卑微的地步。

**我們先祖的罪孽。**祈求上帝不要讓他們承擔他們的祖先犯罪的後果（見出20:5；哀5:7）。
**迎著。**見詩18:5註釋；參詩59:10。
8.en:
**Former iniquities.** Or, “the iniquities of them that were before us.” The prayer is that God will not allow them to suffer the results of the sins of their forefathers (see Ex. 20:5; Lam. 5:7).
**Prevent.** See on Ps. 18:5; cf. Ps. 59:10.

9.zh:
拯救我們的神啊，求你因你名的榮耀幫助我們！為你名的緣故搭救我們，赦免我們的罪。

**拯救我們的上帝啊。**詩人相信上帝拯救的大能。
**你名的榮耀。**求上帝幫助以色列，不是為以色列的緣故，因為她不配，而是為了祂的榮耀（見出32:12）。本節兩次呼求上帝的名（見詩5:11；7:17）。
**赦免（kaphar）。**通常譯為“贖”（見出30:15）。
9.en:
**God of our salvation.** The psalmist has faith in God’s power to save.
**Glory of thy name.** God is asked to come to Israel’s help, not for Israel’s sake—she is undeserving—but for His own glory (see Ex. 32:12). Twice in this verse, appeal is made to God’s name (see Ps. 5:11; 7:17).
**Purge away.** Heb. kaphar, generally translated, “make atonement” (see Ex. 30:15).

10.zh:
為何容外邦人說他們的神在哪裡呢？願你使外邦人知道你在我們眼前伸你僕人流血的冤。

為何？在古代，戰勝一個外國就被視為戰勝他們的神。詩人渴望上帝證明自己的大能。摩西少有兩次發出過類似的請求（出32:12；民14:13-19）。
**外邦人。**各國（見詩2:1；9:5註釋）。
**願你使外邦人知道。**詩人求上帝懲罰那些流上帝僕人之血的邪惡國家。
10.en:
**Wherefore?** In antiquity, victory over a foreign power was considered triumph over its gods. The psalmist is jealous for the vindication of God’s power. Moses made a similar plea on at least two occasions (Ex. 32:12; Num. 14:13–19).
**The heathen.** Nations (see on Ps. 2:1; 9:5).
**Let him be known.** The psalmist pleads that God’s judgment may come upon the wicked nations that have shed the blood of His servants.

11.zh:
願被囚之人的歎息達到你面前；願你按你的大能力存留那些將要死的人。

**嘆息。**指以色列人俘虜的呻吟（見詩137:1-6；哀1:3-5）。
**將要死的人。**直譯是“死亡之子”（見詩102:20）。
11.en:
**Sighing.** The reference is to the groaning of the Hebrews in captivity (see Ps. 137:1–6; Lam. 1:3–5).
**Appointed to die.** Literally, “children of death” (see Ps. 102:20).

12.zh:
主啊，願你將我們鄰邦所羞辱你的羞辱加七倍歸到他們身上。

**鄰邦。**以色列周圍的國家幸災樂禍，不願意幫助以色列人抵抗侵略者（見第4節註釋；參詩44:13；但9:16）。
**七倍。**指完全的報應。“七”象徵完全（見創4:15,24；詩12:6；太18:21,22）。
12.en:
**Neighbours.** The nations surrounding Israel, who gloried in Israel’s misfortune rather than attempting to help her against the invader (see on v. 4; cf. Ps. 44:13; Dan. 9:16).
**Sevenfold.** The idea is that of complete vengeance, seven being a symbol of completeness (see Gen. 4:15, 24; Ps. 12:6; Matt. 18:21, 22).

13.zh:
這樣，你的民，你草場的羊，要稱謝你，直到永遠；要述說讚美你的話，直到萬代。

**你草場的羊。**見詩74:1註釋；參詩78:52。
**述說。**以色列位於通往各國的大道上，應成為世上的光（見賽43:21）。
**直到萬代。**作者承諾世世代代用讚美的話傳揚上帝的慈愛。
13.en:
**Sheep of thy pasture.** See on Ps. 74:1; cf. Ps. 78:52.
**Shew forth.** Israel, situated as she was on the “highway of the nations,” was to be the light of the world (see Isa. 43:21).
**To all generations.** In a paean of praise, the poet promises to pass on to succeeding generations the story of God’s goodness.

0.zh:
序言——這是一首節日讚歌，可能是為一個重大的希伯來節日而寫的。也許是逾越節或住棚節。一開始是歡樂地呼喚參加節日的崇拜（第1-5節），接著通過回顧過去上帝與以色列的關係來說明節日的重要性，勸勉祂的子民要行在祂的道中（第6-16節）。本詩的第一部分是詩人說話。第二部分是上帝對祂的子民說話，鑑於過去的福惠，要求他們順從，並應許將來的福氣，作為順從的結果。在現代猶太教堂的儀式裡，本詩吟唱於猶太人的元旦。
關於本詩的題記，見本冊註釋第617,629頁（《詩篇》序言）。
亞薩的詩，交與伶長。用迦特樂器。
0.en:
INTRODUCTION.—Ps. 81 is a festal hymn presumably composed for use at one of the great Hebrew festivals—probably the Passover or the Feast of Tabernacles. It begins with a joyful summons to join in the worship of the festival (vs. 1–5), and then proceeds to present the significance of the festival by reviewing God’s relationship to Israel in the past and expostulating with His people, urging them to walk in His ways (vs. 6–16). In the first part of the psalm, the psalmist speaks; in the second part, God addresses the people and claims obedience in the light of past blessings, and promises future blessings as the result of obedience. In modern synagogue ritual Ps. 81 is sung on the Jewish New Year’s Day.
On the superscription see pp. 617, 629.

1.zh:
（亞薩的詩，交與伶長。用迦特樂器。）你們當向神─我們的力量大聲歡呼，向雅各的神發聲歡樂！

**大聲歡呼。**顯示非常誠懇（見代下20:19；詩33:3）。1-5節是崇拜的呼喚。
**力量。**見詩27:1；28:8。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–2節）**。《證言》卷八第12頁。
1.en:
**Sing aloud.** Indicating great earnestness and sincerity (see 2 Chron. 20:19; Ps. 33:3). Ps. 81:1–5 is a summons to worship.
**Strength.** See Ps. 27:1; 28:8.

2.zh:
唱起詩歌，打手鼓，彈美琴與瑟。

**手鼓。**見本冊註釋30頁。
**琴。**見本冊註釋34頁。
**瑟。**見本冊註釋33頁。
2.en:
**Timbrel.** Possibly a drum (see p. 30).
**Harp.** See p. 34.
**Psaltery.** See p. 33.

3.zh:
當在月朔並月望─我們過節的日期吹角，

角（shophar）與chasoserah不同，又譯為“號”（見本冊註釋39,40頁）。
**月朔。**見利23:24；民29:1。
**月望（keseh）。**“滿月”。
**過節的日期。**有人認為是指住棚節（見王上8:2,65；12:32；尼8:14；代下5:3；7:8）。在提市黎月一日的吹角節和提市黎月十五日開始的住棚節之間，該月十日是贖罪日。這一系列節日使住棚節成為主要的年度節日。也有的註釋家認為這裡的節日是指逾越節，因為其在宗教年曆中的重要地位。
3.en:
**Trumpet.** Heb. shophar, as distinct from chaṣoṣerah, also translated “trumpet” (see pp. 39, 40).
**New moon.** See Lev. 23:24; Num. 29:1.
**Time appointed.** Heb. keseh, “full moon.”
**Solemn feast.** Some think the Feast of Tabernacles is referred to (see 1 Kings 8:2, 65; 12:32; Neh. 8:14; 2 Chron. 5:3; 7:8). Between the Feast of Trumpets, on the first of Tishri, and the Feast of Tabernacles, which began on the 15th of Tishri, came the Day of Atonement on the 10th day of the month. This order of festivals made Tabernacles the chief annual feast. According to some commentators, the Passover is intended by the expression “our solemn feast day,” owing to the position accorded the Passover in the ritual calendar.

4.zh:
因這是為以色列定的律例，是雅各神的典章。

應當歡樂地守節，因為節日是上帝所設立的，也是上帝子民的特權（見利23:23-25）。
4.en: **For.** The festivals should be joyfully kept because God appointed them, and because they are considered a special privilege of the people of God (see Lev. 23:23–25).

5.zh:
他去攻擊埃及地的時候，在約瑟中間立此為證。我在那裡聽見我所不明白的言語：

**約瑟。**約瑟作為以色列民族代表，可能是由於在埃及期間他的重要地位（見詩80:1；參創49:26）。他被視為同胞的拯救者。
**攻擊埃及地。**可能是指出埃及時期和十大災難，特別是導致以色列人得到解放的第十災。
**我在那裡聽見。**本句的開頭可能與下一節有關，以引出6-16節上帝的勸勉。沒有說明改變了發言者。這種突然的轉換在希伯來語裡並不罕見。
5.en:
**Joseph.** The nation of Israel, represented by Joseph, probably because of his prominence during the sojourn in Egypt (see Ps. 80:1; cf. Gen. 49:26). He was, literally, the “savior” of his people.
**Through the land.** Probably referring to the time of the Exodus, and to the plagues in particular. Perhaps special reference is made to the tenth plague, which effected the release of the Israelites.
**Where I heard.** The sentence beginning with this phrase should probably be connected with the following verse, and thus introduce God’s speech of expostulation which occupies vs. 6–16. There is no verbal indication of change of speakers. Such abrupt transitions are not uncommon in Hebrew.

6.zh:
神說：我使你的肩得脫重擔，你的手放下筐子。

**重擔。**埃及的奴隸往往肩負重擔。上帝把希伯來人從埃及救了出來，解除了他們的重擔（見出1:11-14；5:4-17）。
**筐子。**可能指奴隸所背的筐子，裡面裝造磚的泥土。
6.en:
**Burden.** Egyptian slaves often carried their burdens on the shoulder. God removed the burden of bondage by delivering the Hebrews from Egypt (see Ex. 1:11–14; 5:4–17).
**From the pots.** Or, “from the basket,” probably referring to the basket in which the slaves carried the clay which was to be made into bricks.

7.zh:
你在急難中呼求，我就搭救你；我在雷的隱密處應允你，在米利巴水那裡試驗你。（細拉）

**你在急難中呼求。**見出2:23；3:9；14:10。
**在雷的隱密處。**可能指雲柱（見出14:24）或上帝在西奈山與以色列人立約的經歷（見出19:17-19）。
**米利巴。**見出17:1-7；民20:13；參詩78:20。
**細拉。**見本冊註釋第629頁（《詩篇》序言）。
7.en:
**Thou calledst in trouble.** See Ex. 2:23; 3:9; 14:10.
**Secret place of thunder.** Perhaps a reference to the pillar of cloud (see Ex. 14:24), or to the experience at Sinai (see Ex. 19:17–19), where God entered into covenant relation with Israel.
**Meribah.** See Ex. 17:1–7; Num. 20:13; cf. Ps. 78:20.
**Selah.** See p. 629.

8.zh:
我的民哪，你當聽，我要勸戒你；以色列啊，甚願你肯聽從我。

以色列人儘管悖逆，仍是上帝的子民（見第11節）。上帝不輕易拋棄祂的子民。 想到這一點真令人快樂。
8.en: **O my people.** Even though rebellious, Israel is still God’s people (see v. 11). Blessed thought: God does not easily cast off His people.

9.zh:
在你當中，不可有別的神；外邦的神，你也不可下拜。

指十誡的第二條（見出20:4-6；申5:8-10）。
9.en: **Any strange god.** An allusion to the second commandment of the Decalogue (see Ex. 20:4–6; Deut. 5:8–10).

10.zh:
我是耶和華─你的神，曾把你從埃及地領上來；你要大大張口，我就給你充滿。

**我是。**見出20:2；參申5:6。以色列人容易忘記，所以需要經常提醒。
**你要大大張口。**上帝把以色列出埃及救出來，供給他們物質上和精神上的一切需求。上帝的恩典是多麼豐盛啊（見弗3:20）！
“你來到君王面前，
帶來了許多祈願；
因祂的恩典和大能無比豐盛，
你無須祈求更多”。
10.en:
**I am.** See Ex. 20:2; cf. Deut. 5:6. In view of Israel’s tendency to forget, this reminder was continually needed.
**Open thy mouth wide.** God redeemed Israel from Egypt, and then supplied all their needs, material and spiritual. O the opulence of the gifts of God (see Eph. 3:20)! “Thou art coming to a King, Large petitions with thee bring; For His grace and power are such, None can ever ask too much.”

11.zh:
無奈，我的民不聽我的聲音；以色列全不理我。

**我的民。**見第8節註釋。繼續討論第七節的主題。
**不聽。**見申32:15,18；詩78:10,41,56；參王下17:14；代下36:15,16；結20:8；何9:17。
**懷愛倫註釋（11–12節）**。《先祖與先知》第441頁；《證言》卷三第73頁。
11.en:
**My people.** See on v. 8. The main discourse is resumed from v. 7.
**Would not hearken.** See Deut. 32:15, 18; Ps. 78:10, 41, 56; cf. 2 Kings 17:14; 2 Chron. 36:15, 16; Eze. 20:8; Hosea 9:17.

12.zh:
我便任憑他們心裡剛硬，隨自己的計謀而行。

上帝的靈並不永遠住在人心中（見創6:3）。如果人堅持悖逆，頑固不化，上帝就任憑他們自食其果。在上帝的政權下具有道德的自由選擇權。上帝絕不強迫人的意志。祂警告人，悖逆會帶來毀滅。但祂不阻礙人的選擇（見本冊註釋440,441頁）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷三第172頁。
12.en: **I gave them up.** God’s Spirit does not always strive with men (see Gen. 6:3). When men persist in rebellion and hardness of heart, God lets them have their way and suffer the results of their choosing. God’s government is a government of free moral choice; God does not coerce the will. He warns man that disobedience brings ruin, but does not prevent man’s contrary choice (see PP 440, 441).

13.zh:
甚願我的民肯聽從我，以色列肯行我的道，

**我的民。**見第8節註釋。話題從以色列的過去轉到了現在，說明順從上帝命令的結果。
**肯聽從。**英文KJV版為“聽從了”。
**肯行。**英文KJV版為“行了”（見申5:29；32:29；賽48:18；路19:42）。
“凡口所言，凡筆所寫，
最大悲哀，莫過‘本該！’”
──約翰.格林利夫.惠蒂爾（1807-1892）《莫德.馬勒》
13.en:
**My people.** See on v. 8. The address turns from Israel of the past to Israel of the present, showing what the results of faithful obedience to God’s commands would be.
**Had hearkened.** Rather, “would hearken.”
**Had walked.** Rather, “would walk” (see Deut. 5:29; 32:29; Isa. 48:18; Luke 19:42). “For of all sad words of tongue or pen, The saddest are these: ‘It might have been!’” OHN REENLEAF HITTIER, “Maud Muller.”

14.zh:
我便速速治服他們的仇敵，反手攻擊他們的敵人。

這是對詩人時代以色列人的呼籲。懺悔和順服是從敵人手中得救的前提。
14.en: **Should soon have subdued.** Rather, “should soon subdue.” The appeal is to the Israel of the psalmist’s time. Repentance and obedience are the price of deliverance from the enemy.

15.zh:
恨耶和華的人必來投降，但他的百姓必永久長存。

**必來投降。**或“應該投降”。
**他的百姓。**即他們的民族。
15.en:
**Should have submitted.** Preferably, “should submit.”
**Their time.** That is, as a nation.

16.zh:
他也必拿上好的麥子給他們吃，又拿從磐石出的蜂蜜叫他們飽足。

**他也必拿上好的麥子給他們吃。**主語突然從“我”轉到“他”，在希伯來詩歌裡是常見的（見詩22:26）。
**上好的。**“飽滿的”（見申32:14；詩147:14）。上帝賜下祂福惠的時候，祂是選擇最好的。我們天父的慷慨，不存在任何吝嗇。
**從磐石出的蜂蜜。**最好最純的蜂蜜，被蜜蜂藏在山間磐石的僻靜處（見申32:13）。
16.en:
**He should have fed.** Rather, “He should feed.” Such sudden changes from “I” to “he” are frequent in Hebrew poetry (see Ps. 22:26).
**Finest.** Literally, “fat” (see Deut. 32:14; Ps. 147:14). When God bestows His gifts, He chooses the best. There is nothing niggardly about our Father’s generosity.
**Honey out of the rock.** The best and purest honey, stored by the bees in the rocky fastness of the mountains (see Deut. 32:13).

0.zh:
序言——上帝在本詩中斥責統治著以色列的不義法官，可能寫於司法腐敗和不公氾濫的年代。本詩歌分為三段：一，稱上帝為至高的審判者；二，上帝斥責不義的法官和司法腐敗（2-7節）；三，詩人求上帝起來審判（第8節）。本詩的教訓是所有上帝的兒女應如何相處。詩58篇與本詩主題相似，但寫法不同。研究這首簡短但含義深刻的詩歌，可參閱賽3:13-15。約沙法的經驗也可以作為研究本詩的參考（見代下19:8-11；《先知與君王》第197,198頁）。
關於本詩的題記，見本冊註釋第617,627頁（《詩篇》序言）。
亞薩的詩。
0.en:
INTRODUCTION.—Ps. 82 is God’s arraignment of the unjust judges who are bearing sway over Israel. It was probably composed at a time when there was much that was unjust and corrupt in the administration of justice. The psalm has three divisions: (1) God is introduced as Supreme Judge (v. 1); (2) God proceeds to denounce unjust judges and corrupt judgment (vs. 2–7); (3) the psalmist implores God to arise in judgment (v. 8). The psalm has lessons for all God’s children in their dealings with one another. Ps. 58, which is similar in theme but different in treatment, and Isa. 3:13–15 are of comparative value in the study of this short but impressive psalm. The experience of Jehoshaphat is also worthy of study (see 2 Chron. 19:8–11; PK 197, 198).
On the superscription see pp. 617, 627.

1.zh:
（亞薩的詩。）神站在有權力者的會中，在諸神中行審判，

**上帝（'Elohim）。**見本註釋卷一170,171頁。
**站。**即參加一個會議。
**權力者（'El）。**“上帝”（見本註釋卷一171頁）。“有權利者的會”，可以泛指以色列人（見民27:17；31:16；書22:16,17）；也可根據上下文特指審判官的會議。上帝在那裡把司法權授予審判官。
**諸神（'elohim）。**這裡可能指“審判官”，如出21:6；出22:8,9。“審判官”被稱為“'elohim”，是因為他們代表上帝的權威（見出7:1）。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–4節）**。《先知與君王》第198頁。
1.en:
**God.** Heb. ’Elohim (see Vol. I, pp. 170, 171).
**Standeth.** Or, “taketh His stand,” as in convening or joining an assembly.
**Mighty.** Heb. ’El, “God” (see Vol. I, p. 171). “The congregation of the mighty [God]” may refer to Israel in general (see Num. 27:17; 31:16; Joshua 22:16, 17), or specifically, from the context, to the assembly of magistrates, to whom God delegates the authority of administering justice.
**Gods.** Heb. ’elohim, here possibly “judges,” as ’elohim is translated in Ex. 21:6; Ex. 22:8, 9. Judges may be called ’elohim in the sense that judges are representatives of God’s sovereignty (see Ex. 7:1).

2.zh:
說：你們審判不秉公義，徇惡人的情面，要到幾時呢？（細拉）

幾時？至高的審判者上帝對以色列的審判官說話。
**徇惡人的情面。**在以色列中不允許存在徇情枉法（見利19:15；申1:17；徒10:34）。
**細拉。**見本冊註釋第629頁（《詩篇》序言）。
2.en:
**How long?** God, the Sovereign Judge, speaks to Israel’s judges.
**Accept the persons.** Showing partiality on account of circumstances or position was forbidden in Israel (see Lev. 19:15; Deut. 1:17; Acts 10:34).
**Selah.** See p. 629.

3.zh:
你們當為貧寒的人和孤兒伸冤；當為困苦和窮乏的人施行公義。

**伸冤。**參賽1:23；耶5:28。
**施行公義。**不但要傾聽他們的訴說，也要作出公正的裁決。
3.en:
**Defend.** Compare Isa. 1:23; Jer. 5:28.
**Do justice to.** Not only hear their causes, but render true justice in decisions.

4.zh:
當保護貧寒和窮乏的人，救他們脫離惡人的手。

**救他們脫離。**或“把他們奪走”。
4.en: **Rid them.** Or, “snatch them away.”

5.zh:
你們仍不知道，也不明白，在黑暗中走來走去；地的根基都搖動了。

**你們仍不知道。**本節似乎是詩人的插話，生動地說明上帝對不義法官的斥責（見詩53:4；73:22）。
**在黑暗中。**他們不願認識上帝，所以不配承擔上帝所託付執法的職責（見箴2:13；約3:19）。
**地的根基。**可能指政權道德的基本原則。
**搖動。**當不義的法官執法的時候，政權道德的基礎產生了動搖。地上的政權本該代表上帝的政權，卻陷於無政府狀態。
5.en:
**They know not.** This verse seems to be a parenthetical observation of the psalmist, making vivid, as by an illustration, God’s denunciation of unjust judges (see Ps. 53:4; 73:22).
**In darkness.** Refusing to know God, they are unqualified for their divinely imposed duty of rendering just judgment (see Prov. 2:13; John 3:19).
**Foundations of the earth.** Probably here the fundamental principles of moral government.
**Out of course.** When unjust judges administer the law, the essentials of moral government totter and fall. Earthly government, which should reflect God’s government, turns into anarchy.

6.zh:
我曾說：你們是神，都是至高者的兒子。

**神 （'elohim）。**見第1節註釋。關於救主引用本節，見約10:34-38。
6.en: **Gods.** Heb. ’elohim (see on v. 1). On the Saviour’s use of this verse, see John 10:34–38.

7.zh:
然而，你們要死，與世人一樣，要仆倒，像王子中的一位。

**世人（'adam）。**見詩8:4註釋；另見創1:26註釋。
**王子。**高貴的階層。他們雖被稱為'elohim（見1,6節註釋），仍將因悖逆而死亡。
7.en:
**Men.** Heb. ’adam, “mankind” (see on Ps. 8:4; also on Gen. 1:26).
**Princes.** Persons of exalted rank. Even though they were called ’elohim (see on vs. 1, 6), they will die for their unfaithfulness.

8.zh:
神啊，求你起來審判世界，因為你要得萬邦為業。

**求你起來。**參詩3:7。
**得萬邦為業。**約翰說：“世上的國，成了我主和主基督的國”（啟11:15；參但2:44,45）。
8.en:
**Arise.** Compare Ps. 3:7.
**Inherit all nations.** In the words of John, “The kingdoms of this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord, and of his Christ” (Rev. 11:15; cf. Dan. 2:44, 45).

0.zh:
序言——本詩懇求上帝拯救以色列，使這個神聖的民族繼續生存。各國結成反對以色列人的同盟，可能特別針對約沙法時代摩押人，亞捫人和以東人的結盟（見代下20章；《先知與君王》第200頁）。本詩的信息適用於任何時代上帝的兒女受到敵人的圍攻，需要上帝幫助的時候。這是一首咒詛詩（見本冊註釋第624頁）。據說布爾戰爭（1899-1902）期間，克留格爾（1825-1904年）在對德瓦士蘭（南非）議會演講時，以及給在他官員的信件中，經常引用本詩中的句子。
關於本詩題記，見本冊註釋第617,627節（《詩篇》序言）。
亞薩的詩歌。
0.en:
INTRODUCTION.—Ps. 83 makes a passionate appeal to God for the deliverance of Israel and the continuance of the holy nation. A conspiracy of nations has been formed against Israel; possibly the union of Moab, Ammon, and Edom in the time of Jehoshaphat is specifically referred to (see 2 Chron. 20; PK 200). The message applies to any period when God’s children are beset by a coalition of enemies and are in need of divine aid. This is one of the imprecatory psalms (see p. 624). It is said that Kruger used its verses frequently during the Boer War in addresses to the Volksraad and in the dispatches sent to his officers.
On the superscription see pp. 617, 627.

1.zh:
（亞薩的詩歌。）神啊，求你不要靜默！神啊，求你不要閉口，也不要不作聲！

見詩28:1；參賽62:7。詩人知道，如果上帝的子民要在危機中得救，上帝就不能保持沉默。一系列短句表達了危急時的祈求。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–18節）**。《先知與君王》第200頁。
1.en: **Keep not thou silence.** See Ps. 28:1; cf. Isa. 62:7. The psalmist knows that if God’s people are to be saved in the crisis, God must not be still. The impetuous succession of brief clauses is the language of entreaty in time of extremity.

2.zh:
因為你的仇敵喧嚷，恨你的抬起頭來。

參詩81:15。
2.en: **That hate thee.** Compare Ps. 81:15.

4.zh:
他們說：來吧，我們將他們剪滅，使他們不再成國！使以色列的名不再被人記念！

**將他們剪滅。**指示周圍的各國陰謀消滅以色列民族，瓜分她的領土（見代下20:11；詩138:7）。
**不再被人記念。**參申32:26；詩34:16；109:13。消滅上帝的教會是撒但一貫的目標。仇敵最討厭基督和基督徒。
4.en:
**Cut them off.** The verse indicates the presence of a well-conceived plot on the part of the surrounding nations to blot out Israel from among the nations, probably with the intention of partitioning her land among themselves (see 2 Chron. 20:11; Ps. 138:7).
**No more in remembrance.** Compare Deut. 32:26; Ps. 34:16; 109:13. It has always been Satan’s desire to destroy the church of God. To the enemy, the words “Christ” and “Christian” are objects of supreme contempt.

5.zh:
他們同心商議，彼此結盟，要抵擋你，

見詩2:2。
5.en: **Together.** See Ps. 2:2.

6.zh:
就是住帳棚的以東人和以實瑪利人，摩押和夏甲人，

**住帳篷的。**指阿拉伯部落的遊牧生活。
第6-8節提到各國的勾結。由於沒有歷史證據證明上述國家曾在任何時候結盟反對以色列，提到這些民族最好理解為出於寫詩的需要。這麼一大批可怕敵人的聚集，增添了危機的色彩，強調了以色列人處在邊境敵人手中的危險。以色列被敵國所包圍，只能向上帝求助。上帝有時斷絕人一切物質的援助，是為了讓他們依賴祂。
**夏甲人。**基列以東的一個遊牧民族。在掃羅的時代曾與以色列人交戰（見代上5:10,19-22）。以色列人打敗了他們，佔領了他們的土地。
6.en:
**Tabernacles.** Literally, “tents,” here meaning “tent dwellers” (by the figure of metonymy). The word well describes the nomadic life of the Arabian tribes.
Verses 6–8 mention the conspiring nations. Since there is no historical evidence that all those nations were confederated against Israel at any one time, it may be best to understand the catalogue of peoples as serving the purpose of poetry. The aggregation of such a formidable array of enemies heightens the color of the crisis, giving great emphasis to Israel’s danger at the hands of border enemies. Israel, surrounded by enemy nations, has no recourse but to God. Sometimes God cuts men off from all material aid that they may learn to rely on Him.
**Hagarenes.** A nomadic people who lived east of Gilead and fought the Israelites in the time of Saul (see 1 Chron. 5:10, 19–22). Israel defeated them and occupied their land.

7.zh:
迦巴勒、亞捫，和亞瑪力、非利士並推羅的居民。

**迦巴勒。**可能位於以東北部的山區（見約瑟弗斯《上古史》卷二，第1，2章）。
**亞瑪力。**生活在巴勒斯坦南部以土買和埃及之間。這是一個古老的民族，是以色列人的宿敵。掃羅違背了上帝關於完全消滅亞瑪力人的命令，饒的他們的國王亞甲的命（見撒上15:8-23），所以被剝奪了王位。
7.en:
**Gebal.** Probably the mountain country in the northern part of Edom (see Josephus Antiquities ii. 1. 2).
**Amalek.** A people living south of Palestine between Idumaea and Egypt. They were an ancient people, inveterate foes of Israel. Contrary to God’s command utterly to destroy the Amalekites. Saul spared Agag, their king (see 1 Sam. 15:8–23), and on that account was rejected from being king.

8.zh:
亞述也與他們連合；他們作羅得子孫的幫手。（細拉）

**亞述。**佔據底格里斯河谷的中心地帶（見創10:22註釋）。
**羅得子孫。**摩押人和亞捫人（見創19:37,38；申2:9,19）。這些民族利用其他民族，實施他們消滅以色列人的陰謀。
**細拉。**見本冊註釋第629頁（《詩篇》序言）。
8.en:
**Assur.** The Assyrians, who occupied the central part of the Tigris valley (see on Gen. 10:22).
**Holpen.** This word is an obsolete past participle of the verb “help.”
**Children of Lot.** Moab and Ammon (see Gen. 19:37, 38; Deut. 2:9, 19). These nations made use of the “arm” of the other nations to carry out their nefarious plan to exterminate Israel.
**Selah.** See p. 629.

9.zh:
求你待他們，如待米甸，如在基順河待西西拉和耶賓一樣。

**米甸。**這裡提到基甸戰勝米甸人（見士7章；8章）。這是以色列歷史上最輝煌的勝利之一（見賽9:4；10:26）。
**西西拉。**士4章記載了打敗耶賓的軍隊和底波拉殺死西西拉的故事。士5章是慶祝勝利的凱歌。
**基順。**見士4:13註釋。
9.en:
**Midianites.** The reference is to Gideon’s victory over the Midianites (see Judges 7; 8), which was regarded as one of the most glorious victories in the history of Israel (see Isa. 9:4; 10:26).
**Sisera.** The story of the defeat of Jabin’s armies and the death of Sisera at the hands of Deborah is told in Judges 4, and celebrated in the sublime poetry of Judges 5.
**Kison.** Or, “Kishon” (see on Judges 4:13).

10.zh:
他們在隱多珥滅亡，成了地上的糞土。

**在隱多珥滅亡。**見撒上28:7註釋。
**成了地上的糞土。**他們的屍體成為土壤的肥料（見王下9:37）。
10.en:
**Perished at En-dor.** See on 1 Sam. 28:7.
**As dung.** Their dead bodies fertilized the soil (see 2 Kings 9:37).

11.zh:
求你叫他們的首領像俄立和西伊伯，叫他們的王子都像西巴和撒慕拿。

**俄立。**俄立和西伊伯是米甸人的首領，被基甸率領的以法蓮人所殺死（見士7:25）。
**西巴。**西巴和撒慕拿是米甸人的王，被基甸所殺（見士8:5,21）。追殺米甸人的場面一定非常恐怖，因而以賽亞把它與在紅海消滅埃及人相提並論，形容西拿基立軍隊的毀滅（賽10:26）。
11.en:
**Oreb.** Oreb and Zeeb were princes of Midian slain by the Ephraimites under Gideon (see Judges 7:25).
**Zebah.** Zebah and Zalmunna were kings of Midian, slain by Gideon (see Judges 8:5, 21). The slaughter of Midian must have been surpassingly awful, for Isaiah mentions it along with the destruction of the Egyptians at the Red Sea as typical of the destruction to be visited on the hosts of Sennacherib (Isa. 10:26).

12.zh:
他們說：我們要得神的住處，作為自己的產業。

**住處（ne'oth）。**或者“草原”。結盟的敵國企圖佔領上帝安排祂子民居住的土地。
12.en: **Houses.** Heb. ne’oth, either “abodes,” or “pasturelands.” The conspiring enemy nations plotted to get possession of the land where God dwelt among His people.

13.zh:
我的神啊，求你叫他們像旋風的塵土，像風前的碎稭。

**旋風的塵土（galgal）。**“輪子”。也可指輪狀的幹薊（見賽17:13）。本句祈求敵人完全被消滅和驅逐，就像糠秕被風吹散。
**碎秸。**或“糠秕”（見詩1:4）。指毫無價值，只配燒掉的東西（伯13:25；瑪4:1）。
13.en:
**A wheel.** Heb. galgal, generally “wheel,” although galgal seems also to have been used of the wheel-shaped dried calyx of a thistle (see Isa. 17:13). The prayer is that the enemy may be driven away in utter destruction, as our modern tumbleweed is driven before the wind.
**Stubble.** Or, “chaff” (see Ps. 1:4). These objects describe that which is utterly light and valueless (Job 13:25; Mal. 4:1), fit only for destruction.

14.zh:
火怎樣焚燒樹林，火焰怎樣燒著山嶺，

**火怎樣焚燒樹林。**參賽9:18；10:17,18；亞12:6。
**山嶺。**即山嶺裡的植物。
14.en:
**As the flame.** Compare Isa. 9:18; 10:17, 18; Zech. 12:6.
**Mountains.** That is, the vegetation growing on the mountains.

15.zh:
求你也照樣用狂風追趕他們，用暴雨恐嚇他們。

參詩35:4-6。
15.en: **Persecute them.** Compare Ps. 35:4–6.

16.zh:
願你使他們滿面羞恥，好叫他們尋求你─耶和華的名！

**願你使他們滿面羞恥。**失望和困惑往往顯露在臉上的。
**尋求你耶和華的名。**見詩5:11；7:17註釋。詩人不是祈求讓以色列的仇敵受苦，而是通過上帝臨到他們身上的事，使他們承認祂為他們的上帝，並歸向祂。詩人希望他們的屈辱能導致他們順服上帝的旨意。
16.en:
**Fill their faces.** Disappointment and confusion usually show on the face.
**Seek thy name.** See on Ps. 5:11; 7:17. The psalmist’s prayer is not that the enemies of Israel may be made to suffer, but that, through the events God permits to come upon them, they may be led to acknowledge Him and turn to Him as their God. The psalmist would have their humiliation result in submission to God’s will.

17.zh:
願他們永遠羞愧驚惶！願他們慚愧滅亡！

詩人祈求讓以色列的仇敵蒙羞，到毀滅的邊緣，以致真心實意地歸向上帝（見賽37:20）。
17.en: **Let them be confounded.** The psalmist prays that the enemies of Israel may be humiliated and brought even to the verge of destruction, that they may turn to God in sincerity and truth (see Isa. 37:20).

18.zh:
使他們知道：惟獨你─名為耶和華的─是全地以上的至高者！

**他們。**指結盟的各國。
**耶和華。**見出6:3註釋。
**至高者。**詩人祈求消滅或打垮以色列的仇敵，不是為個人復仇，而是要證明上帝是世界上最高的統治者。懲罰的目的是讓人認識上帝！本詩以這句莊嚴的話語結束。
18.en:
**Men.** Rather, “they,” in reference to the confederate nations.
**Jehovah.** See on Ex. 6:3.
**The most high.** The psalmist prays for the destruction or near destruction of Israel’s enemies, not in personal vindictiveness, but to show that Jehovah is the supreme ruler of the world. The purpose of judgment is that men may know God! On this sublime note the psalm closes.

0.zh:
序言——本詩為上帝的“受膏者”大衛所作（第9節；《證言》卷四534頁），可能寫於他逃離耶路撒冷之時。本詩熱情地抒發了對上帝殿宇和敬拜上帝嚮往和摯愛。詩歌似乎描寫了住在聖所之人的福氣（第1-4,9-11）；前往聖所之人的福氣（第5-8）；以及那些雖然無法在上帝的殿裡敬拜，但信靠上帝之人的福氣。詩歌採用希伯來語哀歌的韻律，渲染了其悲愴的氣氛。這首神聖優美的抒情詩所抒發的感情，已超越了個人的色彩，表達了每一個上帝兒女的情感。因為他們被剝奪了與基督徒同胞交往的特權，渴望與弟兄們一同敬拜上帝。詩84篇可以與詩42篇相比。據說蘇格蘭立約派的伊莎貝爾·艾莉森和馬裡恩·哈里斯在走向絞架時，用“殉道者”的曲調，吟唱了本詩。
關於本詩的題記，見本冊註釋第617,629頁（《詩篇》序言）。
可拉後裔的詩，交與伶長。用迦特樂器。
0.en:
INTRODUCTION.—Ps. 84 was composed by David, the Lord’s “anointed” (v. 9; 4T 534), perhaps when he was exiled from Jerusalem. It is a passionate lyrical expression of devotion and love for the house of Jehovah and His worship. The psalm seems to describe the blessedness of those who dwell in the sacred precincts (vs. 1–4, 9–11); the blessedness of those who make pilgrimages to the sanctuary (vs. 5–8); and the blessedness of those who, deprived of the privilege of actually worshiping in God’s house, nevertheless put their trust in God. The pathos of this tender poem is enhanced by the elegiac rhythm in which the Hebrew lines are cast. The sentiments of this exquisite sacred lyric are more than personal; they are the deepest sentiments of every child of God who, deprived of the privilege of communion with fellow Christians, has ever longed for fellowship with his brethren in the corporate worship of God. Ps. 84 may be compared with Ps. 42. It is said that Isabel Alison and Marion Harris, Scottish Covenanters, sang the words of Ps. 84 to the tune “Martyrs” as they went to the scaffold.
On the superscription see pp. 617, 629.

1.zh:
（可拉後裔的詩，交與伶長。用迦特樂器。）萬軍之耶和華啊，你的居所何等可愛！

**可愛。**或“親切”。
**居所。**或“帳幕”。
1.en:
**Amiable.** Or, “lovely.”
**Tabernacles.** Literally, “dwelling places.”

2.zh:
我羨慕渴想耶和華的院宇；我的心腸，我的肉體向永生神呼籲（或譯：歡呼）。

**我羨慕。**基督徒的祈禱也應該這樣誠懇和熱情（見《證言》卷四534頁）。
**呼籲（ranan）。**或“歡呼”（見詩98:4）。
**永生上帝。**與無生命的偶像不同（見詩42:2。這是其他詩篇中唯一一處提到“永生上帝”的地方，參書3:10；何1:10）。在《新約》經常出現“永生的上帝”（見太16:16；約6:69；徒14:15；羅9:26；林後3:3；來3:12；啟7:2等）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《早期著作》第110頁；《傳道良助》第257；《證言》卷二第223頁；《證言》卷四第534頁。
2.en:
**My soul longeth.** Such earnestness and fervency should characterize the Christian’s prayer (see 4T 534).
**Crieth out.** Heb. ranan, generally, “to cry for joy” (see Ps. 98:4).
**The living God.** As distinguished from idols, which are dead (see Ps. 42:2), the only other place in the Psalter where the expression “living God” appears; cf. Joshua 3:10; Hosea 1:10. In the NT the expression “living God” occurs frequently (see Matt. 16:16; John 6:69; Acts 14:15; Rom. 9:26; 2 Cor. 3:3; Heb. 3:12; Rev. 7:2; etc.).

3.zh:
萬軍之耶和華─我的王，我的神啊，在你祭壇那裡，麻雀為自己找著房屋，燕子為自己找著菢雛之窩。

**麻雀。**麻雀和燕子在巴勒斯坦十分普遍。
**你祭壇。**指聖所（轉喻）。
詩人暗示了本詩的大意：連鳥兒也有可以自由進入聖所，在裡面築巢不受打擾。詩人卻斷絕了快樂的源泉，被剝奪了在聖所敬拜的特權。本節所流露的思鄉之情，成為文學領域中最優美的思鄉絕句。第10節強調了這種情懷。
3.en:
**Sparrow.** Both the sparrow and the swallow were common in Palestine.
**Thine altars.** The sanctuary (by the figure of metonymy).
The general meaning of the verse, whose conclusion the poet only implies, is that even the birds have free access to the sacred precincts of the sanctuary, they make their homes there undisturbed, while the psalmist is exiled from the source of his joy, is denied the privilege of worshiping within the sacred enclosure. The nostalgic appeal of this verse is one of the most delicately beautiful expressions of homesickness in the whole realm of literature. The idea is emphasized in v. 10.

4.zh:
如此住在你殿中的便為有福！他們仍要讚美你。（細拉）

**有福。**見詩1:1註釋。第一個祝福是給予住在聖所裡的人（見代上9:19 26:1；注意本詩題記的恰當性）。詩人羨慕那些奉身在聖所侍奉的人。
**仍要讚美。**聖所是持續不斷地讚美的場所，是天國的預嘗。
**細拉。**見本冊註釋第629頁（《詩篇》序言）。
4.en:
**Blessed.** See on Ps. 1:1. The first blessing is bestowed on those who dwell in the sacred precincts (see 1 Chron. 9:19 26:1; note the appropriateness of the superscription to the psalm). The psalmist envies those who devote their lives to service in the sanctuary.
**Still praising.** The sanctuary is a place of continued praise, a foretaste of heaven.
**Selah.** See p. 629.

5.zh:
靠你有力量、心中想往錫安大道的，這人便為有福！

**有福。**見詩1:1註釋。第二個祝福賜給那些心中思念上帝，在國家的重大節日前往耶路撒冷的人（見第4,12節）。
**力量。**認識到上帝是他力量源泉的人有福的（見第7節）。
**大道9mesilloth）。**有人解釋說：思想通往聖所的道路，做好出發的準備，決心前往耶路撒冷的聖所敬拜的人是有福的。他們每一次前往，都可望見到熟悉的路標；事後，在他的腦海中縈繞著他們所走過的每一步熟悉的道路。
5.en:
**Blessed.** See on Ps. 1:1. The second blessing is bestowed on those who hold God in their hearts as they make the pilgrimage to Jerusalem (see vs. 4, 12) at the time of the great national feasts.
**Strength.** Blessed is the man who realizes that God is the source of his strength (see v. 7).
**Ways.** Heb. mesilloth, “highways.” The following interpretation of the passage has been suggested: the man is happy who meditates on the highways that lead to the sanctuary, who prepares to travel over them, who sets his heart on making the pilgrimage to Jerusalem and worshiping in the sanctuary. On every succeeding pilgrimage he anticipates the familiar landmarks of the road; and ever after, every step of the familiar way lingers in his memory.

6.zh:
他們經過流淚谷，叫這谷變為泉源之地；並有秋雨之福蓋滿了全谷。

**流淚谷。**原文是baka'。含義不明。在其他地方baka'譯為“桑樹”，但在植物學上定義不明確（見撒下5:23註釋）。七十士譯本和武加大譯本亦為“流淚谷”。 朝聖的人憑著信心，盼望和喜樂，把“流淚谷”變成“泉源之地”。這是真宗教效果的美妙說明。在原先悲傷痛苦之處，傳播快樂和安慰（見賽35:1,2,6,7）。
**泉源。**前往天上錫安朝聖的人在曠野開闢泉源，幫助後來的人。基督徒總是要把世界變更加美好的地方。如果我們的心與上帝保持良好的關係，即使在人生惡劣的環境中，我們也能獲得鼓舞。
**蓋滿了全谷。**詩人看見在乾旱之地佈滿水池。上帝祝福朝聖者所看到的一切，因為他們在前進時心中充滿喜樂。
因為《天路歷程》，班揚的貝德福監獄成為別人蒙福的泉源。南丁格爾所經歷的高燒，病菌和壞疽，導致了醫護界的一場革命。
6.en:
**Baca.** Heb. baka’. The meaning of the word is doubtful. Elsewhere baka’ is translated “mulberry tree,” but the exact botanical identification is uncertain (see on 2 Sam. 5:23). The LXX and the Vulgate translate the phrase “valley of Baca” as “valley of tears.” In their faith and hope and joy the pilgrims turn the “vale of tears” into “a well.” This is a beautiful illustration of the effect of real religion, spreading gladness and comfort where before there was only sorrow and trouble (see Isa. 35:1, 2, 6, 7).
**A well.** Real pilgrims on the way to the heavenly Zion open springs in the desert for those who follow on the way. Christians have always made the world a better place to live in. If our hearts are right with God, we shall derive refreshment even from the wretched experiences of life.
**Filleth the pools.** The poet sees the arid ground covered with pools of water. God’s blessing rests upon everything that the pilgrims behold because their hearts are full of joy as they make their pilgrimage.
Bunyan’s Bedford jail became a fountain of blessing to others because of Pilgrim’s Progress. Florence Nightingale’s experience with fever, germs, and gangrene resulted in a revolution in hospital care.

7.zh:
他們行走，力上加力，各人到錫安朝見神。

**力上加力。**這些朝聖者在路上不會有持久的疲勞。他們欣喜地盼望到錫安敬拜，成為他們前進的動力。在旅途中每一次力量的展現都給下一步行程帶來新的活力，新的力量（見賽40:31；約1:16；羅1:17；林後3:18）。本節生動地表現了基督徒共往耶路撒冷的旅途生涯。他們讚美，祈禱，相互安慰，在路上相互鼓勵，加強了對上帝的信心，在接近那城的時候，他們道路中的困難減輕了（見來10:25；《證言》卷五93頁）。
**朝見上帝。**朝聖成功地結束。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《安息日學訓言》第49頁；《餘民教會》 71頁；《給傳道人的證言》第425,441頁；《證言》卷一第179頁；《證言》卷二第405頁；《證言》卷五第93頁；《證言》卷九第200頁。
7.en:
**From strength to strength.** There is no lasting fatigue in the journey of these pilgrims. They are drawn on by the joyful anticipation of worshiping in Zion. Every exhibition of strength in journeying gives added vitality, increased strength, for the next stage of the pilgrimage (see Isa. 40:31; John 1:16; Rom. 1:17; 2 Cor. 3:18). Here is a lovely illustration of the life of Christians journeying together to the New Jerusalem—by their praise, prayer, and mutual comfort, cheering one another along the way, strengthening their faith in God, and making the way less difficult as they approach the city (see Heb. 10:25; 5T 93).
**Appeareth before God.** The pilgrimage is successfully completed.

8.zh:
耶和華─萬軍之神啊，求你聽我的禱告！雅各的神啊，求你留心聽！（細拉）

**求你留心聽。**見詩20:1。
**細拉。**見本冊註釋第629頁（《詩篇》序言）。
8.en:
**Give ear.** See Ps. 20:1
**Selah.** See p. 629.

9.zh:
神啊，你是我們的盾牌；求你垂顧觀看你受膏者的面！

**盾牌。**烏加列語文獻表明（見本冊註釋第618頁），magen可以作動詞，意為“懇求”。這句話可譯為，“上帝啊，我們懇求”。
**你受膏者。**見撒上16:1；撒下22:51；詩89:20。大衛禱告祈求上帝悅納他（見詩119:132）。本節轉用第三人稱，十分微妙。
9.en:
**Shield.** As demonstrated by the Ugaritic (see p. 618), magen may be a verb, meaning “to implore.” The phrase can then be translated, “We implore, look, O God.”
**Thine anointed.** See 1 Sam. 16:1; 2 Sam. 22:51; Ps. 89:20. David prays that God may look with favor upon him (see Ps. 119:132). There is great delicacy in the shift to the third person in this verse.

10.zh:
在你的院宇住一日，勝似在別處住千日；寧可在我神殿中看門，不願住在惡人的帳棚裡。

**勝似在別處住千日。**大衛寧願在聖所的庭院裡過一天，也不願在地上任何地方過一千日。大衛的語言特別辛酸，因為他寫詩時漂泊在外。上帝真正的兒女總是以參加敬拜上帝為樂。
**看門。**詩人寧願做一個聖所的僕人，也不願在惡人中間享受榮華，遠離上帝和聖所。
10.en:
**Better than a thousand.** David would rather spend a single day in the courts of the sanctuary than a thousand days anywhere else on earth. David’s statement is especially poignant, since he was in exile when he composed the psalm. The true child of God ever takes delight in participating in divine worship.
**Doorkeeper.** The psalmist would prefer to be a sanctuary servant rather than to enjoy honor among the wicked, estranged from God and the sanctuary.

11.zh:
因為耶和華─神是日頭，是盾牌，要賜下恩惠和榮耀。他未嘗留下一樣好處不給那些行動正直的人。

**日頭。**上帝是光源，不論從物質上還是從精神上說（見詩27:1；賽60:19,20；瑪4:2；啟21:23；22:25）。彌賽亞是“公義的日頭”（瑪4:2）。
**盾牌。**見詩3:3註釋；參《善惡之爭》第673頁。
**恩惠和榮耀。**基督徒在今生恩典的國度中能得到恩惠，在將來榮耀的國度中獲得榮耀（見啟21:11,24）。
**未嘗留下一樣好處。**見詩34:10；林前2:9；弗3:20；腓4:19。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《善惡之爭》第673頁；《服務真詮》第481頁；《今日的生活》第102頁；《給青年人的信息》第123頁；《拾級就主》第72；《救贖的故事》第102,429頁；《證言》卷一第120頁；《證言》卷九第75頁。
11.en:
**Sun.** God is the source of light, materially and spiritually (see Ps. 27:1; Isa. 60:19, 20; Mal. 4:2; Rev. 21:23; 22:25). The expression “Sun of righteousness” is applied to the Messiah (Mal. 4:2).
**Shield.** See on Ps. 3:3; cf. GC 673.
**Grace and glory.** The Christian finds inward grace here, in the kingdom of grace; outward glory there, in the kingdom of glory (see Rev. 21:11, 24).
**No good thing.** See Ps. 34:10; 1 Cor. 2:9; Eph. 3:20; Phil. 4:19.
**Blessed.** See on Ps. 1:1. The third and last blessing of the psalm falls upon those who, denied the privilege of dwelling in the courts of God, or making pilgrimage to the sanctuary, nevertheless worship God with the eye of faith, in spirit and in truth (see John 4:20–24), putting complete trust in Him. This blessing is the ultimate experience of the one who trusts in God for personal and present salvation. Compare the teachings of the apostle Paul on this subject as set forth in Gal. 2:20.

12.zh:
萬軍之耶和華啊，倚靠你的人便為有福！

見詩1:1註釋。這是本詩第三次，也是最後一次祝福那些無法住在上帝的庭院或前往聖所，但憑著心靈和誠實，以信心敬拜上帝，完全信靠祂的人（見約4:20-24）。這個福氣最終屬於那些信靠上帝現在救他的人。參閱使徒保羅在加2:20所寫這方面的教訓。

0.zh:
序言——本詩包括感謝把以色列人從囚擄中拯救出來（第1-3節）；祈求獲得更充分的復興（第4-7節）；預示將最後賜下屬靈和物質上的福惠作為對詩人祈禱的答覆。沒有充分的證據證明本詩創作的時間。10-13節提供了生動的形象，成為《詩篇》中最優秀的擬人篇章之一。據說O·克倫威爾（1599-1658）最喜歡這首詩。
關於本詩的題記，見本冊註釋第617,627頁（《詩篇》序言）。
可拉後裔的詩，交與伶長。
0.en:
INTRODUCTION.—Ps. 85 consists of a thanksgiving for the deliverance of Israel from the captor (vs. 1–3); a prayer for more complete restoration (vs. 4–7); and a foretaste of the answer to the psalmist’s prayer in the ultimate bestowal of spiritual and material blessings. There is insufficient evidence to tie the psalm to any particular date. Among the supreme personifications of the book of Psalms are the vivid images presented in Ps. 85:10–13. It is said that the psalm was a favorite of Oliver Cromwell’s.
On the superscription see pp. 617, 627.

1.zh:
（可拉後裔的詩，交與伶長。）耶和華啊，你已經向你的地施恩，救回被擄的雅各。

上帝己欣然把以色列的災難變為福氣。本節暗示詩人覺得上帝有時沒有施恩（見詩77:7-9）。
1.en:
**Been favourable.** God had been pleased to turn the calamities of the Jews into blessings. The statement implies that the psalmist felt there were times when God had not been gracious (see Ps. 77:7–9).
**Forgiven.** Captivity came as a result of sin; God’s remission of punishment was considered to be evidence that God had forgiven national sin.
**Covered.** See on Ps. 32:1.
**Selah.** See p. 629.

2.zh:
你赦免了你百姓的罪孽，遮蓋了他們一切的過犯。（細拉）

**赦免了。**被擄是犯罪的後果；上帝豁免懲罰證明上帝赦免了百姓的罪。
**遮蓋了。**見詩32:1註釋。
**細拉。**見本冊註釋第629頁（《詩篇》序言）。

4.zh:
拯救我們的神啊，求你使我們回轉，叫你的惱恨向我們止息。

**求你使我們迴轉。**上帝已恩待自己的子民。詩人現在祈求上帝引導祂的子民悔改。我們無法改變自己。我們需要上帝的恩典（見詩80:3,7,19）。
**拯救我們的上帝啊。**見詩27:9；51:14。
**止息。**似乎與第3節矛盾，但可以理解為上帝忿怒的後果。百姓雖已擺脫囚擄，土地卻依然荒蕪。
4.en:
**Turn.** God has graciously turned toward His people. The psalmist’s prayer now is that God will bring His people to repentance. We cannot turn of our own selves; we need the grace of God (see Ps. 80:3, 7, 19).
**God of our salvation.** See Ps. 27:9; 51:14.
**To cease.** Verbally this statement seems to contradict the statement of v. 3, but it may be understood as referring to the effects of God’s anger. The captivity had been restored, but the land was still in a state of desolation.

5.zh:
你要向我們發怒到永遠嗎？你要將你的怒氣延留到萬代嗎？

**到萬代。**即“一代又一代”。
5.en: **To all generations.** Literally, “from generation to generation.”

6.zh:
你不再將我們救活，使你的百姓靠你歡喜嗎？

**你。**只有上帝才能復興祂的子民。
**救活。**以斯拉曾祈禱“在受轄制之中稍微復興”（拉9:8）。
**歡喜。**宗教復興帶來喜樂（見尼12:27）。
**靠你。**不但因屬世的福惠，而且因萬物的施給者上帝。
6.en:
**Thou.** God alone can revive His people.
**Revive.** Ezra prayed for “a little reviving in our bondage” (Ezra 9:8).
**May rejoice.** A revival of religion brings rejoicing (see Neh. 12:27).
**In thee.** Not in earthly blessings alone, but in God, the giver of all.

8.zh:
我要聽神─耶和華所說的話；因為他必應許將平安賜給他的百姓─他的聖民；他們卻不可再轉去妄行。

**我要聽。**詩人已表達了自己的悲傷和祈禱。現在他安靜地等候平安的答覆。上帝對我們所說的話比我們對祂所說的話更加重要。
**平安（shalom）。**沒有什麼詞比“平安”賦有更甜美的內涵令（見詩29:11；72:3,7；122:6-8；民6:26；賽9:6,7；亞6:13）。
**聖民（chasidim）。**見詩36篇補充註釋。Chasidim表明他們通過自己的生活方式愛上帝。上帝也向他們顯示祂的愛（見詩4:3）。
**妄行。**如果以色列在得救以後恢復妄行，最後的結局將更加糟糕（見太12:45；約5:14）。七十士譯本為“對於那些把心轉向他的人”。
8.en:
**I will hear.** The psalmist has expressed his sorrow and has prayed; now he will wait calmly, quietly, for an answer of peace. What God says to us is more important than what we say to Him.
**Peace.** Heb. shalom. Few Hebrew words are sweeter in their connotations than the word “peace” (see Ps. 29:11; 72:3, 7; 122:6–8; Num. 6:26; Isa. 9:6, 7; Zech. 6:13).
**Saints.** Heb. chasidim (see Additional Note on Ps. 36). The chasidim show their love for God by their way of life, and God shows His love to them (see Ps. 4:3).
**Folly.** If, after deliverance, Israel should return to her folly, her latter end would be still worse (see Matt. 12:45; John 5:14). Instead of “let them not turn again to folly,” the LXX reads “to those who turn the heart unto him.”

9.zh:
他的救恩誠然與敬畏他的人相近，叫榮耀住在我們的地上。

顯然指恢復地上的榮耀和繁華，和以前一樣。
9.en: **Glory.** Here, evidently, the return of earthly glory and prosperity, as of old.

10.zh:
慈愛和誠實彼此相遇；公義和平安彼此相親。

**慈愛和誠實。**這是同義平行的典範，兩個分句表現了上帝的兩大基本特性（見詩25:10；72:3），以形象的擬人手法，展示了整個救贖計劃（見《證言》卷五633頁；《先祖與先知》第349頁；《歷代願望》第762頁）。
**彼此相親。**公正與寬恕表面上互不相容，卻像好友擁抱在一起（見《歷代願望》762頁）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《復臨信徒的家庭》第311頁；《安息日學訓言》第171頁；《歷代願望》第762,834頁；《佈道論》第292頁；《傳道良助》第156頁；《先祖與先知》第349頁；《證言》卷五第633頁；《證言》卷六第60頁；《證言》卷七第209頁。
10.en:
**Mercy and truth.** The exquisite example of synonymous parallelism displayed in this verse joins in each clause the two cardinal attributes of God’s character (see Ps. 25:10; 72:3). In picturesque figures of personification the whole plan of salvation is epitomized (see 5T 633; PP 349; DA 762).
**Have kissed.** Justice and pardon, seemingly alienated from each other, embrace as loving friends (see DA 762).

11.zh:
誠實從地而生；公義從天而現。

**從天而現。**為了與“誠實”相會（參詩85:10；賽45:8）。
11.en: **Look down from heaven.** To meet “truth” (cf. Ps. 85:10; Isa. 45:8).

12.zh:
耶和華必將好處賜給我們；我們的地也要多出土產。

見詩84:11。
12.en: **Good.** See Ps. 84:11.

13.zh:
公義要行在他面前，叫他的腳蹤成為可走的路。

**行在他面前。**見賽58:8。擬人化的公義為恢復上帝的悅納預備道路（見太3:3）。
**成為可走的路。**公義作為先鋒，為救贖祂的子民的耶和華開路。
13.en:
**Shall go before him.** See Isa. 58:8. Righteousness is personified as preparing the way for restoration to divine favor (see Matt. 3:3).
**Shall set us.** Righteousness, as a herald, prepares the way for the coming of Jehovah, who brings salvation to His people.

0.zh:
序言——這是一首崇拜詩歌，慶祝惡人的毀滅和上帝忠心兒女的得勝與喜樂。本詩的創作是詩人有感於安息日與創造主的交往，並看到上帝在自然界中的大能（見《歷代願望》第281,282頁）。根據傳統的說法，利未人在早晨獻奠祭和第一隻羔羊時要唱這首詩（見民28:3-9）。這是西法拉猶太人的一首崇拜詩歌。在安息日，我們最好把眼光從今生的困惑轉到永恆的世界。那裡我們不再有任何的疑惑和迷茫。
關於本詩的題記，見本冊註釋第627頁（《詩篇》序言）。
安息日的詩歌。
0.en:
INTRODUCTION.—Ps. 92 is a liturgical anthem celebrating the destruction of evil and the triumph and happiness of God’s faithful children. The psalm was inspired by the poet’s communion with the Creator on the Sabbath day and his observation of God’s power in nature (see DA 281, 282). Tradition says that it was sung by the Levites in the morning at the time of the drink offering, on the offering of the first lamb (see Num. 28:3–9). It is one of the psalms in the Sephardic liturgy. On the Sabbath it is well that we turn our eyes from the perplexing questions of this world to the eternal world, where we shall be above all doubt and perplexity.
On the superscription see p. 627.

1.zh:
（安息日的詩歌。）稱謝耶和華！歌頌你至高者的名！

**歌頌你。**在安息日特別需要讚美（見《教育論》第251頁）。
**名。**見詩5:11；7:17註釋。
**至高者（`Elyon）。**見本註釋卷一173頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–4節）**。《證言》卷八第12頁。
1.en:
**To sing praises.** Praise is especially appropriate on the Sabbath day (see Ed 251).
**Name.** See on Ps. 5:11; 7:17.
**Most High.** Heb. ‘Elyon (see Vol. I, p. 173).

2.zh:
用十弦的樂器和瑟，用琴彈幽雅的聲音，早晨傳揚你的慈愛；每夜傳揚你的信實。這本為美事。併於上節。

**早晨。**見詩5:3註釋；參哀3:23;《喜樂的泉源》第74,75頁。
**每夜。**見詩4:4註釋；參詩16:7。摩西的律法規定早祭和晚祭，從而設立了晨禱和晚禱（見出29:38,39）。
**用十弦的樂器。**見詩33:2註釋；參詩57:8。本節暗示這首詩歌是用於公眾禮拜的。個人崇拜時一般不需要樂器。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《今日的生活》第200頁。
2.en:
**In the morning.** See on Ps. 5:3; cf. Lam. 3:23; SC 74, 75.
**Every night.** Literally, “in the nights” (see on Ps. 4:4; cf. Ps. 16:7). The Mosaic law provided for worship morning and evening by the establishment of the morning and evening sacrifice (see Ex. 29:38, 39).

4.zh:
因你─耶和華藉著你的作為叫我高興，我要因你手的工作歡呼。

要麼指安息日的制度所紀念的創造（見《歷代願望》第282頁），要麼泛指上帝的作為，或祂大能的特別顯示。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《服務真詮》第463頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（4–5節）**。《歷代願望》第282頁。
4.en:
**Through thy work.** Either the work of creation, celebrated by the Sabbath institution (see DA 282), or God’s works in general, or some particular demonstration of God’s power.
**I will triumph.** Or, “I will cry for joy.”

5.zh:
耶和華啊，你的工作何其大！你的心思極其深！

**你的工作。**見詩40:5註釋。
**心思。**上帝在祂的創造和天意的不斷遠作中所顯示的旨意和計劃，是人類所難以理解的（見賽55:8,9；羅11:33,34；參林前2:9）。
5.en:
**Thy works.** See on Ps. 40:5.
**Thoughts.** God’s purposes, His designs, as revealed in creation and in His continual providences, are beyond the comprehension of man (see Isa. 55:8, 9; Rom. 11:33, 34; cf. 1 Cor. 2:9).

6.zh:
畜類人不曉得；愚頑人也不明白。

粗魯，沒有教養，愚昧，麻木的人是不能理解的。
6.en: **A brutish man.** Men, rude, uncultivated, stupid, dull of perception, cannot understand.

7.zh:
惡人茂盛如草，一切作孽之人發旺的時候，正是他們要滅亡，直到永遠。

這是約伯所困惑的問題（伯21:7-21），經常出現在《詩篇》中（見詩73:2-15）。但本詩的作者沒有困惑。這個問題一經提出，就馬上得到解決，因為認識到惡人取得勝利以後，毀滅就接踵而來（見詩73:18-20）。毀滅是罪惡自然而不可避免的結果。
7.en: **As the grass.** The problem that disturbed Job (Job 21:7–21) and that appears so often in the Psalms (see Ps. 73:2–15) does not disturb the author of this psalm. It is stated and immediately solved in the realization that the destruction of the wicked follows their triumph (see Ps. 73:18–20). Destruction is the natural and inevitable result of wickedness.

8.zh:
惟你─耶和華是至高，直到永遠。

上帝不受惡人的興衰所影響。祂一直坐在至高的寶座上（見《教育論》第173頁；《服務真詮》第417頁）。
8.en: **Art most high.** God, unaffected by the prosperity or downfall of the wicked, remains enthroned on high (see Ed 173; MH 417).

9.zh:
耶和華啊，你的仇敵都要滅亡；一切作孽的也要離散。

**要滅亡。**強調上帝要高舉，惡人要滅亡。
**一切作孽的。**見第7節。
9.en:
**Shall perish.** The repetition of the phrase “for, lo, thine enemies” lends emphasis to the idea that, since God must be exalted, the wicked must perish.
**Workers of iniquity.** See v. 7.

10.zh:
你卻高舉了我的角，如野牛的角；我是被新油膏了的。

**角。**象徵力量（見申33:17）。詩人相信自己與上帝的友誼，相信上帝會高舉他。
**野牛。**見伯39:9註釋。
**新油。**不是陳腐的油（見詩23:5）。
10.en:
**Horn.** A symbol of strength (see Deut. 33:17). The psalmist had such confidence in his friendship with God that he trusted God to lift him up.
**Unicorn.** A wild ox (see on Job. 39:9).
**Fresh oil.** Not oil that is old and rancid (see Ps. 23:5).

12.zh:
義人要發旺如棕樹，生長如利巴嫩的香柏樹。

**要發旺。**見詩1:3；詩52:8；何14:5,6；《服務真詮》第286頁。
**如棕樹。**棕樹的特點是四季常青的（見歌7:8；耶10:5）。參第7,9,11節。
**香柏樹。**見詩29:5；104:16,17；見《證言》卷五第514,515頁。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《教育論》第116頁；《先祖與先知》第450頁；《證言》卷五第514頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（12–14節）**。《服務真詮》第286頁。
12.en:
**Shall flourish.** See Ps. 1:3; Ps. 52:8; Hosea 14:5, 6; MH 286.
**Like the palm tree.** The palm was celebrated for its ability to remain green through winter and summer alike (see S. of Sol. 7:8; Jer. 10:5). Note the contrast with vs. 7, 9, 11.
**Like a cedar.** See Ps. 29:5; 104:16, 17; see 5T 514, 515.

13.zh:
他們栽於耶和華的殿中，發旺在我們神的院裡。

**懷愛倫註釋（13–16節）**。見詩71:9、17、19懷愛倫註釋。

14.zh:
他們年老的時候仍要結果子，要滿了汁漿而常發青，

**年老的時候。**義人將繼續行善，結果累累，榮耀上帝。老年也許是人一生中結果最豐富的時期。退休以後可能是最有成就的。
**滿了汁漿而常發青。**他們必將健康而精力充沛。這裡繼續第12節所開始的比喻。
14.en:
**In old age.** The righteous will continue to be productive and glorify God by their good works. Old age may be the most fruitful part of a man’s life. The years of retirement may be the most productive.
**Fat and flourishing.** They will be healthy and vigorous. The metaphor begun in v. 12 is sustained.

15.zh:
好顯明耶和華是正直的。他是我的磐石，在他毫無不義。

**顯明。**義人老年的幸福和多結果子，證明上帝是信實的。祂信守自己的諾言。
**毫無不義。**本節的最後兩個分句是第一分句“顯明耶和華是正直的”的繼續。
15.en:
**To shew.** The fact that the old age of the righteous is happy and productive proves the faithfulness of God, and shows that He keeps His promises.
**No unrighteousness.** The last two clauses of the verse probably depend upon the first clause of the verse, “to shew that the Lord is upright.”

92.3: **Upon an instrument.** See on Ps. 33:2; cf. Ps. 57:8. The verse suggests the use of the psalm in public worship. Instruments were probably not generally used in private devotions.

0.zh: 序言——本詩頌揚耶和華為宇宙的主宰，展示了上帝從亙古到永遠坐在寶座上的輝煌畫面。這是一系列頌讚詩歌中的第一首（從詩93篇到詩101篇），讚美上帝為創造主，顯示上帝有能力控制受造之物，推翻祂的仇敵，信守諾言，以及祂居所的神聖。七十士譯本的題記裡還注有”安息日前一天”。
0.en: INTRODUCTION.—Ps. 93 celebrates Jehovah as Sovereign of the universe. It is a picture of the magnificent enthronement of Deity upon a throne established from everlasting to everlasting. The psalm is the first of a series of royal psalms (Ps. 93 to Ps. 101) glorifying God as Creator and Lord. Ps. 93 shows His power in control of creation, in the overthrow of His enemies, in the faithfulness of His word, and in the holiness of His house. The LXX includes in its superscription the phrase, “for the day before the Sabbath.”

1.zh:
耶和華作王！他以威嚴為衣穿上；耶和華以能力為衣，以能力束腰，世界就堅定，不得動搖。

**懷愛倫註釋（1–2節）**。《證言》卷八第271頁。
1.en: **Stablished.** An archaic word for “established.”

2.zh:
你的寶座從太初立定；你從亙古就有。

**亙古。**見詩90:1,2；《證言》卷八270頁。
2.en: **Everlasting.** See Ps. 90:1, 2; 8T 270.

3.zh:
耶和華啊，大水揚起，大水發聲，波浪澎湃。

**大水。**或“河流”。指各國人民或入侵的大軍（見賽8:7,8）。詩人也許是頌揚上帝的大能超過一切受造之物。
3.en: **The floods.** Or, “rivers.” Waters here may represent peoples, invading hosts (see Isa. 8:7, 8). Or the psalmist may be glorifying God as omnipotent above His creation.

4.zh:
耶和華在高處大有能力，勝過諸水的響聲，洋海的大浪。

第4節與第3節相對應，可能採取輪唱的方式。
4.en: **Is mightier.** Verse 4, the answer to v. 3, may have been sung antiphonally.

5.zh:
耶和華啊，你的法度最的確；你的殿永稱為聖，是合宜的。

只有永遠才足以表達上帝居所之法度的神聖特徵。聖潔是上帝主權的特點。有限的人類只有在永恆裡才能開始明白上帝無限的特徵。
5.en: **For ever.** Only eternity will be ample enough to show that holiness characterizes the rule of God’s house. Holiness is the characteristic of divine sovereignty. Only in eternity will finite mortals begin to understand the infinite characteristics of Deity.

0.zh: 序言——本詩祈求上帝回答惡人為什麼在表面上取得勝利的問題（第1-7節）；對誇口上帝鞭長莫及的邪惡領袖說話（第8-11節）；從上帝保護義人，義人最後獲勝中找到最終的答案（第12-23節）。本詩保證，不管表面現象如何，公義終將獲勝（見詩92篇）。七十士譯本的題記裡還注有“一週的第四天”。本詩具有崇拜詩歌的特徵。
0.en: INTRODUCTION.—Ps. 94 appeals to God for an answer to the problem of the apparent triumph of the wicked (vs. 1–7), addresses unjust leaders who boast of God’s apparent aloofness from the problem (vs. 8–11), and finds an ultimate answer in God’s defense of the righteous and the final triumph of the right (vs. 12–23). The psalm is a guarantee that, despite appearances, justice will ultimately prevail (see Ps. 92). The LXX has in the superscription the phrase, “for the fourth day of the week.” Ps. 94 has the earmarks of a liturgical psalm.

1.zh:
耶和華啊，你是伸冤的神；伸冤的神啊，求你發出光來！

**伸冤的上帝啊。**重複是為了強調誠懇。
**求你發出光來（yapha`）。**KJV版為“顯示自己”（見詩50:2；詩80:1）。
1.en:
**Vengeance belongeth.** The plea is repeated, emphasizing its earnestness.
**Shew thyself.** Heb. yapha‘, “shine forth with splendor” (see Ps. 50:2; Ps. 80:1).

2.zh:
審判世界的主啊，求你挺身而立，使驕傲人受應得的報應！

**求你挺身而立。**見詩7:6。
**審判世界的主。**見創18:25；詩58:11。
**使……人受應得的報應。**見詩28:4；賽3:64。
2.en:
**Lift up thyself.** See Ps. 7:6.
**Judge of the earth.** See Gen. 18:25; Ps. 58:11.
**Render a reward.** See Ps. 28:4; Lam. 3:64.

3.zh:
耶和華啊，惡人誇勝要到幾時呢？要到幾時呢？

見詩6:3；13:1。詩人倦於惡人在表面上長期佔上風，問上帝為什麼遲遲不顯示自己。
3.en: **How long?** See Ps. 6:3; 13:1. Weary with the apparent supremacy of evil, the psalmist wonders why God is so slow in manifesting Himself.

5.zh:
耶和華啊，他們強壓你的百姓，苦害你的產業。

**強壓。**或“壓碎”（見哀3:34節，參箴22:22；賽3:15）。
5.en: **Break in pieces.** Or, “crush” (see Lam. 3:34; cf. Prov. 22:22; Isa. 3:15).

6.zh:
他們殺死寡婦和寄居的，又殺害孤兒。

本節所提到的罪惡非常可憎，因為這些人軟弱而無力自衛（見詩68:5；詩82:3；出22:22-24；申10:18）。所用的語言似乎暗示是以色列內部的壓迫者。
6.en: **Slay the widow.** The crimes referred to in this verse are peculiarly detestable, because these persons are feeble and unprotected (see Ps. 68:5; Ps. 82:3; Ex. 22:22–24; Deut. 10:18). The language seems to indicate that the oppressors are within the commonwealth of Israel.

7.zh:
他們說：耶和華必不看見；雅各的神必不思念。

**他們說。**不一定是口頭上的。可能是行動上的（見詩10:11,13）。
**耶和華（Yah）。**見詩68:4註釋）。
**必不看見。**本節含有希望得到救助的傾訴和呼籲（見詩14:1,2）。
7.en:
**They say.** Not necessarily vocally, but by their conduct (see Ps. 10:11, 13).
**The Lord.** Heb. Yah (see on Ps. 68:4).
**Shall not see.** Verse 7 concludes the complaint and cry for recompense (see Ps. 14:1, 2).

8.zh:
你們民間的畜類人當思想；你們愚頑人到幾時才有智慧呢？

見詩92:6，參羅3:11。
8.en: **Brutish.** See Ps. 92:6; cf. Rom. 3:11.

11.zh:
耶和華知道人的意念是虛妄的。

**意念。**見詩7:9；26:2；參林前3:20。
原文的“虛妄”不是指“意念”，而是指人本身。
**虛妄。**見詩39:5,6；參傳2:14,15。
11.en:
**Thoughts.** See Ps. 7:9; 26:2; cf. 1 Cor. 3:20.
**They.** Masculine in the Hebrew and hence cannot refer to “thoughts,” which is feminine; men themselves are “vanity.”
**Vanity.** See Ps. 39:5, 6; cf. Eccl. 2:14, 15.

12.zh:
耶和華啊，你所管教、用律法所教訓的人是有福的！

**有福。**見詩1:1註釋。從第一眼看，這個祝福顯得十分奇怪。第12-19節描寫上帝賜給義人一系列美好的祝福。祂懲戒，訓誨，賜下平安，從不放棄，公正地審判，幫助對付惡人，在危險時扶持，安慰（見弗3:20）。詩人的經歷似乎證實了這些神聖的原則。
**管教（yasar）。**“訓練”，“糾正”，“教育”，“懲戒”。見申8:5；伯5:17；詩89:32,33；119:71；參伯33:15-30。如果基督徒接受管教，就有福了！懲戒的主要價值之一就是使接受的人更加同情別人。
**律法（torah）。**見箴3:1註釋。
12.en:
**Blessed.** See on Ps. 1:1. At first glance, this may appear to be a strange beatitude! Verses 12–19 present a remarkable galaxy of blessings that God bestows upon the righteous. He chastens, instructs, gives rest, never forsakes, judges righteously, helps against evil men, upholds in time of danger, and comforts (see Eph. 3:20). The experience of the psalmist seems to reinforce these statements of divine principle.
**Chastenest.** Heb. yasar, “discipline,” “correct,” “instruct,” “chastise.” See Deut. 8:5; Job 5:17; Ps. 89:32, 33; 119:71; cf. Job 33:15–30. If the Christian accepts discipline, he is happy! One of the chief values of chastening is that it gives the afflicted fuller sympathy with others.
**Law.** Heb. torah (see on Prov. 3:1).

13.zh:
你使他在遭難的日子得享平安；惟有惡人陷在所挖的坑中。

**使……得享平安。**心靈的平靜和安寧是接受上帝生活方式的結果。
**遭難的日子。**見詩49:5。
13.en:
**Give him rest.** Quietness and peace of mind are the result of accepting God’s way of life.
**Days of adversity.** See Ps. 49:5.

14.zh:
因為耶和華必不丟棄他的百姓，也不離棄他的產業。

不論上帝的懲戒持續多久，祂忠心的兒女都可以相信上帝絕不放棄他們的保證（見申31:6；撒上12:22；詩37:28；羅11:1,2）。
**懷愛倫註釋（14–21節）**。《先祖與先知》第456頁。
14.en: **Not cast off.** However long God’s chastising may persist, His faithful children may rest in the assurance that God will not forsake them (see Deut. 31:6; 1 Sam. 12:22; Ps. 37:28; Rom. 11:1, 2).

15.zh:
審判要轉向公義；心裡正直的，必都隨從。

**要轉向。**公義將再次證實上帝品格和政權的永恆原則。
**必都隨從。**義人將公開承認自己隨從公義。
15.en:
**Shall return.** Justice will once more conform to the eternal principles of God’s character and government.
**Shall follow it.** The upright will avow openly their allegiance to justice.

16.zh:
誰肯為我起來攻擊作惡的？誰肯為我站起抵擋作孽的？

詩人在第16-19節顯然記錄了自己的經歷。第16節提出問題，第17-19節進行回答。
16.en: **For me.** In vs. 16–19 the psalmist apparently records his own experience, beginning his personal application with a question (v. 16), which he answers in vs. 17–19.

17.zh:
若不是耶和華幫助我，我就住在寂靜之中了。

**我。**見詩16:10註釋。
**寂靜之中。**即在死亡中（見詩31:17,18；參詩115:17）。
17.en:
**My soul.** Or, “I” (see on Ps. 16:10).
**In silence.** That is, in death (see Ps. 31:17, 18; cf. Ps. 115:17).

19.zh:
我心裡多憂多疑，你安慰我，就使我歡樂。

**多憂多疑（sar`appim）。**“心裡不安”（見太6:25-34；《歷代願望》第313頁；《福山寶訓》第141-146頁）。
**安慰。**堅定地信靠上帝會消除憂慮，並代之以安慰。
**歡樂。**上帝以安慰賜給人平靜和安寧的保徵（見詩63:5,6；林後1:3,4；彼前5:7）。
**我。**見詩16:10註釋。
19.en:
**Thoughts.** Heb. śar‘appim, “disquieting thoughts” (see Matt. 6:25–34; DA 313; MB 141–146).
**Comforts.** A firm trust in God removes anxious thoughts and replaces them with “comfortable thoughts.”
**Delight.** God’s comforts give peace and calm assurance (see Ps. 63:5, 6; 2 Cor. 1:3, 4; 1 Peter 5:7).
**My soul.** Or, “me” (see on Ps. 16:10).

20.zh:
那藉著律例架弄殘害、在位上行奸惡的，豈能與你相交嗎？

**相交。**這個反問句要求否定的回答。第3,4節的問題從惡人的毀滅中得到滿意的回答。
**你。**指上帝。
**藉著律例。**他們靠著法律的條文和法庭的裁決，達到了他們邪惡的目的（見王上21:10-13）。
20.en:
**Have fellowship.** The rhetorical question demands a negative answer. The questions of vs. 3, 4 are satisfactorily answered in the destruction of the wicked.
**Thee.** God.
**By a law.** By legal statute, by court decree, they accomplish their nefarious purposes (see 1 Kings 21:10–13).

21.zh:
他們大家聚集攻擊義人，將無辜的人定為死罪。

**人。**見詩16:10註釋。
**將無辜的人定為死罪。**見詩10:8；參太27:4。
21.en:
**Soul.** See on Ps. 16:10.
**Condemn the innocent.** See Ps. 10:8; cf. Matt. 27:4.

22.zh:
但耶和華向來作了我的高臺；我的神作了我投靠的磐石。

**我的高臺。**見詩18:2。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》第413頁。
22.en: **My defence.** See Ps. 18:2.

23.zh:
他叫他們的罪孽歸到他們身上。他們正在行惡之中，他要剪除他們；耶和華─我們的神要把他們剪除。

**他們的罪孽。**見詩7:16；35:8。
**正在行惡之中。**他們正在犯罪時（見詩5:10）。
**我們的上帝。**詩人把人稱從自己（第22節）擴大到聚集崇拜的會眾。
**把他們剪除。**重複是為了強調詩歌結尾的總結（見第1節）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》第456頁。
23.en:
**Their own iniquity.** See Ps. 7:16; 35:8.
**In their own wickedness.** While they are actually committing sinful acts (see Ps. 5:10).
**Our God.** The poet extends the personal note (v. 22) to include the congregation, the people, assembled for corporate worship.
**Cut them off.** The emphatic repetition lends summary force to the conclusion of the psalm (see v. 1).

0.zh: 序言——本詩慶祝耶和華就任為全地的公義統治者，指出偶像的虛空，以及義人受到保護。起為著展示了《舊約》中上帝榮耀最輝煌的畫面之一，僅次於哈3章的詩97篇（見出19章；詩18篇）。“耶和華作王”是這首崇拜詩歌的主題。
0.en: INTRODUCTION.—Ps. 97 celebrates the enthronement of Jehovah as righteous Ruler over the whole earth, and shows that the idols are but nothing and that the righteous are vindicated. Next to the theophany (or manifestation of God’s glory) of Hab. 3, Ps. 97 presents one of the most splendid pictures of divine glory to be found in the OT (see Ex. 19; Ps. 18). “The Lord reigneth” is the theme of this liturgical psalm.

1.zh:
耶和華作王！願地快樂！願眾海島歡喜！

**耶和華作王。**見詩93:1；96:10；99:1。基督徒應當經常作出這種光榮的宣言。
**地快樂。**見詩96:1。
**眾海島。**也包括“沿海地區”。這裡顯然指地中海眾海島和沿海地區（見詩72:10；參賽60:9）。
1.en:
**The Lord reigneth.** See Ps. 93:1; 96:10; 99:1. The Christian should often make this glorious affirmation.
**Earth rejoice.** See Ps. 96:1.
**Multitude of isles.** Literally, “many isles”; the word translated “isles” may mean both “isles” and “coastlands.” Here evidently the islands and coastlands of the Mediterranean Sea are primarily referred to (see Ps. 72:10; cf. Isa. 60:9).

2.zh:
密雲和幽暗在他的四圍；公義和公平是他寶座的根基。

**密雲和幽暗。**描寫在必死的人類眼中上帝威榮的樣子。有些上帝的奧秘是人所無法測度的（見羅11:33；《教育論》第169頁；《喜樂的泉源》第111頁；《先祖與先知》第43頁）。
**公義和公平。**見詩89:14。不論邪惡如何氾濫，公義終必獲勝。
“被踐踏的真理必重新站起；
她將擁有上帝永恆的歲月；
但錯謬則受傷且痛苦地扭動，
並死在他的崇拜者之中”。
──威廉·卡倫·布賴恩特《戰場》
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督比喻實訓》第177頁；《教育論》第169頁；《先祖與先知》第43頁；《拾級就主》第111頁；《證言》卷五第197,699頁。
2.en:
**Clouds and darkness.** Descriptive of how the majesty of God reveals itself to the eyes of mortal man. There are mysteries concerning the Deity man cannot fathom (see Rom. 11:33; Ed 169; SC 111; PP 43).
**Righteousness and judgment.** See Ps. 89:14. It matters not how great the evil may be, righteousness will ultimately prevail. “Truth, crushed to earth, shall rise again; The eternal years of God are hers; But Error, wounded, writhes in pain, And dies among his worshippers.” ILLIAM ULLEN RYANT, “The Battle Field”

3.zh:
有烈火在他前頭行，燒滅他四圍的敵人。

見詩18:13；50:3。

4.en:
**His lightnings.** See Ps. 77:16–18 cf. 104:32; Hab. 3:6–10.
**The earth.** Compare Judges 5:4; Ps. 68:8; 114:7.

5.zh:
諸山見耶和華的面，就是全地之主的面，便消化如蠟。

**諸山……消化。**參士5:5；彌1:4；鴻1:5；彼後3:10；啟20:11。詩人似乎想到上帝在西奈山的顯現。
**見耶和華的面。**重複是為了強調上帝這個無限偉大的稱號（見書3:11,13；彌4:13；參亞4:14；6:5）。
5.en:
**The hills melted.** Compare Judges 5:5; Micah 1:4; Nahum 1:5; 2 Peter 3:10; Rev. 20:11. The divine manifestation at Sinai seems to be in the poet’s mind.
**Presence of the Lord.** The repetition lends emphasis to the all-inclusive title of Deity (see Joshua 3:11, 13; Micah 4:13; cf. Zech. 4:14; 6:5).

6.zh:
諸天表明他的公義；萬民看見他的榮耀。

**諸天表明。**見詩19:1；50:6註釋。
**萬民。**見第1節；參賽40:5）。
6.en:
**The heavens declare.** See on Ps. 19:1; 50:6.
**People.** Literally, “peoples” (see v. 1; cf. Isa. 40:5).

7.zh:
願一切事奉雕刻的偶像、靠虛無之神自誇的，都蒙羞愧。萬神哪，你們都當拜他。

**蒙羞愧。**描寫上帝榮耀顯現時外邦人的反應。偶像在上帝眼中是毫無能力的。
**萬神哪。**見詩82:1,6註釋。如果是指外邦的神，那只是比喻，因為這樣的神實際上並不存在。七十士譯本為：“上帝的眾天使啊，你們都當拜祂”（見對詩8:5節的註釋）。武加大譯本為“所有天使啊，你們都當拜祂”。
7.en:
**Confounded.** A description of the impression made upon the heathen when the glory of God appears. The idols are impotent before God.
**All ye gods.** See on Ps. 82:1, 6. If the gods of the heathen are referred to, it is only in figure, for these gods actually do not exist. The LXX reads: “Worship Him, all ye His angels” (see on Ps. 8:5). The Vulgate has: “Adore Him, all ye angels.”

8.zh:
耶和華啊，錫安聽見你的判斷就歡喜；猶大的城邑（原文是女子）也都快樂。

**錫安。**見詩2:6；9:14；68:16，見詩48:2註釋。本節描寫以色列人對上帝榮耀顯現的反應。錫安聽到耶和華掌權的好消息就歡欣。
**猶大的城邑（原文作女子）。**見詩48:11註釋。
**你的判斷。**他們高興不是出於報復的心理，而是因為真理的勝利。
8.en:
**Zion.** See Ps. 2:6; 9:14; 68:16; see on Ps. 48:2. Ps. 97:8 describes the impression made upon Israel when the glory of God appears. Zion rejoiced when she heard the glad things that the Lord reigned.
**Daughters of Judah.** See on Ps. 48:11.
**Because of thy judgments.** They rejoice, not vindictively, but because truth has triumphed.

9.zh:
因為你─耶和華至高，超乎全地；你被尊崇，遠超萬神之上。

**至高（`Elyon）。**見本註釋卷一173頁。詩83:18）。
**遠超萬神之上。**見詩95:3註釋。
9.en:
**High.** Heb. ‘Elyon (see Vol. I, p. 173; Ps. 83:18).
**Above all gods.** See on Ps. 95:3.

10.zh:
你們愛耶和華的，都當恨惡罪惡；他保護聖民的性命，搭救他們脫離惡人的手。

**恨惡罪惡。**詩人在結束時勸勉憎恨罪惡（見詩45:7；《基督教育之研究》第397頁，參詩34:14-22；林後6:14-18）。罪惡把我們與上帝分開。對罪惡不在乎就為撒但進入生活打開了門路。心中愛上了罪惡，就不再有真正的信仰（見箴8:13）。
**性命。**見詩16:10註釋。
**聖民（chasidim）。**見詩36篇補充註釋。
**搭救他們。**參但3:16-30；6:16-23。
**懷愛倫註釋（10–12節）**。《基督教育之研究》第397頁。
10.en:
**Hate evil.** The psalmist concludes with an exhortation to hate evil (see Ps. 45:7; CT 397; cf. Ps. 34:14–22; 2 Cor. 6:14–18). Evil separates us from God. Indifference to evil opens the way for Satan to enter the life. Where there is love of sin in the heart, there can be no real religion (see Prov. 8:13).
**Souls.** See on Ps. 16:10.
**Saints.** Heb. chasidim (see Additional Note on Ps. 36).
**Delivereth them.** Compare Dan. 3:16–30; 6:16–23.

11.zh:
散佈亮光是為義人；預備喜樂是為正直人。

**散佈（zara`）。**“播（種）”。這個比喻涉及道德問題，如“撒義種”（箴11:18），“撒罪孽”（箴22:8），“耕罪孽”（伯4:8）。人種的是什麼，收的也是什麼。這裡的“亮光”可能指所撒的種子，為誠實尋求真理的人發芽結果。“每個誠實的人都將得見真理的亮光。‘散佈亮光，乃是為義人’。只有信徒們誠懇地尋求真理，如同尋求隱藏的珍寶，教會才能在聖潔中前進”（《善惡之爭》第522頁）。
有一份希伯來語抄本不是zara`，而是zarach（“照耀”）。七十士聖經譯本，亞蘭語譯本和塔古姆譯本都是這樣譯的。Zarach在詩112:4中為“正直人在黑暗中，有光向他發現”。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《給編輯和作者的勉言》第34頁；《善惡之爭》第522頁。
11.en:
**Is sown.** From the Heb. zara‘, “to sow [as of seed in the field]”. The word is used figuratively with reference to moral subjects, as to sow “righteousness” (Prov. 11:18), “iniquity” (Prov. 22:8), “wickedness” (Job 4:8)—things which, when sown, may produce a corresponding harvest. “Light” may here be conceived of as a seed sown, ready to spring forth and bear fruit for the honest seeker after truth. “Every truly honest soul will come to the light of truth. ‘Light is sown for the righteous.’ And no church can advance in holiness unless its members are earnestly seeking for truth as for hid treasure” (GC 522).
Instead of zara‘ one Hebrew manuscript has zarach, “to shine forth.” This reading is supported by the LXX, the Syriac, and the Targums. Zarach is used in Ps. 112:4 in the statement, “Unto the upright there ariseth light.”

12.zh:
你們義人當靠耶和華歡喜，稱謝他可記唸的聖名。

**歡喜。**詩32:11；33:1。
**稱謝。**詩30:4。人最大的快樂應該是認識到有一位上帝。祂是地上兒女的父親。
12.en:
**Rejoice.** Ps. 32:11; 33:1.
**Give thanks.** Ps. 30:4. Man’s highest joy should be in the knowledge that there is a God, and that He is the Father of His earthly children.

0.zh:
序言——本詩呼籲各國各民，自然萬物都讚美宇宙的主宰和審判者上帝（見詩93,95篇序言）。本詩被稱為詩96篇的回聲，但格式更加規範。其三段的長短是一樣的，各有一個題旨：讚美的理由（第1-3節），讚美的方式（第4-6節）和讚美的邀請（第7-9節）。本詩的語言明快而流暢。
關於本詩的題記，見本冊註釋第627頁（《詩篇》序言）。
一篇詩。
0.en:
INTRODUCTION.—Ps. 98 is a superb call to all peoples and to all the forces of nature to praise God, the Sovereign-Judge of the universe (see Introduction to Ps. 93, 95). The psalm has been called an echo of Ps. 96, although it exhibits a more definite pattern of form than that psalm. Three stanzas of similar length, each presenting a unified idea, are clearly discernible: reason for praise (vs. 1–3), manner of praising (vs. 4–6), invitation to praise (vs. 7–9). The psalm has great freshness and spontaneity of spirit.
On the superscription see p. 627.

1.zh:
（一篇詩。）你們要向耶和華唱新歌！因為他行過奇妙的事；他的右手和聖臂施行救恩。

**新歌。**見詩33:3；96:1。1-3節說明讚美耶和華的理由。本詩一開始就是激昂的讚美。
**奇妙的事。**總體的祝福和特殊的祝福（見出15:11,21；詩77:14）。
**右手。**詩44:3；參出15:6；賽52:10；59:16；63:5。
1.en:
**A new song.** Ps. 33:3; 96:1. Verses 1–3 state the reasons for praising Jehovah. The psalm begins on a sublime note of praise.
**Marvellous things.** General blessings and particular benefits (see Ex. 15:11, 21; Ps. 77:14).
**Right hand.** Ps. 44:3; cf. Ex. 15:6; Isa. 52:10; 59:16; 63:5.

2.zh:
耶和華發明瞭他的救恩，在列邦人眼前顯出公義；

**發明了。**通過拯救的行動（見賽52:10）。
**列邦人。**或“各國”（見詩2:1註釋）。上帝公開的行動是為了讓以色列周圍的國家能夠看見祂的大能（見詩97:6）。
2.en:
**Hath made known.** By acts of deliverance (see Isa. 52:10).
**Openly.** Literally, “before the eyes.”
**Heathen.** Or, “nations” (see on Ps. 2:1). God’s acts were so public that all the nations around Israel could see His power (see Ps. 97:6).

3.zh:
記念他向以色列家所發的慈愛，所憑的信實。地的四極都看見我們神的救恩。

**所發的慈愛，所憑的信實。**見詩25:10；26:3。
**地的四極。**見賽52:10；參詩98:2；路2:10；3:6；羅10:12,18。
3.en:
**His mercy and his truth.** See Ps. 25:10; 26:3.
**Ends of the earth.** See Isa. 52:10; cf. Ps. 98:2; Luke 2:10; 3:6; Rom. 10:12, 18.

4.zh:
全地都要向耶和華歡樂；要發起大聲，歡呼歌頌！

**歡樂。**見詩66:1；詩95:1；100:1。第4-6節說明讚美耶和華的方式。
**全地。**本詩的特色是向世界各國呼籲。
**歌頌（zamar）。**指聲樂或器樂，或二者相結合。賦有靈性的受造之物應當讚美上帝。人類擁有可以讚美的聲音，和製造樂器讚美祂的本領。
4.en:
**Joyful noise.** See Ps. 66:1; Ps. 95:1; 100:1. Verses 4–6 state the manner of praising Jehovah.
**All the earth.** The psalm is distinguished by its universal appeal to all peoples.
**Sing praise.** Heb. zamar, “make melody,” either with voice or instrument, or both. Spiritually endowed creatures should consciously show forth the praise of God—men have voices with which to sound His praise and are gifted with the ability to make instruments with which to praise Him.

5.zh:
要用琴歌頌耶和華，用琴和詩歌的聲音歌頌他！

關於第5,6節裡所提到的樂器，見本冊註釋第30,34,39頁。
5.en: **Harp.** On the musical instruments mentioned in vs. 5, 6 see pp. 30, 34, 39.

6.zh:
用號和角聲，在大君王耶和華面前歡呼！

這裡沒有“弱音小提琴”。所有的樂器都發出最大的音量。
6.en: **A joyful noise.** There are no “muted violins” here; “all the stops of the organ are pulled out in full diapason.”

7.zh:
願海和其中所充滿的澎湃；世界和住在其間的也要發聲。

見詩96:11。第7-9節邀請整個自然界讚美耶和華。
7.en: **Sea roar.** See Ps. 96:11. Verses 7–9 extend an invitation to all nature to join in the praise of Jehovah.

8.zh:
願大水拍手；願諸山在耶和華面前一同歡呼；

**願大水拍手。**擬人的手法，可能指岸邊的驚濤駭浪。
**願諸山……歡呼。**參詩65:9-13。細膩地展示大自然以其全部的美來讚美上帝。
8.en:
**Floods clap.** A personification perhaps suggested by the breaking waves on the shore.
**Hills be joyful.** Compare Ps. 65:9–13 for an exquisite picture of nature in all her beauty praising God.

9.zh:
因為他來要審判遍地。他要按公義審判世界，按公正審判萬民。

見詩96:13註釋。贖民和自然萬物都以莫可言喻的渴望，期待著審判救贖的時刻。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《衛生勉言》第303頁。
9.en: **He cometh.** See on Ps. 96:13. The redeemed and all the works of nature look forward with unspeakable anticipation to the time of the redemptive judgment.

0.zh: 序言——本詩歡慶耶和華的王權，呼籲全人類承認祂的偉大並崇拜祂，因為祂本為聖。這首詩歌用不同的方式重複了詩93,97篇的信息。這三篇的開頭都是“耶和華作王”。本詩和第93篇一樣，特別強調聖潔為上帝的主要品性和要求（見詩93:5；詩99:3,5,9）。在本詩美妙的結構中有兩個較長的副歌（第一段和第三段的結尾稍有不同：在第5和9節），三個較短的副歌（第3,5,9節），第三次出現時為擴大為“耶和華我們的上帝本為聖”。
0.en: INTRODUCTION.—Ps. 99 celebrates the kingship of Jehovah, calling on all men to confess His greatness and worship Him who alone is holy. The psalm repeats the message of Ps. 93, 97 in varied form—all three begin with the phrase, “The Lord reigneth”—and like Ps. 93, puts special emphasis on holiness as God’s chief attribute and requirement (see Ps. 93:5; Ps. 99:3, 5, 9). The intricately beautiful structure of Ps. 99 reveals two greater refrains (in slightly varied form, at the end of the first and third stanzas: vs. 5, 9), and three lesser refrains (vs. 3, 5, 9), augmented to “the Lord our God is holy” in its third occurrence.

1.zh:
耶和華作王；萬民當戰抖！他坐在二基路伯上，地當動搖。

**耶和華作王。**見詩93:1；96:10；97:1。
**萬民。**直譯是，“各國”。
**戰抖。**當耶和華顯示祂王權的時候，人類都在祂前面戰抖（見賽64:2）。
**二基路伯上。**見詩80:1；《證言》卷五754頁。
**動搖。**參詩77:18；114:7。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先知與君王》第176頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–3節）**。《服務真詮》第438頁；《證言》卷八第285頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–5節）**。《先知與君王》第29頁。
1.en:
**The Lord reigneth.** See Ps. 93:1; 96:10; 97:1.
**The people.** Literally, “the peoples.”
**Tremble.** When Jehovah manifests His kingship, men tremble before Him (see Isa. 64:2).
**Between the cherubims.** See Ps. 80:1; 5T 754.
**Be moved.** Compare Ps. 77:18; 114:7.

2.zh:
耶和華在錫安為大；他超乎萬民之上。

**在錫安為大。**見詩48:1,2註釋；參詩95:3。
**萬民。**直譯是“各國”，即各民族。以錫安為首都的上帝統治著各國。
2.en:
**Great in Zion.** See on Ps. 48:1, 2; cf. Ps. 95:3.
**The people.** Literally, “the peoples,” that is, the nations. The God who has His capital in Zion rules all nations.

3.zh:
他們當稱讚他大而可畏的名；他本為聖！

**可畏的名。**見詩111:9；見詩5:11；7:17註釋；參申28:58。
**他（hu'）。**可以指“名”，代表耶和華的品性，也可以指“耶和華”。“他本為聖”與第5,9節所重複的副歌比較一致。兩種譯法沒有實質性的區別。聖潔是上帝的崇高品性之一。聖潔也是對上帝兒女的要求（見利19:2）。這裡第一次出現短副歌（見本詩序言，另見第5,9節）。
3.en:
**Terrible name.** See Ps. 111:9; see on Ps. 5:11; 7:17; cf. Deut. 28:58.
**It.** Heb. hu’, which may refer either to “name,” representing Jehovah’s essential character, or, to “Lord,” in which case it should be translated “he.” The translation “He is holy” is more consistent with the repetition of the refrain in vs. 5, 9. There is no essential difference in the two translations. Holiness is one of God’s supreme attributes. Holiness is also demanded of God’s children (see Lev. 19:2). This is the first appearance of the lesser refrain (see Introduction to Ps. 99; also vs. 5, 9).

4.zh:
王有能力，喜愛公平，堅立公正，在雅各中施行公平和公義。

本節第一個分句可能與前面的句子相連，可譯為“他聖潔而有能力，是喜愛公義的王”。王明顯就是耶和華（見第1節）。上帝品格的主要特徵就是喜愛公義（見賽61:8）。
原文在最後一個分句前還有“你” ，強調天上的君王和地上國王的區別。
4.en:
**The king’s strength.** The first clause of v. 4 should probably be connected with the preceding thought and the passage rendered, “He is holy and strong, a King loving justice.” The king is evidently Jehovah (see v. 1). The essential strength of God’s character is in favor of justice (see Isa. 61:8).
**Thou.** Emphatic in the Hebrew, probably to show the contrast between the great King and earthly kings.

5.zh:
你們當尊崇耶和華─我們的神，在他腳凳前下拜。他本為聖！

**當尊崇。**見詩30:1；詩34:3。本節第一次出現長副歌（見本詩序言，另見第9節）。
**他本為聖。**第二次出現短副歌（見第3節註釋）。“他”的原文也可指上帝的腳凳。在烏加列語宗教文獻中（見本冊註釋第618頁），神的腳凳是神裝備的重要部分。
5.en:
**Exalt.** See Ps. 30:1; Ps. 34:3. The verse constitutes the first appearance of the greater refrain (see Introduction to Ps. 99; also v. 9).
**For he is holy.** The second occurrence of the lesser refrain (see on v. 3). The clause may be translated, “for it is holy,” in which case “it” would refer to God’s footstool. In Ugaritic religious literature (see p. 618) the footstool of deity is an important part of the divine furnishings.

6.zh:
在他的祭司中有摩西和亞倫；在求告他名的人中有撒母耳。他們求告耶和華，他就應允他們。

**摩西和亞倫。**本節以詩歌的手法，突然轉到列舉聖潔之人的範例。他們敬拜上帝，為同胞代求，祈禱得到應允。其含義是所有的人，無論是祭司還是百姓，都要敬拜耶和華。今天上帝也呼喚為同胞代求的人。
雖然摩西一般不算祭司，但這裡卻把他列在其中，可能是因為他是屬靈的領袖，從事與聖所有關的工作（見出24:6-8；32:30-32；40:18-33；利8:6-30）。
**撒母耳。**這裡特別提到撒母耳，和摩西一樣，能通過祈禱與上帝相交（見耶15:1：參撒上7:8,9；撒上12:19-23）。
**名。**見詩7:17註釋。
6.en:
**Moses and Aaron.** With startling poetic abruptness, this verse presents examples of representative holy men who worshiped God, interceded for their fellows, and received answers to their prayers. The implication is that all—priests and people—should worship Jehovah. God calls for great interceders today.
Though not generally regarded as a priest, Moses is here numbered among the priests perhaps because of his position of spiritual leadership and because of his work in connection with the sanctuary (see Ex. 24:6–8; 32:30–32; 40:18–33; Lev. 8:6–30).
**Samuel.** Samuel is particularly mentioned, along with Moses, as having power with God in prayer (see Jer. 15:1; cf. 1 Sam. 7:8, 9; 1 Sam. 12:19–23).
**Name.** See on Ps. 7:17.

7.zh:
他在雲柱中對他們說話；他們遵守他的法度和他所賜給他們的律例。

**雲柱。**見出33:9；民12:5。
**遵守。**他們遵守上帝的律法，上帝也應允了他們的禱告。順從上帝的旨意是禱告蒙應允的條件。
7.en:
**Cloudy pillar.** See Ex. 33:9; Num. 12:5.
**They kept.** They obeyed God’s laws, and He answered their prayers. Obedience to the divine will is the condition of answered prayer.

8.zh:
耶和華─我們的神啊，你應允他們；你是赦免他們的神，卻按他們所行的報應他們。

**赦免。**摩西和亞倫都犯過罪，但是上帝憑著祂的憐憫赦免了他們（見出32:1-24；民20:12,13；參詩106:32）。“他們”可能指一般百姓。
**報應。**上帝的懲罰甚至涉及第6節所提到的聖潔的人。摩西和亞倫因為在米利巴的罪而不得進入迦南（見民20:12）。
**按他們所行的。**指他們自作主張的行為。參傳7:29。
8.en:
**That forgavest.** Both Moses and Aaron sinned, but God in His mercy forgave (see Ex. 32:1–24; Num. 20:12, 13; cf. Ps. 106:32). “Them” probably refers to the people generally.
**Tookest vengeance.** God’s chastisement extended even to holy men mentioned in v. 6. Moses and Aaron were excluded from Canaan for their sin at Meribah (see Num. 20:12).
**Inventions.** Literally, “deeds”; the context suggests self-willed activities. Compare Eccl. 7:29.

9.zh:
你們要尊崇耶和華─我們的神，在他的聖山下拜，因為耶和華─我們的神本為聖！

**尊崇耶和華。**第9節是第二次出現長副歌，稍有變動（見第5節註釋）。
**他的聖山。**指全國崇拜的中心錫安（見詩48:2註釋）。
**耶和華我們的上帝本為聖。**第三次出現短副歌，增加了“耶和華我們的上帝”（見第3,5節註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《服務真詮》第415頁；《證言》卷八第264頁。
9.en:
**Exalt the Lord.** Verse 9 is the second appearance of the greater refrain, in slightly modified form (see on v. 5).
**His holy hill.** Zion, the seat of national worship (see on Ps. 48:2).
**Lord our God is holy.** The third occurrence of the lesser refrain, augmented (see on vs. 3, 5).

0.zh:
序言——這是七篇懺悔詩中最傷心的一首，似乎是流亡者在被擄之地的祈禱。本詩以哀歌的語調錶達了在迫害而懦弱中的痛苦和悲傷。但它也含有擺脫囚擄，精神復甦的盼望。本詩在兩種意念之間搖擺。最後的語氣是堅信上帝永遠保護人類。本詩分為四段：前言（第1,2節），傾訴（第3-11節），安慰（第12-22節）和總結（第23-28節）。末世的基督徒也可以用本詩來表達所受的試煉，在最沮喪的時刻從中得到天上安慰的保證。
“困苦人發昏的時候,在耶和華面前吐露苦情的禱告。”這樣的題記在《詩篇》中是唯一的，表達了本詩的特點和宗旨（見本冊註釋第624,628頁）。
困苦人發昏的時候，在耶和華面前吐露苦情的禱告。
0.en:
INTRODUCTION.—Ps. 102 is one of the saddest of the seven penitential psalms. It appears to be the prayer of the exile composed in the land of his captivity. In elegiac strains it tells of pain and sorrow, of persecution and faintheartedness. But it does more than that; it recognizes hope in return from captivity and restoration of spirit. The poem swings between the two ideas, but closes on a sublime note of confidence in God’s eternal constancy in His dealings with the children of men. The psalm falls into four parts: introduction (vs. 1, 2), complaint (vs. 3–11), consolation (vs. 12–22), conclusion (vs. 23–28). In it the latter-day Christian may find expression for his trials and the assurance of heavenly consolation in times of unusual distress.
The superscription, “A Prayer of the afflicted, when he is overwhelmed, and poureth out his complaint before the Lord,” is unique among the superscriptions to the psalms. It characterizes the psalm and designates the purpose for which it was composed (see pp. 624, 628).

1.zh:
（困苦人發昏的時候，在耶和華面前吐露苦情的禱告。）耶和華啊，求你聽我的禱告，容我的呼求達到你面前！

見詩18:6；39:12。

2.zh:
我在急難的日子，求你向我側耳；不要向我掩面！我呼求的日子，求你快快應允我！

**不要向我掩面。**見詩4:6；13:1。
**快快。**見詩69:17。第1,2節連續向上帝求助，強調了詩人沮喪之深和呼籲之強烈。
2.en:
**Hide not.** See Ps. 4:6; 13:1.
**Speedily.** See Ps. 69:17. The depth of the psalmist’s dejection and the intensity of his appeal are emphasized by the cumulative pleas for divine aid in vs. 1, 2.

3.zh:
因為，我的年日如煙雲消滅；我的骨頭如火把燒著。

本節是詩人傾訴的開始。
3.en: **For.** Verse 3 marks the beginning of the psalmist’s complaint.

4.zh:
我的心被傷，如草枯乾，甚至我忘記吃飯。

見伯33:20；詩107:18。
4.en: **Forget to eat.** See Job 33:20; Ps. 107:18.

5.zh:
因我唉哼的聲音，我的肉緊貼骨頭。

見伯19:20；哀4:8。
5.en: **My bones cleave.** See Job 19:20; Lam. 4:8.

6.zh:
我如同曠野的鵜鶘；我好像荒場的鴞鳥。

**鵜鶘（qa'ath）。**見賽34:11；番2:14。確切的物種尚未確定。但據說鵜鶘象徵極端的孤獨和悲哀。
6.en: **Pelican.** Heb. qa’ath, translated “cormorant” in Isa. 34:11; Zeph. 2:14. The exact species of bird referred to is not known, although it has been observed that the pelican is an appropriate symbol of utter loneliness and melancholy.

7.zh:
我警醒不睡；我像房頂上孤單的麻雀。

**儆醒不睡。**英文KJV版為“觀察”。
**麻雀（sippor）。**泛指鳥類（見創7:14；申4:17）。“孤單”可能指喪失偶的鳥。
7.en:
**I watch.** Or, “I am wakeful.”
**Sparrow.** Heb. sippor, a general term for winged animals (see Gen. 7:14; Deut. 4:17). “Alone” is perhaps an allusion to a bird bereft of its mate.

9.zh:
我吃過爐灰，如同吃飯；我所喝的與眼淚攙雜。

見書7:6；伯2:7,8；哀3:16。關於烏加列語的平行結構，見詩42:3註釋。
9.en: **Ashes.** See Joshua 7:6; Job 2:7, 8; Lam. 3:16. For Ugaritic parallels see on Ps. 42:3.

11.zh:
我的年日如日影偏斜；我也如草枯乾。

生動地比喻死亡的臨近（見伯14:2）。撒母耳·巴特勒(Samuel Butler)說過，“我的時光在我身上流逝，就像水在篩子裡流失一樣”。
11.en: **Shadow that declineth.** A striking figure of the approach of death (see Job 14:2). Samuel Butler said, “My years slip through me as water through a sieve.”

12.zh:
惟你─耶和華必存到永遠；你可記唸的名也存到萬代。

**惟你。**詩人突然從默想上帝永恆的統治中得到安慰，超脫了自己的抱怨。上帝是不變的。祂的應許是真實的。儘管祂表面上的不關心曾使詩人難過了一段時間。
**必存。**見詩9:7；哀5:19。
**記念。**見出3:15；詩135:13。
12.en:
**But thou.** Abruptly, the psalmist finds consolation in the contemplation of the eternal sovereignty of God, and rises above his complaint. Because God does not change, His promises are sure, despite His apparent disregard for the psalmist’s suffering for the time being.
**Shalt endure.** See Ps. 9:7; Lam. 5:19.
**Remembrance.** See Ex. 3:15; Ps. 135:13.

14.zh:
你的僕人原來喜悅他的石頭，可憐他的塵土。

流亡者甚至一想到原本輝煌的城市耶路撒冷的廢墟也背感親切，因為他們深愛著錫安（見尼4:2,10；詩79:1）。本節洋溢著懷舊的感傷。我們兒時故居的殘垣斷壁也令人感到親切。
14.en: **Stones.** The exiles even enjoy contemplating the piled-up stones and dust of what was once their glorious city Jerusalem, so deeply in love with Zion are they (see Neh. 4:2, 10; Ps. 79:1). There is a pathetic touch of nostalgia in the concept of this verse. Even the ruins of our childhood home are dear to us.

15.zh:
列國要敬畏耶和華的名；世上諸王都敬畏你的榮耀。

根據上帝的計劃，修復後的錫安將住著一班百姓。他們將實行上帝選擇以色列人的旨意。佈道的活動將使許多外邦人悔改。新國家的繁榮將吸引許多的民族。但以色列人不幸失敗了。如果他們忠於職守，全地就會準備好迎接基督的第一次降臨（《先知與君王》第703,704頁；又本註釋卷四第26-30頁）。
**懷愛倫註釋（15–22節）**。《先知與君王》第370頁。
15.en: **Shall fear.** According to God’s plan, restored Zion would compose a people fulfilling the divine destiny in the choice of Israel. Missionary activities would convert many of the heathen and the prosperity of the new state would attract many nations. Unfortunately Israel failed. Had they been faithful the whole earth would have been prepared for the first advent of Christ (PK 703, 704; see also Vol. IV, pp. 26–30).

16.zh:
因為耶和華建造了錫安，在他榮耀裡顯現。

彌賽亞本來會降臨恢復了的國度中（見第15節註釋；另見本註釋卷四《舊約預言中以色列的地位》）。
16.en: **He shall appear.** The Messiah would have come to the restored state (see on v. 15; also see article, “The Role of Israel in Old Testament Prophecy,” Vol. IV).

18.zh:
這必為後代的人記下，將來受造的民要讚美耶和華。

**記下。**這似乎《詩篇》中唯一提到記下上帝的旨意。
**耶和華（Yah）。**見詩68:4註釋）。
18.en:
**Written.** This seems to be the only mention in the psalms where the record of God’s providences is said to be written.
**Lord.** Heb. Yah (see on Ps. 68:4).

19.zh:
因為，他從至高的聖所垂看；耶和華從天向地觀察，

見申26:15註釋。又見詩14:2。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《服務真詮》第438頁；《證言》卷八第285頁。
19.en: **From heaven.** See on Deut. 26:15; also see Ps. 14:2.

20.zh:
要垂聽被囚之人的歎息，要釋放將要死的人，

**將要死的人。**直譯是“死亡之子”（見詩79:11）。
20.en: **Those that are appointed to death.** Literally, “children of death” (see Ps. 79:11).

21.zh:
使人在錫安傳揚耶和華的名，在耶路撒冷傳揚讚美他的話，

**名。**見詩5:11；7:17註釋。
21.en: **Name.** See on Ps. 5:11; 7:17.

23.zh:
他使我的力量中道衰弱，使我的年日短少。

詩人從上帝永遠的統治中得到安慰。他又回想到自己的軟弱和人生的短暫。但這只是在剎那間。他幾乎馬上就想起了上帝的永恆不變。
