23.en: **My strength.** From the consolation of God’s eternal sovereignty the psalmist falls back again for an instant on his own weakness and the shortness of his life—but it is only for an instant. Almost immediately he is swallowed up again in the contemplation of the unchangeableness of God.

24.zh:
我說：我的神啊，不要使我中年去世。你的年數世世無窮！

詩人的祈禱顯然部分是由於要看見耶路撒冷修復的願望。他不想在希望實現之前就死去。面對上帝的永生，他感到自己的日子十分短暫，過得又快（見第11,12；詩90:2；哈1:12）。
24.en: **In the midst.** The psalmist’s prayer is evidently prompted in part by his desire to see the restoration of Jerusalem. He cannot bear the thought of dying before seeing the fulfillment of his hopes. In the face of God’s eternal existence he feels how fleeting and transient are his own days (see vs. 11, 12; Ps. 90:2; Hab. 1:12).

25.zh:
你起初立了地的根基；天也是你手所造的。

見創1:1。來1:10-12引用第25-27節指基督。《希伯來書》的作者證明，上帝的兒子基督有超越天使的地位。這也證明基督是創造之主。
25.en: **Hast thou laid.** See Gen. 1:1. Verses 25–27 are quoted in Heb. 1:10–12 as an address to Christ. The writer of the epistle to the Hebrews is proving that Christ, as the Son of God, also has a place of pre-eminence above the angels. Here is proof also of the position of Christ as Creator.

26.zh:
天地都要滅沒，你卻要長存；天地都要如外衣漸漸舊了。你要將天地如裡衣更換，天地就改變了。

烏加列文獻（見本冊註釋第618頁）也把諸天比作“要穿舊”的外衣。
26.en: **Garment.** Ugaritic literature (see p. 618) also compares the heavens to a garment that “will wear away.”

0.zh:
序言——本詩是以色列民族的讚歌（見詩78；詩106），敘述上帝如何帶領以色列人，從亞伯拉罕及其子孫的時代直到征服迦南，強調上帝與以色列所立的約。本詩描寫約瑟是埃及和迦南之間的連環。詩歌的古式格律以一系列歡快的對句展開，簡樸的平行結構莊嚴有力。
本詩1-15節實際上與代上16:8-36所記載詩歌的8-22節是一樣的。那是一首大衛的詩，慶祝約櫃安放在耶路撒冷。對原作的改動可能是為了適應後來的禮拜儀式。
詩105篇和106篇是姊妹篇。應當根據《證言》卷八107-116頁，《給傳道人的證言》98頁和《懷氏傳略》第196頁的亮光研究本詩。
0.en:
INTRODUCTION.—Ps. 105 is a national hymn of Israel (see Ps. 78; Ps. 106). It illustrates God’s dealings with Israel from the times of Abraham and his descendants down to the conquest of Canaan, with emphasis on the covenant relationship between God and Israel. In the hymn Joseph is presented as the connecting link between Egypt and Canaan. The antique meter of the hymn marches on in a succession of joyous couplets, majestic in their simple parallelism.
Verses 1–15 of this psalm are practically identical with vs. 8–22 of the psalm recorded in 1 Chron. 16:8–36, which David composed for the ceremony of enshrining the ark in Jerusalem. Variations from the original form of the psalm are probably accounted for by adaptation for liturgical use at a later date.
Ps. 105, 106 are companion psalms. Ps. 105 should be studied in the light of the counsel given in 8T 107–116; TM 98; and LS 196.

1.zh:
你們要稱謝耶和華，求告他的名，在萬民中傳揚他的作為！

**你們要稱謝。**要充分認識上帝在以色列的歷史中所表現的愛。這是本詩的主題。
**他的名。**見詩7:17註釋。
**萬民。**直譯是“各國”。各國都要認識上帝的“作為”，祂的聖名（第3節），祂“奇妙的作為”（第5節）和祂的“判語”（第5節）。本詩以傳道的鐘聲開始。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–45節）**。《證言》卷八第107-109頁；《給傳道人的證言》第98頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–2節）**。《服務真詮》第101頁。
1.en:
**Give thanks.** The love of God as shown in Israel’s history demands full acknowledgment. This is the theme of the psalm.
**His name.** See on Ps. 7:17.
**People.** Literally, “peoples.” All nations are to know God’s “deeds,” His “holy name” (v. 3), His “marvellous works” (v. 5), His “judgments” (v. 5). The psalm opens with a missionary ring.

2.zh:
要向他唱詩歌頌，談論他一切奇妙的作為！

**懷愛倫註釋（2–3節）**。《服務真詮》第255頁；《先知與君王》第566頁。

4.zh:
要尋求耶和華與他的能力，時常尋求他的面。

以色列人只能依靠上帝的能力得救。我們也是。
4.en: **His strength.** Only by God’s strength was Israel saved; only thus may we be saved.

5.zh:
他僕人亞伯拉罕的後裔，他所揀選雅各的子孫哪，你們要記念他奇妙的作為和他的奇事，並他口中的判語。併於上節。

**亞伯拉罕的後裔。**第42節。
**揀選。**直譯是“所揀選的人”（見第43節）。
紀念。參申32:7。
**奇事。**本詩主要指發生在埃及的奇事（見出6:6；7:4）。
5.en:
**Remember.** Compare Deut. 32:7.
**Wonders.** Here chiefly the miracles in Egypt, as constituting much of the content of the psalm (see Ex. 6:6; 7:4).

7.zh:
他是耶和華─我們的神；全地都有他的判斷。

7-11節頌揚上帝是記住自己聖約的主。
7.en: **Our God.** Verses 7–11 extol God as the one who remembers His covenant.

8.zh:
他記念他的約，直到永遠；他所吩咐的話，直到千代─

用詩歌誇張的手法描寫時間之長（見申7:9）。
8.en: **A thousand generations.** Poetic hyperbole for a long period of time (see Deut. 7:9).

13.zh:
他們從這邦遊到那邦，從這國行到那國。

亞伯拉罕離開迦勒底的吾珥（見創11:31節到12:5節）。眾先祖被迫離開迦南（見創12:10；26:1；28:10）。
13.en: **To another.** Abraham left Ur of the Chaldees (see Gen. 11:31 to 12:5). The patriarchs were forced to migrate from Canaan (see Gen. 12:10; 26:1; 28:10).

14.zh:
他不容什麼人欺負他們，為他們的緣故責備君王，

見創12:17；20:3。
**懷愛倫註釋（14–15節）**。《先祖與先知》第131頁；《證言》卷三第94頁；《證言》卷四第229頁。
14.en: **Reproved kings.** See Gen. 12:17; 20:3.

15.zh:
說：不可難為我受膏的人，也不可惡待我的先知。

**不可難為。**見創26:11。
**受膏。**可能指蒙揀選從事特殊的任務。
**先知。**見創20:7。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先知與君王》第571頁。
15.en:
**Touch not.** See Gen. 26:11.
**Anointed.** Probably in the sense of being chosen for a special mission.
**Prophets.** See Gen. 20:7.

16.zh:
他命饑荒降在那地上，將所倚靠的糧食全行斷絕，

見創41:53-57。
16.en: **Called for a famine.** See Gen. 41:53–57.

17.zh:
在他們以先打發一個人去─約瑟被賣為奴僕。

**在他們以先。**見創45:5。
**被賣。**見創37:28,36。
17.en:
**Before them.** See Gen. 45:5.
**Sold.** See Gen. 37:28, 36.

18.zh:
人用腳鐐傷他的腳；他被鐵鍊捆拘。

**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》第218頁。

19.zh:
耶和華的話試煉他，直等到他所說的應驗了。

**耶和華的話。**直到約瑟夢見超過自己兄弟的預言應驗（見創37:5-11）。
**試煉。**指預言和應驗之間約瑟所受的試煉。
19.en:
**His word came.** That is until the prediction of Joseph’s dreams of pre-eminence over his brothers came to pass (see Gen. 37:5–11).
**Tried.** The interval between the prediction and its fulfillment was a period of test for Joseph.

20.zh:
王打發人把他解開，就是治理眾民的，把他釋放，

見創41:14,40,41,44,46-49,45:8。

21.zh:
立他作王家之主，掌管他一切所有的，

**懷愛倫註釋（21–22節）**。《教育論》第53頁；《先祖與先知》第222頁；《證言》卷六第219頁。

22.zh:
使他隨意捆綁他的臣宰，將智慧教導他的長老。

**捆綁。**七十士譯本，亞蘭語譯本和拉丁文通俗（武加大）譯本為yasar（“指教”），而不是希伯來語的'asar（“捆綁”）。它們僅是一個字母的區別。譯成“指教”使本節的兩個部分形成平行。這個觀念可以用一個埃及慣例來說明：埃及的首相要負責監督王室子女的教育。
**隨意（nephesh）。**見詩16:10註釋。與烏加列文獻的用法一致（見本冊註釋第618頁）。
**長老。**或“元老”。
22.en:
**Bind.** The LXX, Syriac, and Jerome read yasar, “to instruct,” instead of the Heb. ’asar, “to bind.” The difference consists in only one letter. Such a reading would make the first part of the verse parallel with the second. The idea might be illustrated from an Egyptian custom, according to which it was the duty of the prime minister, or vizier, to supervise the education of the royal children.
**Pleasure.** Heb. nephesh (see on Ps. 16:10). The translation “pleasure” is in harmony with Ugaritic usage (see p. 618).
**Senators.** Literally, “elders.”

23.zh:
以色列也到了埃及；雅各在含地寄居。

**在含地。**就是埃及。這是平行句（見詩78:51；見創10:6註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《服務真詮》第101頁。
23.en: **The land of Ham.** Egypt, as the parallelism shows (see Ps. 78:51; see on Gen. 10:6).

24.zh:
耶和華使他的百姓生養眾多，使他們比敵人強盛，

參出1:9-16。

25.zh:
使敵人的心轉去恨他的百姓，並用詭計待他的僕人。

**使敵人的心轉去。**聖經常常把上帝說成是做了祂所沒有制止的事情（見撒下12:11；16:22；24:1註釋；見王上12:15）。
**用詭計。**見出1:10。
25.en:
**Turned their heart.** In Bible figure, God is frequently described as doing that which He does not prevent (see on 2 Sam. 12:11; 16:22; 24:1; 1 Kings 12:15).
**Subtilly.** See Ex. 1:10.

26.zh:
他打發他的僕人摩西和他所揀選的亞倫，

**他的僕人摩西。**見出14:31；申34:5；書1:2。
**亞倫。**見出4:14-17,27。
**懷愛倫註釋（26–27節）**。《先知與君王》第16頁。
26.en:
**Moses his servant.** See Ex. 14:31; Deut. 34:5; Joshua 1:2.
**Aaron.** See Ex. 4:14–17, 27.
**27 Among them.** That is, the Egyptians.
**Ham.** See on v. 23.

27.zh:
在敵人中間顯他的神蹟，在含地顯他的奇事。

**在敵人中間。**指埃及人。
**含。**見第23節註釋。

28.zh:
他命黑暗，就有黑暗；沒有違揹他話的。

第九災（見出10:21-23）。詩人沒有按照《出埃及記》裡所記載災難的順序。
28.en: **Darkness.** The 9th plague (see Ex. 10:21–23). The psalmist does not follow the sequence of the Exodus account of the plagues.

29.zh:
他叫埃及的水變為血，叫他們的魚死了。

見出7:14-25。

30.zh:
在他們的地上以及王宮的內室，青蛙多多滋生。

見出8:1-15。

31.zh:
他說一聲，蒼蠅就成群而來，並有蝨子進入他們四境。

**蒼蠅。**見出8:20-24。
**蝨子。**見出8:16-19。

32.zh:
他給他們降下冰雹為雨，在他們的地上降下火焰。

**冰雹。**見出9:18-35。
**火焰。**見出9:23,24。

34.zh:
他說一聲，就有蝗蟲螞蚱上來，不計其數，

**蝗蟲（'arbeh）。**見出10:1-20。
**螞蚱（yeleq）。**，可以指蝗蟲還沒有長出翅膀的階段。在《出埃及記》只用了'arbeh。
34.en:
**Locusts.** Heb. ’arbeh (see Ex. 10:1–20).
**Caterpillers.** Heb. yeleq, thought to represent the unwinged stage of the locust. In the Exodus account only one word (’arbeh) is used.

36.zh:
他又擊殺他們國內一切的長子，就是他們強壯時頭生的。

見出11,12章。

37.zh:
他領自己的百姓帶銀子金子出來；他支派中沒有一個軟弱的。

**銀子金子。**見出12:35,36。以色列在離開埃及以前，索要還沒有償付的工錢（見本冊註釋第281頁）。
**沒有一個軟弱的。**直譯是“沒有蹣跚而行的”。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第824頁。
37.en:
**Silver and gold.** See Ex. 12:35, 36. Before leaving Egypt the children of Israel claimed a recompense for their unpaid labor (see PP 281).
**Not one feeble person.** Literally, “no stumbler.”

38.zh:
他們出來的時候，埃及人便歡喜；原來埃及人懼怕他們。

見出12:33。

39.zh:
他鋪張雲彩當遮蓋，夜間使火光照。

為了引路和抵擋熾熱的陽光（見出13:21；《先祖於先知》第282頁）。第39-41節記錄了曠野中三件主要的奇蹟：雲柱火柱的保護和引導；鵪鶉和嗎哪；從磐石中流出水來。沒有提到紅海。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》第282頁。
39.en: **Cloud.** To lead the way and protect from the burning sun (see Ex. 13:21; PP 282). Verses 39–41 present three of the principal miracles in the wilderness: the protection and guidance of the cloud and fire, the quails and manna, the waters gushing from the rock. The crossing of the Red Sea is not mentioned.

40.zh:
他們一求，他就使鵪鶉飛來，並用天上的糧食叫他們飽足。

**鵪鶉。**見出16:13。
**天上的糧食。**見詩78:24,25註釋。
40.en:
**Quails.** See Ex. 16:13.
**Bread of heaven.** See on Ps. 78:24, 25.

41.zh:
他打開磐石，水就湧出；在乾旱之處，水流成河。

見出17:6；參詩78:15,20。詩105:40,41節強調上帝豐富的恩賜。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》第411頁。
41.en: **Opened the rock.** See Ex. 17:6; cf. Ps. 78:15, 20. Ps. 105:40, 41 emphasize the abundance of God’s gifts.

42.zh:
這都因他記念他的聖言和他的僕人亞伯拉罕。

**懷愛倫註釋（42–45節）**。《教育論》第40頁。

43.zh:
他帶領百姓歡樂而出，帶領選民歡呼前往。

**歡呼（rinnah）。**見出15章。
**懷愛倫註釋（43–45節）**。《先祖與先知》第334頁。
43.en: **Gladness.** Heb. rinnah, “a ringing cry of joy” (see Ex. 15).

44.zh:
他將列國的地賜給他們，他們便承受眾民勞碌得來的，

**懷愛倫註釋（44–45節）**。《先知與君王》第120頁。

45.zh:
好使他們遵他的律例，守他的律法。你們要讚美耶和華！

**遵他的律例。**在末世危急的時候，我們要牢記上帝在過去的歷史中如何賜福給祂的子民，從而相應地安排我們的生活。
**要讚美耶和華。**見詩104:35註釋。
45.en:
**Keep his laws.** In the preoccupations of the last days, we do well to remember God’s blessings upon His people through all generations, and order our lives accordingly.
**Praise ye the Lord.** See on Ps. 104:35.

105.6:
**Seed of Abraham.** See v. 42.
**Chosen.** Literally, “chosen ones” (see v. 43).

0.zh:
序言——這是一首適合吟唱的民族讚歌。第一段（第1-5節）在主題和語言與詩57篇第二段相同；第二段（第6-13節）與詩60篇第二段基本一樣（關於這些詩歌的背景，分別見各自的序言）。詩108篇可能是為了禮儀從這兩首詩歌中組合而成的，用於聖殿的侍奉。
關於本詩的題記，見本冊註釋第616,627頁（《詩篇》序言）。
大衛的詩歌。
0.en:
INTRODUCTION.—Ps. 108 is of a form suitable to be sung as a national hymn. The first section (vs. 1–5) corresponds in thought and wording to the second part of Ps. 57; the second section (vs. 6–13) is practically the same as the second division of Ps. 60 (for the background of these psalms see Introduction to Ps. 57 and to Ps. 60). The respective portions of these psalms may have been combined into Ps. 108 for liturgical purposes, and so used in the Temple service.
On the superscription see pp. 616, 627.

1.zh:
（大衛的詩歌。）神啊，我心堅定；我口（原文是榮耀）要唱詩歌頌！

**心堅定。**詩人對自己的道路拿定了主意，絕不偏離。堅定的立場是人人都必須培養的一種品格。
1-5節與詩57:7-11稍有不同（見該處註釋）。
**我口（原文作榮耀）。**詩人用自己的智慧，口舌，詩歌的技巧以及音樂的天賦，來讚美上帝。他把一切才能都奉獻給他的創造主。
1.en:
**Heart is fixed.** The psalmist had determined his course and would not deviate from it. Steadfastness of purpose is a trait of character that all should cultivate.
Verses 1–5 appear with slight variation as Ps. 57:7–11 (see comments there).
**My glory.** The psalmist will render praise to God with his intellect, tongue, poetic faculty, and musical skill. He has dedicated all his talents to his Maker.

2.zh:
琴瑟啊，你們當醒起！我自己要極早醒起！

**琴瑟啊，你們當醒起。**甜美的以色列歌手不滿足於單用自己的聲音，他還要求有樂器為他的歌唱陪奏。具有音樂天賦的人有特權和責任用自己的才能來榮耀那位“施給者”。
**極早醒起。**把清晨的時間用在敬拜之中，會給一天的工作帶來力量，並提供抵擋誘惑的保障。我們的救主經常在清晨起來長時間地祈禱（見《歷代願望》第90頁；《服務真詮》第52頁；見可3:13註釋）。
2.en:
**Awake, psaltery.** The sweet singer of Israel is not satisfied to use his voice alone; he calls for musical instruments to accompany him in his songs of praise. Those with musical talent have the privilege and duty of using that gift to glorify the Giver.
**Awake early.** The early hours of the morning spent in private devotion provide strength for the day’s duties and a safeguard against temptation. The Saviour often rose to pray a great while before day (see DA 90; MH 52; see on Mark 3:13).

4.zh:
因為，你的慈愛大過諸天；你的誠實達到穹蒼。

上帝的慈愛和誠實的深厚而無邊的。地球容納不下它們。它們超越了天空。
4.en: **Above the heavens.** God’s merciful love and truth are boundless and deep. The earth cannot contain them. They stretch beyond the sky.

5.zh:
神啊，願你崇高過於諸天！願你的榮耀高過全地！

人類讚美上帝，是因為祂豐盛的慈愛。合唱的聲音應該充滿地球和一切榮耀的場所。
5.en: **Be thou exalted.** Man’s praise of God should be according to the abundance of God’s loving-kindness. The sound of the mighty chorus should fill the earth and all the courts of glory.

6.zh:
求你應允我們，用右手拯救我們，好叫你所親愛的人得救。

虔誠者的祈禱能影響許多其他的人，往往會決定整個民族的命運（見雅5:17,18）。上帝所愛的人會得到祂的拯救。
第6-13節詩60:5-12稍有不同（見該處註釋）。
6.en:
**Thy beloved.** The prayer of one godly man reaches out to many others, and often shapes the destiny of a whole nation (see James 5:17, 18). The beloved will be delivered by Him who loves them.
Verses 6–13 appear with slight variation as Ps. 60:5–12 (see comments there).

7.zh:
神已經指著他的聖潔說（說：或譯應許我）：我要歡樂；我要分開示劍，丈量疏割谷。

**指著他的聖潔。**上帝的本性是聖潔的，所以不可能違背自己的諾言（見民23:19；多1:2）。上帝說話的時候，祂的話是斬釘截鐵的。
**疏割谷。**見書13:27註釋。
7.en:
**In his holiness.** God’s nature is holy, and that nature makes it impossible for Him to break His promise (see Num. 23:19; Titus 1:2). When God speaks, His word stands fast.
**Valley of Succoth.** See on Joshua 13:27.

8.zh:
基列是我的；瑪拿西是我的；以法蓮是護衛我頭的；猶大是我的杖；

猶大是王室的支派。圭必不離開它，直等細羅(就是賜平安者)來到（見創49:10）。
8.en: **Judah is my lawgiver.** Judah was the royal tribe from which the scepter would not depart till Shiloh come (see Gen. 49:10).

9.zh:
摩押是我的沐浴盆；我要向以東拋鞋；我必因勝非利士呼喊。

**摩押是我的沐浴盆。**摩押因其驕傲而著稱（見賽16:6）。詩人在這裡把這個傲慢的民族比作器皿，讓勝利的戰士洗腳。
**非利士。**大衛在執政的早期征服了非利士人（見對撒下8:1註釋）。上帝必戰勝祂子民的一切敵人。
9.en:
**Moab is my washpot.** Moab was notorious for its pride (see Isa. 16:6). Here the psalmist compares this haughty nation to a vessel in which a victorious warrior washes his feet.
**Philistia.** Early in his reign David had subdued the Philistines (see on 2 Sam. 8:1). God will triumph over all the enemies of His people.

10.zh:
誰能領我進堅固城？誰能引我到以東地？

**堅固城。**見詩60:9註釋。詩人希望上帝幫助他攻下這個堅固城，使他的指望不致落空（見撒下8:14註釋）。
10.en: **Strong city.** See on Ps. 60:9. The psalmist looked to God to assist him to capture this stronghold, and he did not look in vain (see on 2 Sam. 8:14).

11.zh:
神啊，你不是丟棄了我們嗎？神啊，你不和我們的軍兵同去嗎？

當時上帝似乎拋棄了祂的選民，但事實並非如此。祂帶領以色列軍隊攻入了難以攻克的以東高原，使以東人臣服於以色列人（見王上11:15註釋）。如今祂也會帶領我們攻入敵人的堡壘。信靠祂的人是攻無不克的。
11.en: **Hast cast us off.** At the time, it seemed that God had forsaken His chosen people, but not so. He led the host of Israel against the impregnable heights of Edom, and they became servants of Israel (see on 1 Kings 11:15). Today He can bring us into the strong citadel of the enemy. Nothing can withstand those who trust in Him.

12.zh:
求你幫助我們攻擊敵人，因為人的幫助是枉然的。

在人無法幫助的時候，上帝會來幫助我們。在人靠不住的時候，上帝的兒女可以更加依靠無窮之主的膀臂。
12.en: **Vain.** When human assistance is of no avail, divine help comes to our aid. When confidence in man is shaken, the child of God leans the more heavily on the arm of the Infinite.

13.zh:
我們倚靠神才得施展大能，因為踐踏我們敵人的就是他。

上帝的幫助激勵我們自助。我們從祂那裡得到鼓舞，智慧和力量來戰勝仇敵。在上帝的引導下，教會可以從勝利走向勝利。
13.en: **Valiantly.** God’s help inspires us to help ourselves. From Him we derive courage, wisdom, and strength to gain the victory over our foes. With God for its leader the church may go forth conquering and to conquer.

1.zh:
（大衛的詩。）耶和華對我主說：你坐在我的右邊，等我使你仇敵作你的腳凳。

**耶和華對我主說。**即 “Yahweh 對'adoni說”（見本註釋卷一35頁）。按照耶穌的說法，這是聖父和聖子之間的對話。基督坐在宇宙至尊之處、祂天父的右邊（見弗1:20-23；參林前15:24-28）。
**腳凳。**見詩99:5註釋。
1.en:
**The Lord said unto my Lord.** Substituting the Hebrew words for “Lord” we have the following, “Yahweh said unto ’adoni” (see Vol. I, p. 35). According to Jesus’ statement the conversation occurred between God the Father and God the Son. Christ is seated in the place of highest honor in the universe, the right hand of His Father (see Eph. 1:20–23; cf. 1 Cor. 15:24–28).
**Footstool.** See on Ps. 99:5.

2.zh:
耶和華必使你從錫安伸出能力的杖來；你要在你仇敵中掌權。

**能力的杖。**象徵權柄和能力（見耶48:17）。
2.en: **Rod of thy strength.** A common symbol of authority and power (see Jer. 48:17).

3.zh:
當你掌權的日子（或譯：行軍的日子），你的民要以聖潔的妝飾為衣（或譯：以聖潔為妝飾），甘心犧牲自己；你的民多如清晨的甘露（或譯：你少年時光耀如清晨的甘露）。

**你的民……甘心。**國王在推翻錫安仇敵的大日召集軍隊的時候，會有積極的響應。百姓將樂意隨從他們的領袖。
**聖潔的裝飾。**許多希伯來語抄本，西馬庫斯譯本和武加大譯本為“聖潔的山”。若是這樣，那就是描寫錫安山為以色列軍隊集合的地點。
**甘露。**可能指軍隊的龐大（見撒下17:11,12），或指精神振奮（見詩133:3；何14:5）。
3.en:
**Thy people shall be willing.** Literally, “thy people voluntary offerings.” When the king musters his army for the great day when the enemies of Zion will be overthrown, there will be a ready response. The people will yield willing allegiance to their leader.
**Beauties of holiness.** Many Hebrew manuscripts, and Symmachus and Jerome, read, “mountains of holiness.” If this reading is correct, it pictures the mountains of Zion as the rallying point of the armies of Israel.
**The dew.** Perhaps a figure of the vastness of the army (see 2 Sam. 17:11, 12), or of freshness and vigor (see Ps. 133:3; Hosea 14:5).

4.zh:
耶和華起了誓，決不後悔，說：你是照著麥基洗德的等次永遠為祭司。

**後悔。**從起初就知道末後的主決不會改變祂的旨意（見撒上15:11註釋）。雖然人的失敗會暫時干擾上帝的計劃，但最終一切都必實現上帝原來的旨意。
**永遠為祭司。**這裡用了最有力的語言說明基督是永遠的祭司。祂是上帝的誓言所承諾的（見來7:21）。這個任命是毫無疑問的。
**麥基洗德的等次。**就像至高上帝的祭司，撒冷王麥基洗德一樣，基督既是祭司又是國王（見創14:18；來5:6,10；6:20；7:1-3,11,15,17,24,28）。
4.en:
**Repent.** He who understands the end from the beginning does not change His purpose (see on 1 Sam. 15:11). Though man’s failure may necessitate a temporary interruption of God’s plan, yet in the end all things will be carried out according to His original purpose.
**A priest for ever.** The strongest possible language is employed to show that Christ is an eternal Priest. He is so by virtue of a promise of God confirmed by an oath (see Heb. 7:21). This settles the decree beyond all question.
**Order of Melchizedek.** In Christ the priesthood and the kingship are united as they were in Melchizedek, king of Salem, priest of God (see Gen. 14:18; Heb. 5:6, 10; 6:20; 7:1–3, 11, 15, 17, 24, 28).

5.zh:
在你右邊的主，當他發怒的日子，必打傷列王。

地上有權勢的人無法抵擋上帝的作為。上帝將使自己的事業勝過地上的統治者。
5.en: **Shall strike through kings.** Earthly potentates will not be successful in opposing the work of the Lord. The Lord will make His cause to triumph over earthly rulers.

7.zh:
他要喝路旁的河水，因此必抬起頭來。

**喝路旁的河水。**可能指在艱辛的任務中得到振奮。疲憊的戰士和領導人很喜歡喝“路旁的河水”（見士7:5註釋）。
**抬起頭來。**說明一切疲憊的痕跡都消除了。領導人帶著新的活力準備出發，完成手頭的工作（見路21:28）。
7.en:
**Drink of the brook.** A figure probably suggesting refreshment in the midst of an arduous task. Weary armies and their leaders welcomed the opportunity of drinking water from a “brook in the way” (see on Judges 7:5).
**Lift up the head.** Denoting that all traces of weariness are gone, and the leader is ready to go forward with renewed vigor to accomplish the task at hand (see Luke 21:28).

110.0:
INTRODUCTION.—Ps. 110 was written by David (see Matt. 22:41–45; Mark 12:35–37; Luke 20:41–43). The psalm takes its place among the most majestic songs of Hebrew literature. It has been styled “the pearl of Messianic psalms.” Christ is presented not only as King and Ruler of this world, but also, by God’s solemn oath, as eternal Priest. Compare Zech. 6:13, where Messiah is referred to as both Priest and King.
Ugaritic parallels (see p. 618) are numerous in Ps. 110. It has been estimated that about 46 per cent of the vocabulary of all the psalms finds parallels in Ugaritic. In Ps. 110 the percentage is 71. The same high percentage is found also in Ps. 29 and 93.
On the superscription see pp. 616, 627.

0.zh:
序言——本詩共有二十二行，每行以一個希伯來字母開頭。本詩在結構與詩112篇相同，所以稱為她的姊妹篇（關於離合體詩歌，見本冊註釋第625頁，《詩篇》序言）。詩111和112篇是讚美的詩歌，以“哈利路亞”開始（見第1節註釋）。
讚美耶和華
0.en: INTRODUCTION.—Ps. 111 consists of twenty-two lines, each line beginning with a letter of the Hebrew alphabet. A similar construction is found in Ps. 112, and for this reason they have been called twin psalms (for a discussion of acrostic psalms, see p. 625). Ps. 111, 112 are psalms of praise and begin with “Hallelujah” (see on v. 1).

1.zh:
你們要讚美耶和華！我要在正直人的大會中，並公會中，一心稱謝耶和華。

**你們要讚美耶和華。**希伯來語是haleluYah（“哈利路亞”）。
1.en: **Praise ye the Lord.** Heb. halelu Yah, the expression from which “hallelujah” is derived.

2.zh:
耶和華的作為本為大；凡喜愛的都必考察。

粗心的觀察者是看不到上帝創作的細節的。只有勤懇研究，才能發現。就像礦工挖到地下去尋找寶藏，只有甘心挖掘的人才能發現上帝作為中的財富。
**懷愛倫註釋（2–4節）**。《今日的生活》第175頁。
2.en: **Sought out.** The details of God’s handiwork are not always apparent to the casual observer. They must be explored and discovered by eager study. As the miner digs in the earth to find its riches, so the works of God yield their treasure to him who is willing to dig for it.

4.zh:
他行了奇事，使人記念；耶和華有恩惠，有憐憫。

安息日是創造的紀念（創2:2,3；《歷代願望》第281頁）。先祖與先知視它為神聖的日子。上帝在西奈山宣佈祂神聖律法的時候，再次強調了安息日的神聖性(出20:8-11)。基督在世時，曾在安息日參加會堂的崇拜（見可1:21；路4:16）。使徒保羅在基督復活以後多年，也遵守第七天安息日（見徒13:14；17:2）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第281頁；《證言》卷五第74頁。
4.en: **To be remembered.** The clause reads literally, “He made a memorial [or “remembrance,” or “mention”] for his wonderful works.” The Sabbath is a memorial of creation (Gen. 2:2, 3; DA 281). The memorial was held sacred by patriarchs and prophets. God reiterated and re-emphasized the sanctity of the Sabbath when He proclaimed His holy law from Sinai (Ex. 20:8–11). When here on earth Christ worshiped in the synagogue on the Sabbath day (see Mark 1:21; Luke 4:16). The apostle Paul, years after Christ’s resurrection, observed the seventh-day Sabbath (see Acts 13:14; 17:2).

5.zh:
他賜糧食給敬畏他的人；他必永遠記念他的約。

**糧食（tereph）。**上帝曾在曠野向以色列人提供嗎哪，滿足他們的需要，祂也必將照樣在祂子民困難的時候照顧他們的需要（見賽33:16；《善惡之爭》第626,629頁）。
5.en: **Meat.** Heb. ṭereph, “food.” As God made provision for Israel’s wants in the wilderness by providing manna for them, so He will care for the needs of His people in times of distress (see Isa. 33:16; GC 626, 629).

7.zh:
他手所行的是誠實公平；他的訓詞都是確實的，

**確實（'aman）。**“確立”，“可靠”。上帝的誡命規定了人的責任和義務，是真實可靠的。誡命是永遠確立而不變的。
**懷愛倫註釋（7–8節）**。《善惡之爭》第288,434頁；《福山寶訓》第81頁；《先祖與先知》第342頁。
7.en: **Sure.** From the Heb. ’aman, “to be firmly established,” “to be trustworthy.” The commandments of God, in which man’s duties are set forth, are trustworthy and true. They remain steadfast forever, they are unchangeable.

8.zh:
是永永遠遠堅定的，是按誠實正直設立的。

上帝統治宇宙的原則是不變的。上帝“沒有改變，也沒有轉動的影兒”（雅1:17）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《教育論》第30頁。
8.en: **They stand fast.** The Lord has certain immutable principles by which He governs the universe. With God there “is no variableness, neither shadow of turning” (James 1:17).

9.zh:
他向百姓施行救贖，命定他的約，直到永遠；他的名聖而可畏。

**可畏（yara'）。**指“敬畏”人（創50:19）或上帝（申6:13）。Nora'在《舊約》中共出現44次（參申7:21；尼1:5；代上16:25；詩96:4；但9:4；詩89:7譯為“大有威嚴”）。Nora'一般是針對上帝，但也可針對事物或行為（出34:10；申8:15；詩45:4等），然而顯然是指上帝的作為。nora'除了兩次指百姓以外（賽18:2,7），都不是針對人的。關於名號“可畏”的使用，見《歷代願望》第613頁。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《兒童教育指南》第538頁；《歷代願望》第613頁；《教育論》第243頁；《佈道論》第133頁；《早期著作》第70,122頁；《傳道良助》第178頁；《福山寶訓》第157頁；《今日的生活》第282頁；《先知與君王》第49,236頁；《先祖與先知》第307頁；《證言》卷一第410頁。
9.en: **Reverend.** From the Heb. yara’, “to fear,” either man (Gen. 50:19) or God (Deut. 6:13). The form of the verb here used, nora’, means literally, “to be feared,” or “to be reverenced.” Nora’ occurs 44 times, but is rendered “reverend” only here. Elsewhere it is generally translated “terrible” (Deut. 7:21; Neh. 1:5; etc.). It is also translated “to be feared” (1 Chron. 16:25; Ps. 96:4), “dreadful” (Dan. 9:4), and “to be had in reverence” (Ps. 89:7). Nora’, though generally applied to God, is used also of things or acts (Ex. 34:10; Deut. 8:15; Ps. 45:4; etc.), though seemingly with reference to divine acts. Nora’ is nowhere applied to human beings except in two instances, where it is applied to a nation (Isa. 18:2, 7), but even here the appellation seems to be used with reference to the acts of God. On the use of the title “reverend” see DA 613.

10.zh:
敬畏耶和華是智慧的開端；凡遵行他命令的是聰明人。耶和華是永遠當讚美的！

**懷愛倫註釋**。《兒童教育指南》第23,87,316,493頁；《基督教育之研究》第108,502頁；《安息日學訓言》第21頁；《佈道論》第136頁；《基督教育之研究》第136,169,328,381頁；《給青年人的信息》第27,190,290,329頁；《先知與君王》第34頁；《給傳道人的證言》第161；《證言》卷三第491頁；《證言》卷四第27,208,425,553頁；《證言》卷五第84頁；《證言》卷八第199頁（見箴9:10節更多註釋）。

0.zh: 序言——詩113-118篇組成“哈列”（頌讚詩），在猶太人的重大節日裡詠唱。在逾越節，詩113篇和詩114篇在就餐之前唱，詩115-118篇在就餐之後唱。耶穌和祂的門徒在祂被出賣的那天晚上，在樓上唱的就是這些詩篇的段落（太26:30；可14:26；《教育論》第166頁；《歷代願望》第672頁）。本詩分為三段，每段有三節。
0.en: INTRODUCTION.—Ps. 113–118 constitute the Hallel, which is recited at the great feasts of the Jews. During the Passover, Ps. 113 and Ps. 114 were sung before the repast and Ps. 115–118 after the repast. Stanzas from these psalms were sung by Jesus and the disciples in the upper room the night of the betrayal (Matt. 26:30; Mark 14:26; Ed 166; DA 672). Ps. 113 consists of three equal stanzas, each of which contains three verses.

1.zh:
你們要讚美耶和華！耶和華的僕人哪，你們要讚美，讚美耶和華的名！

**你們要讚美耶和華。**見詩104:35；111:1註釋，另見詩148；150篇。
1.en: **Praise ye the Lord.** See on Ps. 104:35; Ps. 111:1; see also Ps. 148; 150.

2.zh:
耶和華的名是應當稱頌的，從今時直到永遠！

**懷愛倫註釋（2–3節）**。《教育論》第166頁。

3.zh:
從日出之地到日落之處，耶和華的名是應當讚美的！

從清晨到晚上，以色列軍營中傳出讚美的歌聲。今日上帝子民的聚會也當如此。不感激上天的福惠，往往是背道的開始（羅1:20-22）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》第342頁。
3.en: **Unto the going down.** From early morning until late evening the song of praise was heard ascending from Israel’s encampment. So it should be at the gatherings of God’s people today. A lack of gratitude for the blessings of Heaven often marks the start of apostasy (Rom. 1:20–22).

4.zh:
耶和華超乎萬民之上；他的榮耀高過諸天。

描繪上帝在諸天之中登基，萬國都受祂統治（見但2:21）。
4.en: **All nations.** God is pictured as enthroned in the heavens, with all nations under His control (see Dan. 2:21).

5.zh:
誰像耶和華─我們的神呢？他坐在至高之處，

**懷愛倫註釋（5–6節）**。《教育論》第132頁；《服務真詮》第435頁；《證言》卷八第283頁。

6.zh:
自己謙卑，觀看天上地下的事。

雖然上帝擁有榮耀的威嚴，但祂不放過任何小事。卑微軟弱的人類知道了宇宙的主宰關心著他們生活中的一切事務，那該有多大的安慰啊！這個偉大的真理所包含的意義，是人間的哲學所無法測度的。
6.en: **Humbleth himself.** With all God’s glorious majesty, there is nothing too small to pass His notice. What a comfort to weak and frail humanity to know that the Master of the universe is interested in all the affairs of our lives! This great truth has a depth of meaning that no human philosophy can ever fathom.

7.zh:
他從灰塵裡抬舉貧寒人，從糞堆中提拔窮乏人，

描寫救人脫離極端的貧困和孤獨。
7.en: **Out of the dunghill.** A picture of deliverance from extreme poverty and social isolation.

8.zh:
使他們與王子同坐，就是與本國的王子同坐。

指蹄升到最尊貴的地位（見伯36:7；見撒下9:7註釋）。上帝把最卑微的人從深坑提拔到最高的位置上。
8.en: **With princes.** A figure suggesting elevation to the highest rank and dignity (see Job 36:7; see on 2 Sam. 9:7). The Lord lifts the truly humble from the lowest pit and causes him to dwell on the highest place.

9.zh:
他使不能生育的婦人安居家中，為多子的樂母。你們要讚美耶和華！

參哈拿的故事（撒上1章）。
9.en: **Joyful mother.** Compare the experience of Hannah (1 Sam. 1).

0.zh: 序言——本詩結構嚴謹，形象生動，分為兩段，各有兩節，語言簡潔厄要。
0.en: INTRODUCTION.—Ps. 114 is noted for its perfection of form and dramatic vividness. This poem consists of four stanzas of two verses each. In each stanza the dominant note is set forth in terse language.

2.zh:
那時，猶大為主的聖所，以色列為他所治理的國度。

原文動詞為陰性。本節的分行是按韻律，而不是依據邏輯。“猶大”和“以色列”並沒有進行對照。
2.en: **Judah.** Here, the land of Judah, as shown by the feminine form of the Hebrew verb. The division of the lines in this verse is rhythmical, not logical. There is no contrast intended between the words “Judah” and “Israel.”

3.zh:
滄海看見就奔逃；約但河也倒流。

**滄海看見。**這裡用擬人手法描寫紅海趕緊開路，好讓以色列人在乾地上走過。
**約旦河也倒流。**以色列從埃及到迦南的開頭和結束都有奇蹟顯現。這同一位上帝也帶領我們脫離埃及罪惡的奴役。祂必安全地引導我們經過約旦河是波浪，到達彼岸的應許之地。 這使我們得到莫大的鼓舞。
3.en:
**The sea saw it.** The Red Sea here is personified and is represented as hastening to prepare a path for the children of Israel to march through on dry ground.
**Jordan was driven back.** The miraculous providences were seen at both the beginning and the ending of Israel’s journey from Egypt to Canaan. We can take courage in the fact that the same God who led us out of the Egyptian bondage of sin will conduct us safely through Jordan’s stormy billows to the Land of Promise on the farther shore.

4.zh:
大山踴躍，如公羊；小山跳舞，如羊羔。

顯然是用詩歌的手法描寫伴隨著上帝在西奈山頒佈律法的地震（見出19:18）。在出埃及和進入聖地的兩大奇蹟中間，是上帝的偉大啟示。上帝在西奈山嚴肅地頒佈了祂神聖的律法。
4.en: **The mountains skipped.** Evidently a poetical description of the earthquake that accompanied the giving of the law at Sinai (see Ex. 19:18). Between the two miraculous wonders of the Exodus from Egypt and the entrance into the Holy Land stands the great revelation of God when, with great solemnity, He gave His holy law at Sinai.

5.zh:
滄海啊，你為何奔逃？約但哪，你為何倒流？

詩人要大自然解釋她的奇怪表現，和它為什麼偏離平時的軌道。
5.en: **What ailed thee?** The poet is asking nature to explain her strange behavior, to account for the fact that she seems to be turned out of her regular course.

7.zh:
大地啊，你因見主的面，就是雅各神的面，便要震動。

這裡回答上一節的問題。是上帝的臨格改變了大自然的規則。
7.en: **Tremble.** The answer to the questions raised in the preceding verses. The presence of God has changed the course of nature’s laws.

8.zh:
他叫磐石變為水池，叫堅石變為泉源。

上帝既讓利非訂和加低斯的磐石流出水來（見出17:6；民20:8-11），祂也必向祂忠心的僕人供應生命的水（見約4:14）。凡不斷喝這水的人將永遠不渴。這水將在他裡面成為永不枯竭的泉源，使他自己和疲乏的同路人在行走天路時得到滋潤。
8.en: **Turned the rock.** The God who made water flow from the rock in Rephidim and from the cliff at Kadesh (see Ex. 17:6; Num. 20:8–11) provides streams of living water for His faithful servants (see John 4:14). He who continues to drink of this water will never thirst, but the water will become in him a never-failing spring to refresh both himself and the weary fellow traveler along the heavenly way.

0.zh:
序言——本詩是詩人慶祝個人得救的感恩詩。詩中頌揚上帝拯救的大能。
七十士譯本把本詩分為兩篇：1-9節為114篇；10-19節為115篇（見本冊註釋第627頁）。
0.en:
INTRODUCTION.—Ps. 116 is a psalm of thanksgiving in which the psalmist celebrates an experience of personal deliverance. The psalm extols God’s saving power.
In the LXX, Ps. 116 appears as two psalms: vs. 1–9 as Ps. 114 and vs. 10–19 as Ps. 115 (see p. 627).

1.zh:
我愛耶和華，因為他聽了我的聲音和我的懇求。

原文的時態也可譯為“聽著”。即詩人正在讚美上帝應允了祈禱。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–8節）**。《教育論》第166頁。
1.en: **Hath heard.** The tense of the Hebrew verb permits the translation “is hearing.” The meaning thus suggested is that the psalmist is praising God for repeated answers to prayer.

2.zh:
他既向我側耳，我一生要求告他。

詩人保證堅持自己祈禱的習慣。
2.en: **As long.** The psalmist pledges consistency in his prayer habits.

3.zh:
死亡的繩索纏繞我；陰間的痛苦抓住我；我遭遇患難愁苦。

**陰間（she'ol）。**不是指折磨人的地獄，而是比喻死人的住所，不論是義人還是惡人（見箴15:11註釋）。本節不能作為地獄永火的依據。詩人用“死亡的繩索”和“陰間的痛苦”指自己在今生所經歷並蒙主拯救而擺脫的苦難。“死亡的繩索”與死後毫無關係。詩人所經受的試煉顯然使他更接近死亡。
3.en: **Hell.** Heb. she’ol, not a hell of torment but the figurative abode of the dead, both of the righteous and of the wicked (see on Prov. 15:11). This text lends no support to the doctrine of an ever-burning hell. The psalmist applies the expressions “sorrows of death” and “pains of hell” to himself as descriptive of experiences he passed through in this life and from which he had been delivered. Hence the expression “pains of hell” can have no connection with an experience after death. The trial through which the psalmist passed had evidently brought him nigh to death.

6.zh:
耶和華保護愚人；我落到卑微的地步，他救了我。

**愚人（pethi）。**指“沒有經驗的青年人”或“單純的青年人”。七十士譯本為nepia（“嬰孩”），用於太11:25。就像慈父看護和引導小孩嫩弱的腳步，上帝也憑著祂的慈愛引導祂的兒女行走人生的道路。
6.en: **The simple.** Heb. pethi, “inexperienced youth,” or “simple youth.” The LXX has nepia, “babes,” the word employed in Matt. 11:25. As a loving father guards and guides the tender feet of his infant child, so the Lord in His mercy guides His children along life’s pathway.

7.zh:
我的心哪！你要仍歸安樂，因為耶和華用厚恩待你。

只有完全信靠上帝，才能得到真正的安樂。這樣的安樂是沒有憂慮和煩惱的（見太11:29）。
7.en: **Rest.** True rest is found only by trusting God fully. Such rest banishes anxiety and restlessness (see Matt. 11:29).

9.zh:
我要在耶和華面前行活人之路。

就是與上帝和諧一致。二人若不同心，豈能同行呢（見摩3:3）？。
9.en: **I will walk.** To walk before (literally, “in the presence of”) God means to be in harmony with Him. Two cannot walk together except they be agreed (see Amos 3:3).

10.zh:
我因信，所以如此說話；我受了極大的困苦。

**我因信。**或“我信靠”。
**所以。**或“當……時候”。詩人懷著強烈的信心祈求拯救
10.en:
**I believed.** Or, “I trusted.”
**Therefore.** Better, “when.” The psalmist’s request for deliverance was lodged in strong faith.

11.zh:
我曾急促地說：人都是說謊的！

人在巨大的痛苦中往往對同胞作出草率的判斷，然後又深感內疚。雖然人可能顯得虛謊，經常靠不住，但實際上並不像初看上去那樣沒有希望。
11.en: **In my haste.** Under heavy affliction men often form hasty judgments concerning their fellow men; but hasty speaking is often followed by bitter remorse. Though men appear deceitful and are frequently unreliable, the situation is seldom as hopeless as it at first appears.

12.zh:
我拿什麼報答耶和華向我所賜的一切厚恩？

當我們被原先指望求助的人所拋棄時，就學會了欣賞上天的幫助和恩賜。詩人想用最好的語言來表達對上帝所賜一切恩典的感激。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》第187頁；《證言》卷五第87,220頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（12–14節）**。《歷代願望》第348頁；《服務真詮》第101頁。
12.en: **His benefits.** When apparently forsaken by men from whom we expected assistance, we learn to appreciate the help and benefit that come from heaven. The psalmist wonders how he can best express his gratitude to God for all the benefits bestowed upon him.

13.zh:
我要舉起救恩的杯，稱揚耶和華的名。

**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷五第317頁。

14.zh:
我要在他眾民面前向耶和華還我的願。

不還向上帝所許的願是極其嚴重的事情（見徒5:1-10）。
14.en: **Pay my vows.** It is a serious thing not to pay vows made to the Lord (see Acts 5:1–10).

15.zh:
在耶和華眼中，看聖民之死極為寶貴。

上帝不會忽略祂聖民的死（見太10:29-39）。守護的天使陪伴著聖民走過死亡的幽谷，記下他們的安息之地，並在光耀的復活清晨首先歡迎他們（《教育論》第305頁）。據說許多早期教會受迫害的基督徒在殉難時都背誦這節經文。其中的信息鼓舞他們進入幽谷。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷五第317頁。
15.en: **Death of his saints.** The Lord does not regard with indifference the death of His saints (see Matt. 10:29–39). Guardian angels accompany the saints through the valley of the shadow of death, mark their resting places, and are the first to greet them in the glorious resurrection morning (Ed 305). It is said that many of the persecuted Christians in the early church went to martyrdom repeating this verse and that its message buoyed up their courage as they passed into the dark valley.

17.zh:
我要以感謝為祭獻給你，又要求告耶和華的名。

見詩107:22註釋。
17.en: **Thanksgiving.** See on Ps. 107:22.

18.zh:
我要在他眾民面前，在耶和華殿的院內，在耶路撒冷當中，向耶和華還我的願。你們要讚美耶和華！併於上節。

感謝為祭。見第14節註釋。
**院內。**讚美上帝並不限於密室。見證上帝慈愛的聲音應當從聖民的會中發出。公眾的讚美和私下的祈禱都是蒙上帝悅納的。。
**懷愛倫註釋（18–19節）**。《先祖與先知》第539頁。
18.en: **Pay my vows.** See on v. 14.

116.19: **In the courts.** Praise to God is not to be confined to the closet. Men’s voices bearing testimony to God’s goodness should be heard in the assembly of the saints. Public praise as well as private devotion is commended in the Word of God.

0.zh:
序言——據《先祖與先知》664頁，大衛是在撒母耳逝世以後不久創作了詩120和121篇。這位敬虔者的離去，對於大衛個人來說，是一個重大的損失。他意識到撒母耳的束縛力既已消除，掃羅必變本加厲地追逐他。
第2節裡的誹謗者（第2節）很有可能是指掃羅，但也有人認為是指以東人多益（撒上22:22；見撒上26:19註釋）。
“上行之詩”的含義不明。除了本詩之外還有詩121-134篇。這些詩歌最有可能是朝聖之歌，是以色列人每年在前往耶路撒冷過節的路上唱的（見本冊註釋第538頁；又見第625,627頁）。
上行（或作登階。下同）之詩。
0.en:
God the Ever-wakeful Watchman When death claims esteemed friends and valued counselors, then it is that men realize anew that their trust must not be placed in princes, but in the ever-living, ever-watchful Lord. Though the voice of earlier advisers seemed indispensable and the watchful warnings invaluable, they cannot be compared with the promised guidance by One who never slumbers or sleeps. God is as desirous of manifesting His beneficient guidance today as He was in David’s day. Psalm 121:2-8
INTRODUCTION.—According to PP 664 David composed Ps. 120 and 121 shortly after the death of Samuel. The removal of this godly man was a great personal loss to David. He recognized that now that Samuel’s restraining influence had been removed. Saul would pursue him with greater fury than ever.
The slanderer (v. 2) is most probably Saul, though Doeg the Edomite (1 Sam. 22:22; see on 1 Sam. 26:19) has also been suggested.
There is considerable uncertainty regarding the meaning of the expression “a Song of degrees,” perhaps better translated, “a Song of ascents,” appearing in the superscription to this psalm and in the superscriptions to Ps. 121–134. The most probable explanation is that these psalms were employed as pilgrim psalms, sung as the children of Israel journeyed up to Jerusalem to the yearly festivals (see PP 538; see also pp. 625, 627).

1.zh:
（上行（或作登階，下同）之詩。）我在急難中求告耶和華，他就應允我。

上帝不僅垂聽祈禱，而且按照祂無窮的智慧予以回答。
1.en: **He heard me.** Literally, “he answered me.” Not only does the Lord hear prayers; He answers them according to His infinite wisdom.

2.zh:
耶和華啊，求你救我脫離說謊的嘴唇和詭詐的舌頭！

**說謊的嘴唇。**見詩120篇介紹。關於舌頭的作用，見雅3:5,6。當一個人受到誹謗時，可以從耶穌的話中得到安慰（太5:10-12）。
2.en: **Deceitful tongue.** See Introduction to Ps. 120. On the power of the tongue see James 3:5, 6. Consolation, when one is slandered, may be found in the words of Jesus (Matt. 5:10–12).

3.zh:
詭詐的舌頭啊，要給你什麼呢？要拿什麼加給你呢？

誹謗會使說鄰居壞話的人心裡更加卑鄙和墮落，並給社會帶來誤解和紛爭。
3.en: **False tongue.** Slander embitters and degrades the soul of the one who speaks evil of his neighbor, and brings misunderstanding and contention into society.

4.zh:
就是勇士的利箭和羅騰木（小樹名，松類）的炭火。

**利箭。**第4節回答了第3節的問題。利箭顯然指上帝給誹謗者的報應。
**羅騰木（小樹名，松類）。**原文是rethamim。據認為指金雀花樹，是多枝少葉的灌木（見伯30:4註釋）。阿拉伯人現在用它來生產優質木炭，可以燒出很旺的火。
4.en:
**Sharp arrows.** Verse 4 is the answer to the question raised in v. 3. Evidently these sharp arrows represent the retribution the Lord brings upon the slanderer.
**Juniper.** Heb. rethamim, believed to represent a plant called broom, a treelike shrub with many twigs but with few leaves (see on Job 30:4). From this broom the Arabs today manufacture charcoal of good quality which makes an intensely hot fire.

5.zh:
我寄居在米設，住在基達帳棚之中，有禍了！

**米設。**見創10:2註釋。
**基達。**見創25:13註釋。米設和基達顯然喻指大衛流亡之地。
5.en:
**Mesech.** Rather, “Meshech” (see on Gen. 10:2).
**Kedar.** See on Gen. 25:13. Meshech and Kedar are evidently used figuratively of the lands of David’s exile.

6.zh:
我與那恨惡和睦的人許久同住。

可能指掃羅王（見詩120篇序言）。
6.en: **That hateth peace.** Perhaps a reference to King Saul (see Introduction to Ps. 120).

7.zh:
我願和睦，但我發言，他們就要爭戰。

大衛儘量要與掃羅和他邪惡的謀士們和平相處，所得到的卻是仇恨和敵意。
7.en: **I am for peace.** Literally, “I am peace.” David’s attempts to live peaceably with Saul and his evil advisers, were answered with hatred and hostility.

0.zh:
序言——本詩是在苦難中向上帝懇求幫助。人稱從單數變為複數（見第1,2節），使祈求帶有民族的性質。
關於本詩的題記，見詩120篇序言，又見本冊註釋第625,627頁（《詩篇》序言）。
上行之詩 。
0.en:
INTRODUCTION.—Ps. 123 is an earnest appeal to God for help in time of distress. The change from the singular to the plural (see vs. 1, 2) places the appeal on a national basis.
On the superscription see Introduction to Ps. 120; also pp. 625, 627.

1.zh:
（上行之詩。）坐在天上的主啊，我向你舉目。

信心和盼望的眼睛始終仰望上帝。祂是宇宙至高的統治者。
1.en: **Lift I up.** The eye of faith and hope must always be uplifted to God, the Supreme Ruler of the universe.

2.zh:
看哪，僕人的眼睛怎樣望主人的手，使女的眼睛怎樣望主母的手，我們的眼睛也照樣望耶和華─我們的神，直到他憐憫我們。

**僕人。**正如家裡的僕人仰賴主人的支持，基督徒也仰賴上帝在肉身和屬靈方面的扶持。僕人在受到誤解或傷害時，要靠主人的保護。信徒也當仰賴上帝的手拯救（見林前4:3,4）。
**望主人的手。**參詩145:15。詩人描寫上帝所造的萬物都仰賴祂供給日常的需要。
2.en:
**Servants.** As the servants in a household look to the master for support, so Christians are dependent upon God for physical help and spiritual sustenance. When the servant receives wrong or injury, he looks to his master for protection. So the believing child should look to the hand of the Lord to deliver him (see 1 Cor. 4:3, 4).
**Look unto the hand.** Compare Ps. 145:15, where the psalmist pictures all the creatures of God’s hand as looking to Him for their daily needs.

3.zh:
耶和華啊，求你憐憫我們，憐憫我們！因為我們被藐視，已到極處。

沒有足夠的資料來確定詩人所指的是以色列歷史上的哪一個危險時期。
3.en: **Exceedingly filled.** There are insufficient data to determine to what crisis in Israel’s national history the psalmist is alluding.

4.zh:
我們被那些安逸人的譏誚和驕傲人的藐視，已到極處。

參結16:49；摩6:1；亞1:15。脫離苦難的安逸生活不是培養品格的土壤。上帝讓苦難臨到祂的子民，是為了使他們放棄安逸的生活，盼望天上的家。我們應該感謝上帝，因為祂用磨難的手使人傲慢的本性埋入塵土。
4.en: **At ease.** Compare Eze. 16:49; Amos 6:1; Zech. 1:15. Freedom from affliction and a life of comfortable ease are not the soil in which character develops. The Lord permits affliction to come upon His people to wean them away from a life of ease and make them long for their heavenly home. We should thank God for the hand of affliction that lays the pride of man in the dust.

0.zh:
序言——這首讚美詩感謝上帝的大能在民族危機中施行拯救。具體的背景尚未確定。周邊的敵人不斷威脅著以色列人。選民多次幾乎被消滅。但上帝提供了逃生之路。
關於本詩的題記，見詩120篇序言，另見本冊註釋第616,625,627頁（《詩篇》序言）。
大衛上行之詩。
0.en:
INTRODUCTION.—Ps. 124 is a hymn of thanksgiving to God for His mighty deliverance in time of national crisis. The precise occasion is not identified. Surrounding enemies were a constant threat to Israel. Many times it seemed that the chosen people would be annihilated. However, the Lord provided a way of escape.
On the superscription see Introduction to Ps. 120; also pp. 616, 625, 627.

1.zh:
（大衛上行之詩。）以色列人要說：若不是耶和華幫助我們，

這裡是對於拯救源泉的正確承認。當祈禱實現、危機過去以後，人往往會忘記福惠的泉源（見路17:12-17）。這是一個醒目的宣告。上帝是以色列人的盟友。有上帝站在以色列人一邊，百姓就不必懼怕仇敵。
1.en: **Been the Lord.** An appropriate acknowledgment of the source of the deliverance. Too often the source of blessing is forgotten once the petition is realized and the crisis past (see Luke 17:12–17). A striking announcement. God had been Israel’s ally. With God on the side of Israel, the people need fear no foe.

3.zh:
向我們發怒的時候，就把我們活活地吞了。

惡人表現了大毀滅者撒但的精神（見約8:44）。
3.en: **Swallowed us up.** The wicked reflect the spirit of the great destroyer, Satan himself (see John 8:44).

5.zh:
狂傲的水必淹沒我們。

正如咆哮的洪水掃蕩前面的一切，對敵擋的事物似乎不屑一顧，如果沒有上帝的限制，惡人也會吞沒義人，毀滅他們（見《善惡之爭》第614頁）。
5.en: **Proud waters.** As the swollen flood—waters sweep everything before them, and seem disdainful of opposing objects, so the wicked would engulf the righteous and bring about their destruction if God did not restrain them (see GC 614).

6.zh:
耶和華是應當稱頌的！他沒有把我們當野食交給他們吞吃（原文是牙齒）。

這裡把以色列的敵人比作想要吞吃獵物，但受到上帝制止的野獸。
6.en: **A prey.** The metaphor changes. The adversaries of Israel are likened to wild beasts ready to devour their prey, but held in check by God.

7.zh:
我們好像雀鳥，從捕鳥人的網羅裡逃脫；網羅破裂，我們逃脫了。

這裡把以色列比作落入網羅驚恐無奈的鳥兒，但突然網羅破裂而得以逃脫了。
7.en: **Snare is broken.** Israel is likened to a frightened, defenseless bird caught in a trap, but suddenly freed by the breaking of the snare.

8.zh:
我們得幫助，是在乎倚靠造天地之耶和華的名。

只要這兩個上帝創造大能的重大紀念存在，上帝的兒女就不必害怕微不足道的人類會對他們做什麼。創造天地的主宰擁有無限的資源。宇宙萬物都在祂的監察之下，順從祂的旨意。
8.en: **Heaven and earth.** As long as these two great monuments of God’s mighty creative power exist, God’s children need not fear what puny man can do to them. He who made heaven and earth is infinite in resources; all the forces of the universe are within His view, and obedient to His will.

0.zh:
序言——本詩深化了義人可以確信上帝不斷保護他們的主題。正如耶路撒冷受惠於它的地理位置，信靠上帝的人也會擺脫惡人的詭計。他們必躲開仇敵一切帶著火焰的飛鏢。
關於本詩的題記，見詩120篇序言，又見本冊註釋第625,627頁（《詩篇》序言）。
上行之詩。
0.en:
INTRODUCTION.—Ps. 125 develops the theme that the righteous can be assured of the Lord’s guardianship over them continually. As Jerusalem is secure by its geographical location, so those who trust in God will be secure from the machinations of the wicked. They are safe from all the fiery darts of the enemy.
On the superscription see Introduction to Ps. 120; also pp. 625, 627.

1.zh:
（上行之詩。）倚靠耶和華的人好像錫安山，永不動搖。

見詩48:2註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–2節）**。《先祖與先知》第538頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–3節）**。《使徒行述》第86頁。
1.en: **Mount Zion.** See on Ps. 48:2.

2.zh:
眾山怎樣圍繞耶路撒冷，耶和華也照樣圍繞他的百姓，從今時直到永遠。

**圍繞耶路撒冷。**耶路撒冷得天獨厚，位於山脊之上的（見詩48:2註釋），東有汲淪谷，南有欣嫩子谷，與周圍的山隔開，西有泰勒波溫谷（Tyropoeon Valley）與古城隔開。周圍的山一般要高一些。如橄欖山高達大約2,723英尺，而古城最高處約為2,470英尺。
**圍繞他的百姓。**正如群山圍繞著耶路撒冷，上帝也以祂不斷加深的慈愛包圍祂的子民，保守他們在祂的羊欄裡，不讓想害他們的人進來。
2.en:
**Round about Jerusalem.** Jerusalem was uniquely situated on a mountain ridge (see on Ps. 48:2), separated from the surrounding hills by the Kidron Valley to the east, the Valley of Hinnom to the south, and the ancient city by the Tyropoeon Valley to the west. The surrounding hills were generally higher. The Mt. of Olives, for example, reaches an altitude of about 2,723 ft. at its highest point as compared with an altitude of about 2,470 ft. for the highest point of the ancient city.
**Round about his people.** As this girdle of mountains encircles the city, so the ever-widening circle of God’s love surrounds His people. That circle keeps them within His fold, and also keeps those who would do harm from entering in.

3.zh:
惡人的杖不常落在義人的分上，免得義人伸手作惡。

指外邦的王權。義人不會繼續受惡人所支配，以免長期的壓迫和與惡人為伍，使以色列接受他們的一些罪惡行徑。
3.en: **Rod of the wicked.** The heathen scepter. The righteous will not continue to be dominated by the wicked, lest prolonged oppression and continual association with evil men lead Israel to adopt some of their evil ways.

5.zh:
至於那偏行彎曲道路的人，耶和華必使他和作惡的人一同出去受刑。願平安歸於以色列！

與惡人所處的混亂不安相對照，義人得享平安（見詩122:6-8）。
5.en: **Peace.** In contrast with the confusion and unrest in which the wicked find themselves, the righteous experience peace (see Ps. 122:6–8).

0.zh:
序言——這是一首描寫家庭虔誠和幸福的田園詩。
關於本詩的題記，見詩120篇序言；另見本冊註釋第625,627頁（《詩篇》序言）。
上行之詩
0.en:
INTRODUCTION.—Ps. 128 is an idyllic picture of family piety and felicity..
On the superscription see Introduction to Ps. 120; also pp. 625, 627.

1.zh:
（上行之詩。）凡敬畏耶和華、遵行他道的人便為有福！

**有福。**見詩1:1註釋。
**敬畏。**敬畏上帝是一切真幸福的基礎。這不是來自負疚感的恐懼，而是出於對上帝的熱愛和敬重。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《給管家的勉言》第155頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–2節）**。《證言》卷四第495頁。
1.en:
**Blessed.** See on Ps. 1:1.
**That feareth.** The fear of God is the foundation of all true happiness. This is not the shuddering fear that comes from conscious guilt, but the fear that arises from an ardent love and profound reverence for God.

2.zh:
你要吃勞碌得來的；你要享福，事情順利。

義人的勤勞得到祝福。辛勞的工人得以享受自己勞動的果實。聖經並沒有認可懶惰，而是處處倡導勞動的尊嚴。人生的辛勞和憂慮是為愛而安排的（見《先祖與先知》第60頁），其目的是在他墮落的狀態中給他提供保護（見創3:17-19註釋）。
2.en: **Labour of thine hands.** The industry of the good man is blessed and the diligent toiler enjoys a recompense for his labor. The Scriptures give no sanction to indolence but everywhere uphold the dignity of labor. Man’s life of toil and care was appointed in love (see PP 60), as a protection to him in his fallen state (see on Gen. 3:17–19).

3.zh:
你妻子在你的內室，好像多結果子的葡萄樹；你兒女圍繞你的桌子，好像橄欖栽子。

**多結果子的葡萄樹。**多結果實，優美和人們賴以生存的葡萄樹，象徵著家中的賢妻良母。
**橄欖栽子。**希伯來人視葡萄和橄欖為世上最好的水果。所以擁有賢德的妻子和忠心的兒女是人在世上最大的福氣。
3.en:
**Fruitful vine.** The fruitfulness, gracefulness, and dependence for support of the vine is a fitting symbol of the loyal wife and mother in the home.
**Olive plants.** The Hebrews considered the vine and the olive among earth’s choicest fruits. So a noble wife and dutiful children are the greatest gifts that a man can possess on this earth.

4.zh:
看哪，敬畏耶和華的人必要這樣蒙福！

義人不但自己蒙福，而且給周圍的人帶來福氣。
4.en: **Blessed.** Not only is the good man blessed himself; he is a blessing to all around him.

5.zh:
願耶和華從錫安賜福給你！願你一生一世看見耶路撒冷的好處！

正如希伯來人不斷地維持耶路撒冷的興旺，基督徒也要為建設地上的教會而努力。
5.en: **The good of Jerusalem.** As the Hebrews kept continually before them the prosperity of Jerusalem, so the Christian will constantly work for the upbuilding of God’s church on earth.

6.zh:
願你看見你兒女的兒女！願平安歸於以色列！

**兒女的兒女。**一個敬畏上帝的人必得享高壽，看見自己的子孫興旺。
**願平安歸於以色列。**最好把這句話看作臨別時的祝福。
6.en:
**Children’s children.** The man who fears the Lord will live to a ripe old age and see his family perpetuated.
**Peace upon Israel.** It is preferable to take these words as a parting benediction, “Peace be upon Israel.”

0.zh:
序言——這是一首慶祝民族得救的詩歌。詩人述說了以色列作為一個民族所經歷的試煉，以及上帝怎樣介入，給仇敵造成混亂。這是一首田園詩，引用了若干農業方面的比喻。本詩的創作背景尚未確定。詩人所關心的不是具體的事件，而是其中的教訓。
關於本詩的題記，見詩120篇序言；另見本冊註釋第625,627頁（《詩篇》序言）。
上行之詩。

1.zh:
（上行之詩。）以色列當說：從我幼年以來，敵人屢次苦害我，

**屢次。**或“多不勝數”，“經常”。
**從我幼年以來。**見耶2:2；何2:3,15；11:1。以色列的“幼年”在埃及受到殘酷的奴役，現在回顧上帝把他們從那片黑暗的土地中拯救出來。

2.zh:
從我幼年以來，敵人屢次苦害我，卻沒有勝了我。

信靠上帝的人，雖然常經苦難，卻不會被打敗（見林後4:8-10）。在基督裡他總是能取得勝利。

3.zh:
如同扶犁的在我背上扶犁而耕，耕的犁溝甚長。

這是描寫以色列人的背上被壓迫者的皮鞭打傷。身上的鞭痕就像田裡的犁溝。

6.zh:
願他們像房頂上的草，未長成而枯乾，

風或鳥攜帶著種子落在東方房屋的平頂上，很快就發芽了，但因為沒有厚土，不久就枯萎了，沒有任何收成（太13:5）。那些想謀害以色列的人也是這樣。他們的計劃開始時似乎會成功，但不會有結果。

7.zh:
收割的不夠一把，捆禾的也不滿懷。

沒有禾捆，也沒有收成。

8.zh:
過路的也不說：願耶和華所賜的福歸與你們！我們奉耶和華的名給你們祝福！

參得2:4。對於錫安的仇敵，決不會有這樣的祝福。

0.zh:
序言——本詩表達了罪人在絕望中向上帝呼籲寬恕。他承認如果上帝按照他的罪對待他，他的案情就毫無希望。主耶和華向這位罪人表現為赦免人的上帝。
關於本詩的題記，見詩120篇序言，又見本冊註釋第625,627頁（《詩篇》序言）。
上行之詩。
0.en:
INTRODUCTION.—Ps. 130 is the confession of a sinner who in despair cries unto the Lord for forgiveness. He recognizes that if the Lord should deal with him according to his sin, his case would be hopeless. The Lord reveals Himself to this sinner as a pardoning God.
On the superscription see Introduction to Ps. 120; see also pp. 625, 627.

1.zh:
（上行之詩。）耶和華啊，我從深處向你求告！

**從深處（de profundis）。**故本詩名為De profundis Psalm。詩人雖然處在深深的苦難中，仍承認上帝樂意回答這種狀況下的祈禱。
1.en: **Out of the depths.** Latin, de profundis; hence the psalm has been named the De profundis Psalm. The psalmist was in deep distress, but he recognized that the Lord delights to answer prayer under such circumstances.

3.zh:
主─耶和華啊，你若究察罪孽，誰能站得住呢？

要在審察的大日站立得住，就得完全依靠上帝的赦罪之恩，祈求基督的公義。
**懷愛倫註釋（3–8節）**。《給傳道人的證言》第15頁。
3.en: **Shouldest mark.** Literally, “shouldest observe,” “shouldest watch.” In order to stand in the great day of scrutiny, we must rely wholly upon God’s pardoning mercy and forgiving love and plead the righteousness of Christ.

4.zh:
但在你有赦免之恩，要叫人敬畏你。

上帝樂意赦免懺悔的罪人。祂的本性就是有慈愛有赦免。但是祂的赦免是有條件的（見詩32:1註釋）。
4.en: **Forgiveness.** God delights in forgiving the penitent sinner. His nature is merciful and forgiving. But there are prerequisites to forgiveness (see on Ps. 32:1).

5.zh:
我等候耶和華，我的心等候；我也仰望他的話。

回答不可能像詩人所期望的那樣快，但由於他相信主的話，他就在盼望中耐心等候。憂愁的黑夜似乎是漫長的，但他知道不久將要破曉，黑雲必將消散，“公義的日頭”的光輝必將顯現（見瑪4:2）。
5.en: **I wait.** The answer may not come as quickly as the psalmist would like, but because of his confidence in that word he waits patiently in hope. Even though the night of sorrow may seem long, he knows that the morning will soon break. When the dark, black clouds of night roll away, the bright beams of “the Sun of righteousness” will be seen (see Mal. 4:2).

6.zh:
我的心等候主，勝於守夜的，等候天亮，勝於守夜的，等候天亮。

**懷愛倫註釋**。《給傳道人的證言》第445頁。

7.zh:
以色列啊，你當仰望耶和華！因他有慈愛，有豐盛的救恩。

**以色列啊，你當仰望耶和華。**詩人邀請同胞分享他這個有福的盼望。
**慈愛（chesed）。**“上帝的愛”（見詩36篇補充註釋）。
**豐盛的救恩。**上帝有無限的能力，能夠而且願意“充充足足地成就一切超過我們所求所想的”（弗3:20）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督比喻實訓》第245頁。
7.en:
**Let Israel hope.** The psalmist asked his people to join with him in this blessed hope.
**Mercy.** Heb. chesed, “divine love” (see Additional Note on Ps. 36).
**Plenteous redemption.** There is unlimited power with God, and He is able and willing, yes, He delights in doing for us “exceeding abundantly above all that we ask or think” (Eph. 3:20).

8.zh:
他必救贖以色列脫離一切的罪孽。

**他。**原文是強調的。除此以外別無拯救（太1:21；徒4:12）。詩人已經從負疚感的深淵中出來，站到救贖和赦免的山頂之上。
8.en: **He.** Emphatic in the Hebrew. There is salvation in no other (Matt. 1:21; Acts 4:12). The psalmist has come out of the depths of a crushing sense of sin and is now standing upon the mountaintop of redemption and forgiveness.

0.zh:
序言——本詩表達了孩子般的信靠和謙卑的服從。詩人所培養的自制達到了無以復加的程度。
關於本詩的題記，見詩120篇序言；另見本冊註釋第616,625,627頁（《詩篇》序言）。
大衛上行之詩。
0.en:
INTRODUCTION.—Ps. 131 is a song expressing childlike trust and humble resignation. The psalmist had cultivated the art of self-discipline to the place where he no longer strove for the highest place.
On the superscription see Introduction to Ps. 120; see also pp. 616, 625, 627.

1.zh:
（大衛上行之詩。）耶和華啊，我的心不狂傲，我的眼不高大；重大和測不透的事，我也不敢行。

在經驗的學校中，詩人必須放棄驕傲和自私，培養溫柔謙卑的精神。上帝眼中的偉人乃是最謙卑的人。耶穌說：“凡婦人所生的，沒有一個興起來大過施洗約翰的”（太11:11）。但約翰是最謙卑的人。他達到了克己的崇高境界（見約3:30）。“與寶座最接近的，乃是卑微的腳凳”（見耶45:5）。只有真正的謙卑才是真正的偉大。
1.en: **Not haughty.** In the school of experience the psalmist had to renounce pride and selfishness and to develop a meek and lowly spirit. The great men in God’s sight are men of deep humility. Christ stated that among those born of women there had not arisen a greater than John the Baptist (Matt. 11:11), and yet he was one of the humblest of men. John reached the height of self-abnegation (see John 3:30). “Nearest the throne itself shall be, the footstool of humility” (see Jer. 45:5). None but the sincerely humble are truly great.

2.zh:
我的心平穩安靜，好像斷過奶的孩子在他母親的懷中；我的心在我裡面真像斷過奶的孩子。

詩人斷絕了世俗的野心和慾望，得享上帝裡面的平安和滿足。
2.en: **Weaned child.** The psalmist had been weaned away from worldly ambitions and desires, and now enjoyed security and contentment in God.

3.zh:
以色列啊，你當仰望耶和華，從今時直到永遠！

詩歌的語氣從個人的感受轉變成對全體以色列人的呼籲。詩人斷絕了自私的願望，為他的以色列同胞發出祈禱。他為上帝而活，並鼓勵朋友和同胞們效法他。他個人的勝利成為全體以色列人效法的榜樣。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《給傳道人的證言》第15頁。
3.en: **Let Israel hope.** The tone of personal experience changes to a request for all Israel. Having been weaned from his own selfish desires, the psalmist was able to utter a prayer for his people Israel. He was living for the Lord and encouraging all his friends and countrymen to follow his example. Personal victory became a pattern for all Israel to follow.

0.zh:
序言——本詩紀念大衛建造敬拜之所的願望，和上帝對這位牧者君王的慈悲應許（見撒下7:1-13；《證言》卷一第203頁）。
關於本詩的題記，見詩120篇序言；另見本冊註釋第625,627頁（《詩篇》序言）。
上行之詩。
0.en:
INTRODUCTION.—Ps. 132 is a song commemorating David’s desire to build a house of worship and the Lord’s gracious promises to the shepherd king (see 2 Sam. 7:1–13; 1T 203).
On the superscription see Introduction to Ps. 120; see also pp. 625, 627.

1.zh:
（上行之詩。）耶和華啊，求你記念大衛所受的一切苦難！

見代上22:14。大衛所受的苦難，有些是自己造成的，有些是外來的。
1.en: **All his afflictions.** See 1 Chron. 22:14. Some of the trials David endured were of his own making, others came upon him from without.

2.zh:
他怎樣向耶和華起誓，向雅各的大能者許願，

見撒下7:1-13。歷史記錄沒有提到這個誓言。
2.en: **Sware.** See 2 Sam. 7:1–13. The historical account does not mention the oath.

3.zh:
說：我必不進我的帳幕，也不上我的床榻；

大衛決心把為上帝建造聖所，視為頭等重要的大事。
3.en: **I will not come.** David resolved to make the building of a house for the Lord the item of pre-eminent importance in his affairs.

4.zh:
我不容我的眼睛睡覺，也不容我的眼目打盹；

這是東方式的比喻（見箴6:4）。詩人覺得如果不為上帝的約櫃預備安放之處，就不得安心。他對上帝的聖工非常關心，以致把其他的一切都放在第二位。
4.en: **Not give sleep.** An Oriental figure (see Prov. 6:4). The psalmist could not enjoy rest till he had prepared a resting place for the ark of God. He was so in earnest about God’s work that everything else took second place.

6.zh:
我們聽說約櫃在以法他，我們在基列‧耶琳就尋見了。

**我們聽說約櫃。**詩人的意念一下子轉到了沒有固定居所的約櫃。
**以法他。**這句詩歌的含義不明。有人認為“以法他”是指伯利恆，因為以法他是伯利恆的古名（見創35:19註釋）。也有人認為是指基列耶琳（見代上2:24,50）。約櫃在那裡放了二十年（撒上7:2）。
**基列耶琳。**英文KJV版為“樹林”。希伯來語是Qiryath Ye`arim。
6.en:
**We heard of it.** An abrupt transition of thought to the unhoused ark.
**Ephratah.** The meaning of this poetical passage is obscure. Some see in “Ephratah” a reference to Bethlehem, since Ephratah was the ancient name of that city (see on Gen. 35:19). Others see a reference to Kirjath-jearim (1 Chron. 2:24, 50), where the ark was for 20 years (1 Sam. 7:2).
**Wood.** Heb. ya‘ar, which should probably be rendered as a proper name, Jaar (see RSV), which, in turn, is probably a shortened form of Kirjath-jearim, Heb. Qiryath Ye‘arim.

8.zh:
耶和華啊，求你興起，和你有能力的約櫃同入安息之所！

求上帝惠臨以色列人為祂預備的安息之所（見代下6:41,42）。
8.en: **Arise.** A prayer that the Lord will occupy the resting place Israel provided for Him (see 2 Chron. 6:41, 42).

9.zh:
願你的祭司披上公義！願你的聖民歡呼！

**披上公義。**聖潔是對於擔任聖職之人的要求（見伯29:14；啟19:8）。
**聖民（chasidim）。**見詩36篇補充註釋。
9.en:
**With righteousness.** Purity and holiness are required of those who minister in sacred offices (see Job 29:14; Rev. 19:8).
**Saints.** Heb. chasidim (see Additional Note on Ps. 36).

10.zh:
求你因你僕人大衛的緣故，不要厭棄你的受膏者！

每一個繼承王位、擔負起神聖職責的大衛後裔，在就任時都應獻上這樣的禱告。
10.en: **Thine anointed.** This prayer might appropriately have been offered as each successor in the line of David mounted the throne and entered upon his sacred office.

11.zh:
耶和華向大衛、憑誠實起了誓，必不反覆，說：我要使你所生的坐在你的寶座上。

見撒下7:12。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷一第203頁。
11.en: **Lord hath sworn.** See 2 Sam. 7:12.

12.zh:
你的眾子若守我的約和我所教訓他們的法度，他們的子孫必永遠坐在你的寶座上。

對大衛的應許是以順從為條件的（見王上8:25；參撒下7:14；見撒下7:12-16註釋）。
12.en: **If.** The promises to David were conditional on obedience (see 1 Kings 8:25; cf. 2 Sam. 7:14; see on 2 Sam. 7:12–16).

13.zh:
因為耶和華揀選了錫安，願意當作自己的居所，

**懷愛倫註釋**。《善惡之爭》第19頁。

14.zh:
說：這是我永遠安息之所；我要住在這裡，因為是我所願意的。

“如果以色列民族保持對上天的效忠，耶路撒冷就會永遠屹立，作為上帝所特選的”（《善惡之爭》第19頁；見《歷代願望》第577頁）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》第732頁。
14.en: **My rest.** Better, “my resting place.” “Had Israel as a nation preserved her allegiance to Heaven, Jerusalem would have stood forever, the elect of God” (GC 19; see DA 577).

15.zh:
我要使其中的糧食豐滿，使其中的窮人飽足。

如果以色列人遵從了上帝的計劃，他們在屬世方面也必興旺（見申18:1-14）。
15.en: **Her provision.** Temporal prosperity would have been the lot of Israel if she had followed the divine plan (see Deut. 18:1–14).

16.zh:
我要使祭司披上救恩，聖民大聲歡呼！

**使祭司披。**這是對第9節祈禱的回應。以色列不幸沒有履行自己的職責。她的祭司不但沒有披上救恩的外衣，反而褻瀆了真正的崇拜（結22:26）。
**聖民（chasidim）。**見詩36篇補充註釋。
16.en:
**Clothe her priests.** A response to the prayer of v. 9. Israel tragically failed in her mission. Instead of being clothed with salvation her priests became profaners of true worship (Eze. 22:26).
**Saints.** Heb. chasidim (see Additional Note on Ps. 36).

17.zh:
我要叫大衛的角在那裡發生；我為我的受膏者預備明燈。

**發生（samach）。**“發芽”。其名詞semach“苗裔”指彌賽亞（見耶23:5；33:15；亞3:8；6:12）。
**明燈。**參王上15:4。
**為我的受膏者。**指國王大衛。“受膏者”希伯來語是mashiach（即“彌賽亞”），其詞根mashach（“塗油”）。
17.en:
**To bud.** Heb. samach, “to sprout,” or “to spring up.” The noun semach, “branch,” “twig,” or “sprout,” is used as a title of the Messiah (see Jer. 23:5; 33:15; Zech. 3:8; 6:12).
**A lamp.** Compare 1 Kings 15:4.
**For mine anointed.** That is, for the king, here a reference to David. The word “anointed” is from the Heb. mashiach, literally, “messiah,” from the root mashach, “to anoint.”

18.zh:
我要使他的仇敵披上羞恥；但他的冠冕要在頭上發光。

**冠冕（nezer）。**“授任聖職”，或“聖職授任的標誌”。指王冠或大祭司的冠冕（見出29:6）。七十士譯本用“我的聖潔”替代“他的冠冕”。
**發光（sus）。**其名詞Sus（“開花”或“前面的裝飾”）指大祭司冠冕上刻著“歸耶和華為聖”的閃光的金牌（見出28:36,37）。
18.en:
**Crown.** Heb. nezer, “a consecration [to an office],” also “a diadem [or sign of consecration].” It can be appropriately applied to a king’s crown or to a high priest’s diadem (see Ex. 29:6). The LXX reads “my holiness” in place of “his crown.”
**Flourish.** Heb. ṣuṣ, “to blossom.” Ṣuṣ is here used in the sense “to shine,” “to sparkle,” or “to glitter.” The corresponding noun ṣiṣ, “a blossom” or “a front ornament,” is used in referring to the glittering plate of gold bearing the inscription “Holiness to the Lord,” which the high priest wore on his miter (see Ex. 28:36, 37).

0.zh:
序言——這是一首美麗的短詩，稱讚弟兄和睦之福。這種和睦是以色列人在耶路撒冷過大節時的特點。在這種場合中充滿和諧與弟兄友愛的氣氛。
關於本詩的題記，見詩120篇序言；另見本冊註釋第616,625,627頁（《詩篇》序言）。
大衛上行之詩。
0.en:
INTRODUCTION.—Ps. 133 is a short but beautiful poem extolling the blessedness of brotherly unity. Such unity characterized the meetings of the Israelites at the great festivals of Jerusalem. Harmony and brotherly love prevailed on these occasions.
On the superscription see Introduction to Ps. 120; see also pp. 616, 625, 627.

1.zh:
（大衛上行之詩。）看哪，弟兄和睦同居是何等地善，何等地美！

**弟兄。**表示親密的關係。大衛和他的親友躲在亞杜蘭洞時，吟唱了本詩（見《先祖與先知》第658頁）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《復臨信徒家庭》第179頁；《今日的生活》第276頁；《先祖與先知》第658頁。
1.en: **Brethren.** The term denotes a tie of intimate relationship. David sang Ps. 133 when his relatives and friends were in hiding in the cave of Adullam (see PP 658).

2.zh:
這好比那貴重的油澆在亞倫的頭上，流到鬍鬚，又流到他的衣襟；

**油（shemen）。**這裡顯然不是指普通的油，而是大祭司受膏時所用的聖油（出29:7；30:23-33）。聖潔甘美的膏油香氣四溢。澆在亞倫的頭上，又流到他的衣襟。兄弟之愛也是這樣。它以其芳香和聖潔的影響祝福所有的人。
2.en: **Ointment.** Heb. shemen, “oil,” here evidently not common oil, but the sacred oil with which the high priest was anointed (Ex. 29:7; 30:23–33). It had a sweet perfume; it was holy; it was diffusive. When it was poured upon Aaron’s head, it dropped upon his garments. So it is with brotherly love. It blesses all with its sweet and holy influence.

3.zh:
又好比黑門的甘露降在錫安山；因為在那裡有耶和華所命定的福，就是永遠的生命。

**黑門的甘露。**精神振奮的一個象徵。來自上天的兄弟之愛是充滿生氣的。這是天家情誼的預嘗。由於隨從們所表現的同情和愛心，大衛在亞杜蘭洞藏身時吟唱了這首詩歌（《先祖與先知》第658頁）。
3.en: **Dew of Hermon.** A symbol of refreshment. Brotherly love born of heaven refreshes and revives. It is a foretaste of the fellowship enjoyed in the heavenly home. Because of the sympathy and affection which his associates showed him, David could sing this psalm while he was in the cave of Adullam (PP 658).

0.zh:
序言——本詩向聖所中值夜班侍奉耶和華的人發出呼籲（第1,2節）及其回應（第3節）。
這首短詩是最後一篇上行之詩（見詩120篇序言；另見本冊註釋第625,627頁《詩篇》序言）。
上行之詩。
0.en:
INTRODUCTION.—Ps. 134 consists of an appeal to the night attendants in the sanctuary to worship Jehovah (vs. 1, 2) and a response (v. 3).
This short psalm is the last of the Songs of Ascents (see Introduction to Ps. 120; see also pp. 625, 627).

1.zh:
（上行之詩。）耶和華的僕人夜間站在耶和華殿中的，你們當稱頌耶和華！

**你們當稱頌耶和華。**見詩63:4註釋。
**夜間站在耶和華殿中的。**利未人被指定擔任聖職，既值日班，也值夜班（見代上9:33）。
1.en:
**Bless ye the Lord.** See on Ps. 63:4.
**By night stand.** The Levites were employed in their sacred work by night as well as by day (see 1 Chron. 9:33).

2.zh:
你們當向聖所舉手，稱頌耶和華！

是祝福的手勢（見利9:22），也是祈禱的手勢（見詩141:2）。
2.en: **Lift up your hands.** A gesture of blessing (see Lev. 9:22), as well as an attitude in prayer (see Ps. 141:2).

3.zh:
願造天地的耶和華，從錫安賜福給你們！

**造天地的耶和華。**這是區別真神和假神的特殊標誌（見詩115:15註釋）。
**你們。**指全體會眾，也指每一個人。
**從錫安。**把來自宇宙創造主的祝福，說成是來自大君之城。
3.en:
**That made.** The special mark of distinction between the true God and false gods (see on Ps. 115:15).
**Thee.** Each one individually as well as the congregation as a whole.
**Out of Zion.** The benediction from the Creator of the universe is represented as coming from the city of the Great King.

0.zh: 序言——本詩呼籲讚美上帝，為祂過去和將來為祂子民所做的事。第一部分（第1-14節）勸勉人讚美上帝的良善，接著譴責偶像，並進一步勸人稱頌上帝的名（第15-21節）。
0.en: INTRODUCTION.—Ps. 135 is an appeal to praise the Lord, because of what He has done for His people and because of what He is to His people. The first section (vs. 1–14) contains an exhortation to praise the Lord for His goodness. This is followed by a denunciation of idols and a further exhortation to bless the name of God (vs. 15–21).

1.zh:
你們要讚美耶和華！你們要讚美耶和華的名！耶和華的僕人站在耶和華殿中；站在我們神殿院中的，你們要讚美他！

**讚美。**見詩113:1；見詩104:35註釋。
1.en: **Praise.** See Ps. 113:1; see on Ps. 104:35.

2.zh:
併於上節。

這是對祭司和工人的特別呼籲（見第19,20節註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋（2–5節）**。《給傳道人的證言》第15頁。
2.en: **Ye that stand.** A call especially to priests and ministers (see on vs. 19, 20).

3.zh:
你們要讚美耶和華！耶和華本為善；要歌頌他的名，因為這是美好的。

**美好的。**指歌頌上帝的名，或指上帝的名本身（見詩147:1）。
3.en: **Pleasant.** Referring either to the singing of praises to God’s name or to the name itself (see Ps. 147:1).

4.zh:
耶和華揀選雅各歸自己，揀選以色列特作自己的子民。

**特作自己的子民。**希伯來語是segullah（“個人財產”，見申7:6,7；14:2；參彼前2:9）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷一第282頁。
4.en: **Peculiar treasure.** Heb. segullah, “personal property” (see Deut. 7:6, 7; 14:2; cf. 1 Peter 2:9).

5.zh:
原來我知道耶和華為大，也知道我們的主超乎萬神之上。

其他的神根本不存在（見第15-18節）。
5.en: **Above all gods.** Other gods had no real existence (see vs. 15–18).

6.zh:
耶和華在天上，在地下，在海中，在一切的深處，都隨自己的意旨而行。

見詩115:3。上帝的旨意行使在祂廣袤的宇宙裡。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《服務真詮》第416頁。
6.en: **Whatsoever.** See Ps. 115:3. God’s pleasure is carried out in all the domains of His vast universe.

7.zh:
他使雲霧從地極上騰，造電隨雨而閃，從府庫中帶出風來。

**懷愛倫註釋**。見詩147:8、16-18懷愛倫註釋。

8.zh:
他將埃及頭生的，連人帶牲畜都擊殺了。

埃及的災難充分展示了上帝的權威。第十災特別厲害，影響也特別大（見出12:29註釋）。
8.en: **Smote the firstborn.** The plagues of Egypt were a mighty manifestation of God’s sovereignty. The tenth plague was especially severe and hence especially impressive (see on Ex. 12:29).

11.zh:
就是亞摩利王西宏和巴珊王噩，並迦南一切的國王，

西宏和噩試圖阻擾以色列人進軍巴勒斯坦（民21:21-35；申2:30-37；3:1-13）。
11.en: **Sihon.** Sihon and Og attempted to intercept the progress of the Israelites to the land of Palestine (Num. 21:21–35; Deut. 2:30–37; 3:1–13).

12.zh:
將他們的地賞賜他的百姓以色列為業。

西宏和噩的領土被流便，迦得，和半個瑪拿西支派所佔領（民32:33）。
12.en: **Heritage.** The territories of Sihon and Og were occupied by the Reubenites, the Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh (Num. 32:33).

13.zh:
耶和華啊，你的名存到永遠！耶和華啊，你可記唸的名存到萬代！

**可記念的（zeker）。**意為“提到”。對人的記憶可以忘卻，但上帝的名卻要“紀念”到永遠。
13.en: **Memorial.** Heb. zeker, “mention.” The memory of men is forgotten, but God’s name will be “mentioned” to all eternity.

14.zh:
耶和華要為他的百姓伸冤，為他的僕人後悔。

**為他的百姓伸冤。**見申32:36註釋。
**為他的僕人後悔（nacham）。**這裡指“難過”。
14.en:
**Judge his people.** See on Deut. 32:36.
**Will repent himself.** Heb. nacham. In the form here employed nacham means “to be sorry for.”

15.zh:
外邦的偶像是金的，銀的，是人手所造的；

關於15-18節，見詩115:4-8註釋。
15.en: **Silver.** For vs. 15–18, see on Ps. 115:4–8.

19.zh:
以色列家啊，你們要稱頌耶和華！亞倫家啊，你們要稱頌耶和華！

**要稱頌。**見詩63:4註釋。
**亞倫家啊。**指祭司（見出29:9）。擔任屬靈要職的人最應該稱頌上帝。
19.en:
**Bless.** See on Ps. 63:4.
**House of Aaron.** The priests (see Ex. 29:9). Those holding high spiritual office should be foremost in blessing the Lord.

20.zh:
利未家啊，你們要稱頌耶和華！你們敬畏耶和華的，要稱頌耶和華！

當以色列人陷入偶像崇拜，摩西召喚站在上帝一邊的人時，所有的利未人都響應了（見出32:26註釋）。他們被安排從事聖工（見民18:6註釋）。
20.en: **House of Levi.** When Israel fell into idolatry and Moses made a call for those who were on the Lord’s side, all the sons of Levi responded (see on Ex. 32:26), and they were set aside for holy service (see on Num. 18:6).

21.zh:
住在耶路撒冷的耶和華該從錫安受稱頌。你們要讚美耶和華！

見詩134:3註釋。
21.en: **Out of Zion.** See on Ps. 134:3.

0.zh: 序言——本詩是猶太人的大哈列（頌讚詩）。一再重現的副歌“因他的慈愛永遠長存”，肯定是由崇拜者或聖殿詩班輪唱的。
0.en: INTRODUCTION.—Ps. 136 has been known among the Jews as the Great Hallel. The recurring refrain “for his mercy endureth for ever” was doubtless sung as a response, either by the worshipers or by a Temple choir.

1.zh:
你們要稱謝耶和華，因他本為善；他的慈愛永遠長存。

**你們要稱謝耶和華。**任何時候都可以感謝上帝對人的良善和慈愛。
**他的慈愛永遠長存。**“慈愛”的原文是chesed，意為“上帝的愛”（見詩36篇補充註釋）。本詩的每一節都重現這個副歌。
1.en:
**O give thanks.** There is no time when it is inappropriate to render thanks to God for His goodness and mercy to man.
**His mercy endureth for ever.** Literally, “for to eternity his love.” The word translated “mercy” is chesed, which means, “divine love” (see Additional Note on Ps. 36). The refrain is repeated in every verse of this song.

2.zh:
你們要稱謝萬神之神，因他的慈愛永遠長存。

參申10:17；林前8:5,6。
2.en: **The God of gods.** Compare Deut. 10:17; 1 Cor. 8:5, 6.

3.zh:
你們要稱謝萬主之主，因他的慈愛永遠長存。

**主（'Adon）。**見本冊註釋第171-173頁。
3.en: **Lord.** Heb. ’Adon (see Vol. pp. 171–173).

4.zh:
稱謝那獨行大奇事的，因他的慈愛永遠長存。

上帝施行奇蹟是沒有對手的。只有無限的智慧才能設計出宇宙中莫可言喻的種種奇蹟。
4.en: **Great wonders.** God is the unrivaled miracle worker. Only a Being of infinite intelligence could have designed the universe with its indescribable wonders.

5.zh:
稱謝那用智慧造天的，因他的慈愛永遠長存。

在上帝所造宇宙的奧秘裡，隱藏著無限的智慧。科學的發現，越來越證明上帝創造的奇妙。大自然的每一個部分都是精心設計的。
5.en: **By wisdom.** What wisdom lies hidden in the secrets of the universe God has made! Scientific discoveries continually reveal more and more of the marvels of His creation. Design is seen in every department of nature.

6.zh:
稱謝那鋪地在水以上的，因他的慈愛永遠長存。

見創1:9,10。
6.en: **Above the waters.** See Gen. 1:9, 10.

7.zh:
稱謝那造成大光的，因他的慈愛永遠長存。

指創造周第四日的奇蹟，見創1:14-19的記載。
7.en: **Great lights.** A reference to the wonders of the fourth day of creation week, as recorded in Gen. 1:14–19.

9.zh:
他造月亮星宿管黑夜，因他的慈愛永遠長存。

一天中任何時候都是有規則的。當我們仰望夜空，觀看天上的“明燈”時，就會想到上帝對我們的大愛。月亮使我們高興，閃爍的星光似乎對人講述安慰的消息。
9.en: **Moon and stars.** No hour of the day is left without rule. When we look up to the sky at night and see the lamps of heaven, we are reminded of God’s great love to us. The moon gladdens the heart, and the twinkling stars seem to speak messages of comfort.

11.zh:
他領以色列人從他們中間出來，因他的慈愛永遠長存。

法老和奴隸主們決心不讓以色列人擺脫在埃及的奴役。但上帝既已計劃和應許解救祂的子民，又有祂的子民的配合，任何地上和陰間的權勢都無法抵擋。驕傲的君主如果藐視上帝，拒絕配合，就是自取滅亡。
11.en: **Brought out Israel.** Pharaoh and his slave masters were determined not to let the children of Israel go from their servitude in Egypt. However, when the Lord plans and promises to release His people and His people cooperate, there is no power in earth or hell that can withstand Him. When the proud monarch defies Him and refuses to cooperate he does so to his own destruction.

13.zh:
稱謝那分裂紅海的，因他的慈愛永遠長存。

見出14章。上帝在紅海中開出一條路，讓以色列人走在乾地上。照樣，祂也必在洶湧的波濤中，在我們缺乏信心的眼裡似乎無路可走的地方，為我們開出一條路來。
13.en: **Divided the Red sea.** See Ex. 14. As the Lord made a road through the Red Sea so that the Israelites walked on dry ground, so will He open up before us a way through the waters of adversity that are surging before us, and which seem impassable to our faithless eye.

16.zh:
稱謝那引導自己的民行走曠野的，因他的慈愛永遠長存。

在曠野的長途跋涉中，上帝始終是祂子民的供應者和領導者。祂夜間用火柱，日間用雲柱引導以色列人（出13:21）。祂供給他們水，並從天上賜下食物（見出16,17）。
16.en: **Led his people.** Throughout the wilderness journeyings the Lord was the Provider and Leader of His people. He guided Israel by the pillar of fire by night and the cloud by day (Ex. 13:21). He provided them with water and sent them food from heaven to them (see Ex. 16, 17).

19.zh:
就是殺戮亞摩利王西宏，因他的慈愛永遠長存；

**西宏。**見詩135:11註釋。
19.en: **Sihon.** See on Ps. 135:11.

21.zh:
他將他們的地賜他的百姓為業，因他的慈愛永遠長存；

迦南地是上帝賜給以色列人的。祂曾應許亞伯拉罕，他的後裔將承受這塊土地（創15:18）。
21.en: **Heritage.** The land of Canaan was given to Israel by a grant from God. He had promised to Abraham that his seed would inherit this country (Gen. 15:18).

23.zh:
他顧念我們在卑微的地步，因他的慈愛永遠長存。

以色列人曾在埃及為奴，落到了十分卑微的地步，但上帝並沒有忘記他們的困境。上帝不但沒有忘記，而且施行援助和拯救，這對於陷入悲傷，疾病和罪孽之中的人是多大的安慰啊。
23.en: **Low estate.** Israel was brought unto a low estate of bondage and slavery in Egypt, but the Lord did not forget them in their distress. To all who have fallen low in sorrow, in sickness, or in sin, how comforting it is to know that the Lord does not forget, but sends help and deliverance.

25.zh:
他賜糧食給凡有血氣的，因他的慈愛永遠長存。

上帝供養祂所創造的一切生靈（見詩104:27）。
25.en: **Giveth food.** God sustains all His living creatures (see Ps. 104:27).

0.zh: 序言——本詩被稱為“囚虜之歌”是很合適的。她描寫在被擄之地的以色列人。他們的詩人沉默了，而囚擄他們的人則嘲弄他們，要他們彈琴唱錫安之歌。俘虜們的心情是沉重的。本詩哀婉的語調始終引起讀者對困苦灰心之人的同情。
0.en: INTRODUCTION.—Ps. 137 has been fittingly termed the Song of the Captive. It portrays the Israelites in the land of exile. Their minstrels are silent, while their captors taunt them, asking them to tune their harps and sing one of the songs of Zion. The captives’ hearts are heavy. The plaintive note in this psalm is one that never fails to draw out the sympathy of the reader for the distressed and disheartened captives.

1.zh:
我們曾在巴比倫的河邊坐下，一追想錫安就哭了。

**巴比倫的河。**巴比倫被稱為“眾水”之地（耶51:13）。幼發拉底河是主流。它有許多支流。囚虜們經常到這些河岸邊去。
**就哭了。**回想聖城，特別是現在已成廢墟的聖殿，他們傷心欲絕，忍不住自己的淚水。在他們看來，沒有什麼地方比得上迦南。這是一塊美地（申8:7-9），在他們心中留下許多珍貴的記憶。
1.en:
**Rivers of Babylon.** Babylon was known as the land of “many waters” (Jer. 51:13). The most important watercourse was the Euphrates, which has many tributaries. The captives had resorted to the banks of these streams.
**We wept.** The remembrance of the Holy City and especially of their Temple now in ruins made their hearts so sorrowful that they found it impossible to restrain their tears. To them there was no land like Canaan. It was a goodly land (Deut. 8:7–9). It held many precious memories for them.

2.zh:
我們把琴掛在那裡的柳樹上；

琴聲（見本冊註釋第34頁）曾給他們帶來快樂和享受。但現在他們遭遇患難，琴聲也沉默了。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第28頁。
2.en: **Hanged our harps.** The music of the lyre (see p. 34) had been sweet and delightful to them, but now that calamity had overtaken them, their harps were silent.

3.zh:
因為在那裡，擄掠我們的要我們唱歌，搶奪我們的要我們作樂，說：給我們唱一首錫安歌吧！

**要我們唱歌。**關於亞述人對本節情形的描繪，見本冊35頁圖九，及該處註釋。
**錫安歌。**他們的主人嘲笑他們，要他們唱一首聖歌。
3.en:
**Required of us a song.** For an Assyrian pictorial representation of this verse see Fig. 9, p. 35, together with comments made there.
**Songs of Zion.** Their masters were deriding them and asking them to sing one of their sacred melodies.

5.zh:
耶路撒冷啊，我若忘記你，情願我的右手忘記技巧！

在這種情形同意唱聖殿之歌，在以色列人看來，似乎是對自己所愛之城的褻瀆。他即使忘記自己最寶貴的財產，也不會忘記以色列的驕傲和榮耀——錫安。
5.en: **If I forget.** To have consented to sing a song of the Temple under these conditions would have seemed to the Israelite like being unfaithful to his beloved city, which he adored with all his heart. Sooner would he forget his most treasured possession than forget Zion, the pride and glory of Israel.

6.zh:
我若不記念你，若不看耶路撒冷過於我所最喜樂的，情願我的舌頭貼於上膛！

**舌頭貼。**指不會說話。
6.en: **Tongue cleave.** That is, lose the ability to speak.

7.zh:
耶路撒冷遭難的日子，以東人說：拆毀！拆毀！直拆到根基！耶和華啊，求你記念這仇！

以東人對以色列人多次不顧手足之情。他們儘管與雅各的後裔有親屬關係，卻幫助巴比倫人攻擊以色列人（俄10-14章）。先知一再譴責以東人虧待自己的兄弟民族（耶49:7；哀4:21；結25:12-14；珥3:19；摩1:11）。
7.en: **The children of Edom.** Edom manifested an unbrotherly spirit toward Israel on several occasions. Despite their kinship with the descendants of Jacob, the Edomites helped the Babylonians against the Israelites (Obadiah 10–14. Edom is repeatedly denounced by the prophets for its heartless treatment of a brother nation (Jer. 49:7; Lam. 4:21; Eze. 25:12–14; Joel 3:19; Amos 1:11).

9.zh:
拿你的嬰孩摔在磐石上的，那人便為有福！

在古代的戰爭中，經常發生殺害無辜兒童的事。這是最殘暴最可惡的行為（王下8:12；賽13:16；何10:14）。鑑於巴比倫人的這種暴行（見耶51:24），詩人只是指出了生命的定律：“你怎樣行，祂也必照樣向你行”（俄15節；比較太7:2）。
9.en: **Against the stones.** The murder of innocent children, though customary in ancient warfare, was one of the cruelest and most abhorrent of all practices (2 Kings 8:12; Isa. 13:16; Hosea 10:14). In view of the fact that such stern treatment had been meted out by the Babylonians (see Jer. 51:24), the psalmist is simply enunciating a law of life—“as thou hast done, it shall be done unto thee” (Obadiah 15; cf. Matt. 7:2).

0.zh:
序言——本詩是在大難中向上帝懇求幫助。
根據題記，本詩是大衛在山洞裡藏身時創作的，但不知道是哪一個山洞。也許是亞杜蘭洞（撒上22章），隱基底（撒上24章），或歷史記錄中沒有提到的一個山洞。有人據詩142:6認為，在上述兩個地點中，隱基底的可能性較大。
關於本詩的題記，見本冊註釋第616,628頁（《詩篇》序言）。
大衛在洞裡作的訓誨詩，乃是祈禱。
0.en:
INTRODUCTION.—Ps. 142 is an earnest appeal to God for help in a time of overwhelming trouble.
According to the superscription this psalm was composed while David was hiding in a cave, but the cave is not identified. It may have been Adullam (1 Sam. 22) or En-gedi (1 Sam. 24), or even a cave not mentioned in the historical narrative. On the basis of Ps. 142:6 some think that of the two mentioned, En-gedi is the more likely.
On the superscription see pp. 616, 628.

1.zh:
（大衛在洞裡作的訓誨詩，乃是祈禱。）我發聲哀告耶和華，發聲懇求耶和華。

見詩107:13註釋。
1.en: **I cried.** See on Ps. 107:13.

2.zh:
我在他面前吐露我的苦情，陳說我的患難。

**苦情（síach）。**或“憂慮”。詩人沒有埋怨上帝如何對待自己。他是向上帝傾訴，而不是抱怨。
2.en: **Complaint.** Heb. síach, meaning also “concern.” The psalmist had no complaint against God’s dealings with him. He was complaining to God, not of God.

3.zh:
我的靈在我裡面發昏的時候，你知道我的道路。在我行的路上，敵人為我暗設網羅。

詩人的傾訴不為了告訴上帝什麼事，而是向天上的朋友訴說自己的苦衷。
3.en: **Thou knewest.** When the psalmist poured out his complaint, it was not with the idea of informing God, but rather with the idea of sharing his troubles with his heavenly Friend.

4.zh:
求你向我右邊觀看，因為沒有人認識我；我無處避難，也沒有人眷顧我。

**右邊。**見詩121:5註釋。
**認識我。**在危急關頭，似乎沒有一個人願意承認與他的友誼。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《服務真詮》第172頁。
4.en:
**Right hand.** See on Ps. 121:5.
**Would know me.** It seemed that no one was willing to acknowledge his friendship for the psalmist because of the danger involved.

5.zh:
耶和華啊，我曾向你哀求。我說：你是我的避難所；在活人之地，你是我的福分。

見詩119:57註釋。
5.en:
**Portion.** See on Ps. 119:57. Our Refuge in Extremity There are times when the spirit is wrapped in perplexity and distraught by false accusations. Under the stress of emotion the intellectual powers of good judgement are often confused, and the soul knows not which way to turn. At such a time one can open the heart to God and place full confidence in His overruling providence. Then the life will be filled with the bounties of the Lord, and the depression and consternation that formerly harassed the soul depart. Psalm 142:3
Historical background to 1 Samuel 24 if "the cave" of this Psalm is at En-gedi.

7.zh:
求你領我出離被囚之地，我好稱讚你的名。義人必環繞我，因為你是用厚恩待我。

**環繞（kathar）。**真正跟從上帝的人，顯然很高興詩人的得救，並與他一起感恩。
**用厚恩待我。**儘管眼下困難重重，前途險惡，詩人仍憑著信心展望得救的日子。
7.en:
**Compass.** Heb. kathar. The form here found means “to congregate around a person.” Evidently those who were true followers of God were glad when the psalmist was delivered, and shared with him in thanksgiving.
**Deal bountifully.** Though the present may be difficult and the future foreboding, the psalmist looks forward with confidence to the time of his deliverance.

0.zh:
序言——本詩祈求拯救，表達對上帝慈愛和憐憫的信心。其語氣和背景與詩142篇相似。
本詩分為兩個相等的段落，用“細拉”隔開。每段的詩節都是成對排列的。
關於本詩的題記，見本冊註釋第616,627頁（《詩篇》序言）。
大衛的詩。
0.en:
INTRODUCTION.—Ps. 143 is an appeal for deliverance and an expression of confidence in God’s love and mercy. In tone and background Ps. 143 closely resembles Ps. 142.
The psalm consists of two equal divisions, separated by Selah. In each division the verses are arranged in pairs.
On the superscription see pp. 616, 627.

1.zh:
（大衛的詩。）耶和華啊，求你聽我的禱告，留心聽我的懇求，憑你的信實和公義應允我。

詩人求告他所絕對信任的上帝慈愛和公義。
1.en: **In thy righteousness.** The psalmist appeals to God’s essential goodness and justice, in which he has unquestioning confidence.

2.zh:
求你不要審問僕人；因為在你面前，凡活著的人沒有一個是義的。

雖然聖經多次提到“義人”（見創18:23,24等）， 但詩人認識到，嚴格地說來，與上帝相比，是沒有一個義人的（見伯9:2）。人只有憑著信才能得到基督的義。但人的努力決不能使人成義（弗2:8,9）。行為是信心的結果，而不是信心的基礎。先要有信心。真正的信心一定會有行為。
2.en: **In thy sight.** Although the Scriptures frequently call men “righteous” (see Gen. 18:23, 24; etc.), the psalmist recognizes that in the absolute sense, when compared with God, no man is righteous (see Job 9:2). Man can obtain the righteousness of Christ only through faith. Human effort can never make a man righteous (Eph. 2:8, 9). Works are the fruit of faith; they are not the root of faith. Faith comes first, and where there is true faith works are sure to follow.

4.zh:
所以，我的靈在我裡面發昏；我的心在我裡面悽慘。

詩人在表面上絕望的狀況中心靈麻木了，產生了一種可怕的孤獨感。
4.en: **My heart.** The apparently hopeless situation in which the psalmist found himself numbed his heart. A feeling of terrible loneliness took possession of his soul.

5.zh:
我追想古時之日，思想你的一切作為，默唸你手的工作。

這樣的回顧既帶來憂傷，也帶來盼望。詩人傷心是因為今不如昔。但當他想到上帝過去所顯示的大能時，心中就得到了鼓舞，希望上帝再次垂聽他的禱告。他鼓起勇氣繼續祈求。
5.en: **I remember.** Such remembrance can bring both sadness and hope. The psalmist was sad because the present was not like the past. As he remembered the former manifestations of God’s power, his heart was encouraged in the hope that the Lord would again answer his prayer. He made bold to continue his request.

6.zh:
我向你舉手；我的心渴想你，如乾旱之地盼雨一樣。（細拉）

**如干旱之地。**如同大地經過長期乾旱而開裂，似乎在默默地張嘴求水解渴，詩人也渴望天上的甘霖澆灌自己的心靈。
**細拉。**見本冊註釋第629頁（《詩篇》序言）。
6.en:
**As a thirsty land.** As the land during a long period of drought opens in yawning cracks, as if parting its lips in mute pleadings for water to quench its thirst, so the psalmist longed for the showers of heaven to water his soul.
**Selah.** See on p. 629.

7.zh:
耶和華啊，求你速速應允我！我心神耗盡！不要向我掩面，免得我像那些下坑的人一樣。

**求你速速應允我。**見詩69:17註釋。
**我心神耗盡。**見詩84:2註釋。
**不要向我掩面。**見詩4:6；13:1註釋。
**坑。**見詩28:1註釋。
7.en:
**Hear me speedily.** See on Ps. 69:17.
**My spirit faileth.** See Ps. 84:2.
**Hide not thy face.** See Ps. 4:6; 13:1.
**Pit.** See on Ps. 28:1.

8.zh:
求你使我清晨得聽你慈愛之言，因我倚靠你；求你使我知道當行的路，因我的心仰望你。

**清晨。**見詩90:14註釋。詩人希望自己的痛苦到清晨時結束。晨曦怎樣驅散黑暗，他懇求上帝的臨格也驅散他心靈中的黑暗。在清晨祈禱默想上帝的慈愛是非常合適的！
**求你使我知道。**見詩25:4註釋。
8.en:
**In the morning.** See on Ps. 90:14. The psalmist hoped that the morning would end his grief. As the light of dawn dispels the darkness, so he asks that the light of God’s presence shall banish the darkness from his soul. How fitting is the early morning for devotion, for meditation on the loving-kindness of the Lord!
**Cause me to know.** See on Ps. 25:4.

9.zh:
耶和華啊，求你救我脫離我的仇敵！我往你那裡藏身。

**求你救我。**見詩59:1註釋。
**我往你那裡藏身。**當生活中的風暴洶湧氾濫，將要把人吞滅時，上帝是藏身之處（見詩46:1）。
9.en:
**Deliver me.** See on Ps. 59:1.
**I flee unto thee to hide me.** Literally, “unto thee I have hidden.” God is a hiding place when the storms of life are raging and about to overwhelm (see Ps. 46:1).

11.zh:
耶和華啊，求你為你的名將我救活，憑你的公義，將我從患難中領出來，

見詩31:3註釋。詩人求告上帝的聖名，作為要上帝垂聽他祈禱的理由。
11.en: **For thy name’s sake.** See on Ps. 31:3. The psalmist falls back upon the holy name as a reason why the Lord should hear his request.

0.zh:
序言——本詩頌揚上帝在戰爭與平安時的力量中和幫助。最後宣揚以上帝為主之人的快樂和幸福。
關於本詩的作者，見《基督教育之研究》第496頁。關於題記，見本冊註釋第616頁（《詩篇》序言）。
大衛的詩。
0.en:
INTRODUCTION.—Ps. 144 is a song extolling God’s strength and help both in war and in peace. The psalm closes on a note proclaiming the joy and happiness that come to those who have God for their Lord.
On the authorship of the psalm see CT 496. On the superscription see p. 616.

1.zh:
（大衛的詩。）耶和華─我的磐石是應當稱頌的！他教導我的手爭戰，教導我的指頭打仗。

**磐石（sur）。**見詩18:2,31,46註釋。Sur比喻堅固，耐久和不變的東西。
**教導我的手爭戰。**見詩18:34註釋。詩人並沒有美化戰爭。他只是承認上帝賜給他本領，打敗驕傲強大的歌利亞。在打仗時大衛不穿人間的任何盔甲，而是披戴天國的軍裝。
1.en:
**Strength.** Heb. ṣur, “rock” (see on Ps. 18:2, 31, 46). Ṣur is used figuratively to denote something solid, enduring, and immovable.
**My hands to war.** See on Ps. 18:34. The psalmist is not glorifying war itself. David recognized that God gave him the skill to defeat the arrogant and mighty Goliath. In the conflict David did not trust to any human armor, but he went clothed in the panoply of heaven.

2.zh:
他是我慈愛的主，我的山寨，我的高臺，我的救主，我的盾牌，是我所投靠的；他使我的百姓服在我以下。

我慈愛的主（chesed0）見詩36篇補充註釋。
**我的山寨。**見詩18:2註釋。
**高臺。**見撒下22:3註釋。
**盾牌（magen）。**參撒下22:3及該節註釋。
2.en:
**Goodness.** Heb. chesed (see Additional Note on Ps. 36).
**My fortress.** See on Ps. 18:2.
**High tower.** See on 2 Sam. 22:3.
**Shield.** Heb. magen, translated “shield” in 2 Sam. 22:3 (see comments there).

3.zh:
耶和華啊，人算什麼，你竟認識他！世人算什麼，你竟顧念他！

見詩8:4註釋。
3.en: **What is man!** See on Ps. 8:4.

4.zh:
人好像一口氣；他的年日如同影兒快快過去。

**一口氣（hebel）。**今生何等短暫！我們的智力和體力還沒有得到發展，就要結束生命。
4.en: **Vanity.** Heb. hebel, here probably meaning “a breath.” How transitory is this life of ours! We scarcely have developed our physical and mental powers when we are taken by death.

5.zh:
耶和華啊，求你使天下垂，親自降臨，摸山，山就冒煙。

**懷愛倫註釋（5–6節）**。《先祖與先知》第109頁。

6.zh:
求你發出閃電，使他們四散，射出你的箭，使他們擾亂。

當天國的炮火開始發射的時候，人的抵抗力顯得多麼微弱！基督復臨時，上帝能力的可怕顯示將是人類所從來沒有見過的（見《先祖與先知》第109頁）。
6.en: **Cast forth lightning.** When heaven’s artillery is set in motion how puny is the strength of man to resist it. At the second coming of Christ there will be more terrible manifestations of God’s power than have yet been witnessed (see PP 109).

7.zh:
求你從上伸手救拔我，救我出離大水，救我脫離外邦人的手。

詩人在這裡改變了比喻。大水意味著的極大的危險，這裡無疑指包圍著大衛的仇敵。
7.en: **Great waters.** The psalmist changes the figure. Great waters mean overwhelming dangers, and here no doubt refer to David’s enemies, who were on every side.

8.zh:
他們的口說謊話；他們的右手起假誓。

可能指他們舉右手說假話。即用詭計撒謊。
8.en: **Right hand.** Perhaps meaning that their falsehood was right-handed, that is, they told lies with dexterity.

9.zh:
神啊，我要向你唱新歌，用十弦瑟向你歌頌。

**新歌。**詩人從虛謊轉向崇尚真實的東西。他厭於地上的謊言和欺騙，轉而向上帝唱讚美的新歌。他的手與口相配合，因為他用十絃琴伴奏。
**十弦瑟。**見本冊註釋第36頁。
9.en:
**New song.** The psalmist turns from the false to adore that which is true. Weary of earthly liars and deceivers, he turns to God with a new song—a fresh song of praise. His hand also would assist his tongue, for he would employ an instrument of ten strings as his accompaniment.
**Psaltery.** See p. 33.
**Instrument of ten strings.** See p. 36.

10.zh:
你是那拯救君王的；你是那救僕人大衛脫離害命之刀的。

君王們處在特殊的危險之中，大衛也不例外。上帝在許多戰爭中保護了他。但更重要的是，上帝拯救了他這個罪人。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《今日的生活》第291頁。
